parties:
Abdus Sabur Mollah (Md) ------- Defendant No. 1-Petitioner
Vs
Md Ahad Mollah and others ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
2. This Rule was issued calling upon the defendant-opposite party No. 1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 21-11-2007 (decree signed on 27-11-2007) passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Faridpur in Title Appeal No. 96 of 2002 affirming the judgment and decree dated 16-4-2002 (decree signed on 22-4-2002) passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Boalmari , Faridpur in Title Suit No. 44 of 2000 decreeing the suit in preliminary form allotting 50 decimals of land in favour of the plaintiff and 18 decimals of land in favour of the defendant No. 1 should not be set-aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 3. Facts of the case, briefly, are that the opposite party No. 1, as plaintiff instituted a suit being Title Suit No. 44 of 2000 before the learned Assistant Judge, Boalmari, Faridpur imploding the defendants for partition of the suit land as descried in the schedule of the plaint. The case of the plaintiff in short is that the suit jama was originally belonged to Jaliluddin Mollah, who transferred 1.76 acres of land including 68 decimals of land of the suit plot to his son, Abdus Samad Mollah (defendant No. 3) by a registered deed of gift dated 5-2-1974 and thereafter, the defendant No. 3 sold out 1.05 acres of land including 50 decimals of land of suit plot No. 1157 to the plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 by the registered Kabala dated 22-8-1991. The suit land was never partitioned by metes and bounds. The plaintiff mutated his name and paid rent to the Government, the plaintiff possessed 50 decimals of land of the suit plot No. 1157 at its western side. The defendant No. 1 purchased some land from the defendant No. 3 and there was dispute in respect possession in the suit land and therefore, on 15-5-2000 the plaintiff requested for amicable partition but the defendant No. 1 refused to do so and hence, the suit. 

 4. The petitioner as defendant No. 1 entered appearance in the suit and filed a written statement denying all the material averments of the plaint stating, inter-alia, that the defendant Nos. 2, 3 are full brother of the plaintiff, the suit jama was originally belonged to Jaliluddin, who transferred 1.76 acres of land including 68 decimals of land of the suit plot in favour of his son (defendant No. 3) by way of a registered deed of gift dated 5-3-74 and thereafter, the defendant No 3 sold out 60 decimals of land of the suit plot and 05 decimals of land of non suit plot No. 1161 to the defendant No. 1 (petitioner) and handed over possession to him. The defendant-petitioner has possessed the suit land by bargadars and the current record of right prepared in his name, the plaintiff has no right, title and possession over the suit land, the plaintiff filed the instance suit for depriving the defendant No. 1 after creating a benami sale deed and, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 4. Where the plaintiff has right, title and possession over the suit land? 

 5. Whether the plaintiff is entitled to get the reliefs as prayed for or any other reliefs. 

 8. on appeal, the learned. Additional District Judge, Faridpur by his judgment and decree dated 21-11-2007 passed in Title Appeal No. 96 of 2002, concurred with findings with learned trial Judge and dismissed the appeal holding that the trial Court has rightly decreed the suit in preliminary form allotting 50 decimals of the suit plot in favour of the plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 and 18 decimals of land in favour of the defendant No. 1 and the instant Revision application is directed against that judgment and decree. 

 10. Mr Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 submits it is on record that kabala dated 22-8-1991 in favour of plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 is an admitted kabala and it has not been set-aside by any competent Court, the plaintiff proved his possession by adducing sufficient corroborative evidence over 50 decimals of the suit land and both the Courts below taking into consideration of the evidence and materials on record found that the defendant No. 3 sold out 1.05 acres of land including 50 decimals of land of suit plot No. 1157 to the plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 by the registered Kabala dated 22-8-1991, the suit land was never partitioned by metes and bounds, the defendant No. 1 purchased some land from the defendant No. 3, the plaintiff-petitioner mutated his name and paid rent to the Government, the plaintiff possessed 50 decimals of land of the suit plot No. 1157 at its western side and such concurrent findings of fact on possession and title are based on proper appreciation of the evidence and materials on record and, as such, the question of interference does not arise at all. 

 11. Finally, Mr Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan submits that according to the admitted facts of the case it is crystal clear that the record of right was wrongly prepared in the name of the defendants and the same was brought to the notice of the plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 after filing the suit. He adds that the proposition of law is by now well settled that record of right is not a document of title it does not create or extinguish title to land. At best, along with other evidence, it may support an evidence of title and in this case both the Courts below on the facts of the case and on consideration of the legal position rightly decided this point in favour of the plaintiff. Mr Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan to fortify his argument has relied on the decisions reported in 28 DLR (AD) 61, 13 MLR (AD) 6. 

 16. In the instant case the opposite party No. 1, as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 44 of 2000 in the Court of the learned Assistant Judge, Boalmari, Faridpur on the averments that the suit jama was originally belonged to Jaliluddin Mollah, who transferred 1.76 acres of land including 68 decimals of land of the suit plot to his son, Abdus Samad Mollah (defendant No. 3) by a registered deed of gift dated 5-2-1974 and thereafter, the defendant No. 3 sold out 1.05 acres of land including 50 decimals of land of suit plot No. 1157 to the plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 by registered Kabala dated 22-8-1991, the plaintiff mutated his name and paid rent to the Government, the plaintiff possessed 50 decimals of land of the suit plot No. 1157 at its western side. The defendant No. 1 purchased some land from the defendant No.3 and there was dispute in respect of possession in the suit land, the suit land was never partitioned by metes and bounds and thus, on 15-5-2000 the plaintiff requested the defendant No. 1 for amicable partition but in vain. 

 18. The plaintiff-opposite party No. 1 to prove his case examined 5 witnesses including himself as PW 2 and exhibited some documents. PW 1, Ayub Ali, as inspector of Boalmari Krishi Bank exhibited the original kabala No. 2685 dated 22-8-91 as exhibit No. 1. PW 2, plaintiff, Md Ahad Molla stated in his deposition that: এই জমি দলিল উদ্দিন ৩নং বিবাদী ছামাদ মোল্যাকে দান করে দখল বুঝায়ে দেই ইং ৫-২-৭৮ তারিখে। উক্ত দলিলের সহিমোহর নকল দলিল দিয়েছি। প্রদর্শনী-১(ক)। সামাদ মোল্যা (৩নং বিবাদী) স্বত্ববান দখলীকার থাকাকালে ইং ২২-৮-৯১ তারিখের দলিল মূলে আমার নিকট ৫০ শতক জমি বিক্রয় করে দখল দেয়। উক্ত দলিলের সহিমোহর নকল জমা দিয়ে উহা প্রদর্শনী-১ চিহ্নিত হয়। This witness in his deposition also stated that a shalo machin and water house stood in his 50 decimals of suit land, he mutated his name and paid rent to the Government. PW 3 stated in his deposition that he is a deed writer of Boalmari sub-registry office, on 22-8-1991 the parties of the deed went to him and he written the deed in question and on that date the sub-registrar registered the same. PW 4, Md Fazlul Haque Mollah, stated in his deposition that: আমি মোকদ্দমার পক্ষদের ও নালিশী জমি চিনি। নালিশী দাগের উত্তর পাশে জমি আছে। নালিশী জমির মধ্যে পশ্চিমাংশে ৫০ শতক জমি আহাদ মোল্যা ১০/১১ বৎসর দখল করে।বাকী জমি সামাদ মোল্যা খাইত। এই জমিতে আহাদ মোল্যার শ্যালো ম্যাশিন ও হাউজ আছে ৭/৮ বৎসর ধরে। নালিশী দাগের পূর্বাংশে সবুর মোল্যা ৩ বৎসর যাবৎ সামাদের দখলকারী অংশ দখল করে।PW 5, Md Ali Afzal stated in his deposition that: আমি মোকদ্দমার পক্ষদের চিনি ও নালিশী জমি চিনি। নালিশী জমির নাল পশ্চিমে আমার জমি তবে ঐ ভিন্ন মৌজা মুরাইল পশ্চিম খন্ডের মধ্যে। নালিশী জমির মধ্যে আহাদ মোল্যা ১১/২ পাখির একটু বেশী পশ্চিম নাল দিয়ে দখল করে ৩০ শতক পাখি। সবুর ঐ দাগের পূর্বাংশে সামাদের দখলীয় জমি ৩/৪ বৎসর খায়। এর আগে সবুর কোন জমি খাইত না। 

 21. As regards the plaintiff's case of title to the suit land it is based on the kabala (Ext. 1) dated 22-8-1991. 

 22. The trial Court on consideration of the evidence on record found the claim of the plaintiff is true and decreed the suit and the appellate Court below as last Court of fact on consideration of the evidence on record, facts and circumstances, held that "trial court has rightly decreed the suit in preliminary form allotting 50 and 18 decimals of land of the suit plot in favour of the plaintiff-respondent and defendant-appellant respectively and I find nothing to interfere with judgment passed by the learned trial Court." Both the trial Court and lower appellant Court came to a common finding that the plaintiff has been succeeded to prove his right, title, possession as well as share of 50 decimals of land of the suit plot No. 1157 at its western side. 

 25. From the facts as disclosed in the paint, written statement, deposition of witnesses, it becomes clear that the record of right was wrongly prepared in the name of the defendants. The court of appeal below after a detailed discussion of the attending circumstances borne out by records held "mere preparation of record of right as contended by the appellant does not create any right and title on the suit land". Furthermore, it appears from the record that the original kabala dated.22-8- 1991 was mortgaged to Krishi Bank, Boalmari Branch and it was called for comparison, the trial Court has decided that the kabala of the plaintiff is earlier to the kabala of the defendant No. 1 and the plaintiff's kabala has been duly acted upon. 

 26. The proposition of law is well settled that a registered kabala is an evidence of title which will prevail over other records of rights, until and unless such kabala is cancelled on specific allegation of fraud by any civil Court in an appropriate civil suit and in this case the defendant petitioner admitted in his evidence that he did not file any such suit for declaration of title and cancellation of registered kabala dated 22-8-1991 (Ext. 1). 

 "The records of rights of the Government which at best are evidence of possession at the time when such records are prepared and not an evidence of title. This is a well established principle of law. A registered kabala is an evidence of title which will prevail over the other records of rights as such until and unless such kabala is cancelled on a specific allegation of fraud by any civil Court in an appropriate civil suit." 

 28. In this case it is also found that (Ext.1) was the original kabala dated 22-8-1991, which mortgaged to Krishi Bank, Boalmari Branch by the plaintiff and it was called for comparison at the trial and that registered document is more than 20 years old document. No dispute was raised in the trial Court as to its registration (kabala dated 22-8-1991). Therefore, sitting under revisional jurisdiction, I am unable to accept the contention of Mr AKM Shamsul Haque, the learned Advocate for the petitioner that the defendant No. 3 in collusion with the plaintiff-opposite party created the fraudulent kabala dated 22-8-1991 (Ext.1) in order to defraud the defendant-petitioner or the kabala dated 22-8-1991 (Ext. 1) was not acted upon. 

 39. In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs. The judgment and decree of affirmance dated 21-11-2007 (decree signed on 27-11-2007) passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Faridpur in Title Appeal No. 96 of 2002 is hereby maintained.

parties:
Bangladesh Railway Dhaka and others-----------Appellant (In CA No. 187/08)
VS
Monowara Begum and others ---------- Respondents (In all the cases)
full_judgment:
2. The relevant facts, for the disposal of the appeals, are that the respondent No.1 Monwara Begum filed aforesaid writ petition stating that the land measuring an area of 2.8172 acres appertaining to CS plot No. 186, CS khatian No. 6615 and CS Sheet No.22 and Tawzi No.13448 of Mouza Shahar Dhaka, at present, Ramna District Dhaka, (hereinafter referred this case land) originally belonged to Nawab Khaja Yusuf Jan. CS khatian No. 6615 was correctly prepared in his name. Nawab Khaja Yusuf Jan transferred the said land along with his some other properties to his only daughter Mst. Nurunnessa Khanam alias Nurun Bibi and her husband Syed Mohammad Kashmiri on 25-9-1922 by a deed of gift and delivered possession to them who accepted the gift and took over possession of the said land. Thereafter, they died one after another leaving only son Syed Jamil Hasan. SA Khatian was prepared in his name. Jamil Hasan entered into an agreement for sale of the suit land with the writ petitioner on 11-4-1990 for a consideration of Taka 30,00,000 (taka thirty lac) and upon receiving Taka 29,50,000 he executed an agreement for sale. On 15-4-1991, Syed Jamil Hasan denied to execute and register the sale deed and, thus, the writ petitioner instituted Title Suit No. 161 of 1991 in the First Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for Specific Performance of Contract. Said suit was transferred in the Second Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka and renumbered as Title Suit No.139 of 1993 and was decreed on compromise by a judgment and decree dated 6-7-1993. Accordingly, sale deed was executed and registered through Court on 21-9-1994 executing the said decree. The petitioner got delivery of possession of the case land through Court on 27-1-1996. The Government, insptie of service of summons, did not contest the said suit. On query, Additional Deputy Commissioner (LA), Dhaka by his Memo No. 324/LA section General /95 dated 6-4-1995 informed that the case land was not acquired for Bangladesh Railway. The proclamation No. 342 dated 02.09.1882 published in the Calcutta Gazette on 6th September, 1882 shows that the villages/ areas were' acquired by the Government for the purpose of construction of Dhaka-Mymensingh State Railway. But the case land, situated within Mouza Dhaka Shahar, was not acquired. On the basis of the said proclamation, CS khatian No.16868 was published in the name of Eastern Bengal State Railway. Said CS khatian No. 16868 is covered by ward No. 3, sheet No. 4 while the petitioner's case land is covered by CS khatian No. 6615 of Ward No. 3, Sheet No. 22. Dhaka City Corporation, the writ respondent No. 3 appellant prepared a sketch map by its surveyor demarcating the case land of the petitioner. The case land of the writ petitioner is situated not within the area of Osmani Uddayan as evidenced by the said sketch map. The writ petitioner with a view to construct an international Standard Five Star Hotel and Shopping Centre in the case land in the name and style of M/s South East. Development Corporation (Pvt.) Ltd. applied to the Prime Minister and Chairman of Board of Investment for approval of the said project. After due investigation, the said project was approved in the 184th Board Meeting of the Board of Investment, Office of the Prime Minister on 21-1-2000 and the Board of Investment issued a certificate being Registration No. 2000005122-H dated 30-5-2000 under section 11 of the Board of Investment Act, 1989. For implementation of the said project at a cost of Taka 564 crore, a foreign loan equivalent to 10 Million US dollar was sanctioned by International Investment World Inc. Company, U.S.A. by a letter dated 14-3-2000. Considering the importance of the use of said project for NAM conference, the respondent No.1, by a Memo No. Sha Pro-6/RAJ-68/98/256 dated 24-5-2001 addressed to RAJUK, asked to issue clearance certificate and to approve the plan for the said project in favour of the writ petitioner. On 27-6-2001, the petitioner came to know from news item published in the "Daily Star" that the approvals of the proposal for construction of five star hotel within Osmani Uddyan has been cancelled on 26-6-2001. Against which, the writ petitioner filed writ petition No, 2882 of 2001 and obtained Rule and got an order of status-quo. In connection with the said writ petition, contempt Rule was issued for violation of the order of status-quo against the petitioner and her husband Advocate MA Khaleque. In that case the High Court Division directed the police to take over possession of the disputed land and to protect the same. The contempt Rule was disposed of accepting the petitioner's unconditional apology. The Rule issued in writ petition was discharged. However, police took over possession of the disputed land. In view of aforesaid circumstances, the writ petitioner has filed this writ petition for a direction upon the writ respondents to hand over possession of the disputed land. 

 4. Mr Ivlahbubey Alam, learned Senior Advocate appearing with Mr KS Salauddin for the appellants in all the appeals, submits that it is apparent on the face of the record that the decree passed in the suit for specific performance of contract as obtained by the writ petitioner was fraudulent and collusive one. He submits that Syed Jamil Hasan, judgment debtor, himself filed Title Suit No.151 of 1980 in the third Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for declaration of his title and recovery of khas possession which established that the writ petitioner's alleged vendor, had no possession in the disputed land and his title in the case land, if any, is disputed so the writ petitioner is not entitled to get possession of the disputed land from this Court getting direction by way of mandamus. He submits that in the suit for specific performance of a contract, title of the disputed land had not been ascertained, the High Court Division erred in law in making the Rule absolute. He further submits that over the subject matter, several suits are pending for determination of its ownership, the High Court Division erred in law in giving direction to hand over possession of the same. He further submits that the land, in question, was acquired for Railway in 1882 and, accordingly, possession of the same was handed over to the Railway and, at present, same is under the management by the Dhaka City Corporation, the High Court Division erred in law in making the Rule absolute. He further submits that the writ petitioner managed a collusive and fraudulent decree in respect of most valuable land situated in the heart of City price of which is taka few hundred crores, the High Court Division erred in law in making the Rule absolute. 

 5. Mr AF Hassan Ariff and Mr Abdul Baset Mazumder, learned Senior Counsel appearing for the respondents, submit that the writ petitioner respondent came to an agreement with the original owner of the case land and by filing a suit' for specific performance of contract got decree and upon executing the said decree he obtained sale deed registered through Court, thereby, acquired valid title in the same, the High Court Division upon proper appreciation of materials on record, rightly observed that writ petitioner is entitled to get possession of the same. He further submits that in the instant writ petition, the writ petitioner respondent sought for direction to get possession of the case land wherefrom she was dispossessed forcibly, the High Court Division rightly directed the writ respondent appellants to hand over the possession of the case land to the writ petitioner respondent. 

 7. In this case, it appears that the writ petitioner claimed title in the case land by virtue of a decree which she obtained in a suit for specific performance of contract. It is the claim of the writ petitioner that she, upon executing the said decree, obtained sale deed registered and took delivery of possession through Court wherefrom she has been dispossessed subsequently. 

 9. Moreover, in a suit for specific to whether there is any controversy between the vendor and the vendee as to execution of the agreement for sale and whether earnest money has been paid etc. and the Court directs the vendor to execute the necessary document in favour of the vendee. A decree for specific performance of contract only declares the right of decree holder to have a deed of transfer of the property covered by the decree executed in his favour. The decree by itself does not transfer the title. It is the execution of the sale deed that transfers the property. Such transfer of title is taken place if the vendor himself has transferable perfect title in the land transferred. In that suit, neither the appellants of these appeals were impleaded nor title of the disputed land has been adjudicated and ascertained. It is to be mentioned here that meanwhile, Syed Jamil Hasan himself filed a suit for setting aside the aforesaid compromise decree on the ground of fraud and collusion. 

 "It is relevant to point out here that the vendor of the said land namely Syed Jamil Hasan, from whom the petitioner allegedly purchased the same and obtained possession, has himself filed Title Suit No. 151 of 1980 in the 3rd Court of the learned Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession. If the vendor of the case land has himself filed suit to obtain title and possession of the property from the Bangladesh Railway, then it cannot be believed that during the pendency of that suit the petitioner has got possession of the said land from the vendor. It has also been alleged by the petitioner that she has obtained title in the said land through a sole decree in a suit for specific performance of contract and thereafter obtained possession of the said land through the process of Court although in a suit for specific performance of contract delivery of possession is not intended by the process of Court." 

 13. Against the aforesaid observation, the writ petitioner Monwara Begom filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1472 of 2006 and this Division while disposing of the leave petition has observed, "It is relevant to point out here that vendor of the land, namely, Syed Jamil Hasan, from whom possession, has himself filed Title Suit No.151 of 1980 in the 3rd Court the learned Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession. If the vendor of the case land has himself filed suit to obtain title and possession of the property from the Bangladesh Railway, then it cannot be believed that during the pendency of that suit the petitioner has got possession of the said land from the vendor." 

 16. Several cases are pending for ascertaining the title of the case land in different Courts. Earlier Motwalli of Shahjadi Waqf Estate filed Title suit No. 363 of 1985 against Railway and others and in that suit Mdnsif, 4th Court Dhaka found the title and possession of the Railway. In Title Appeal No. 158 of 1987 and 159 of 1987, Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka observed that the disputed land is the acquired land of the Government and Railway has been possessing the same. The plaintiff of the said suit fought up to the Appellate Division and lost. Syed Jamil Hasan, the alleged vendor of the writ petitioner, himself filed Title Suit No.151 of 1980 for declaration of title and recovery of possession in the then 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge. Dhaka against Railway and others admitting the possession of the Railway. The said suit is still pending in the Second Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka where the same was renumbered as Title Suit No.837 of 2015. That is, at the time of alleged execution of "bainanama" Syed Jamil Hasan's title was doubtful and he had no possession of the case land. A title which has not been perfected and which cannot rationally be said to be free from doubt is no title at all. 

 17. Since the appellants, in possession, of the disputed lands, have raised a serious question as to the validity of the writ petitioner's title and her claimed possession and thereafter, dispossession and that there is no conclusive evidence of the writ petitioner's title in the same, the High Court Division in an application under Article 102 of the Constitution cannot put the writ petitioner in possession by dispossessing the appellants from the case land. In the case of Mohan Panday vs Usha Rani Rajaria reported in 1992 (IV) SCC 61 it has been laid down that no mandamus can be based on a Civil Court decree, which would be in the nature of executing or giving effect to a civil decree. This writ petition was full of disputed facts and the prayer made in it cannot be granted in a proceeding under Article 102 of the Constitution as factual disputes cannot be decided in this proceeding. The writ of mandamus cannot be demanded ex-debito justifiae but it issues only in the discretion of the court. It is a high prerogative writ and is to ampliate justice not to give effect of a decree which is apparently fraudulent and collusive in nature. It is a malafide attempt on behalf of writ petitioner Monowara Begum, wife of an Advocate to grab the property of the Republic. She came in this Court with unclean hands.

parties:
GENERAL MANAGER, BANGLADESH RAILWAY 
vs. 
BADRUDDIN MIMED BEING DEAD HIS HEIRS-MOST. SAJEDA BEGUM AND OTHERS
full_judgment:
Hasan Foez Siddique, J: This appeal is directed against the judgment and decree dated 20th November, 2007 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 86 of 1995 affirming those dated 30.11.1994 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Gazipur in Title Suit No. 136 of 1994 dismissing the suit. 

 2. The relevant facts, for the disposal of this appeal, are that the Railway filed the aforesaid suit for declaration of its title in respect of the land as described in the schedule to the plaint and for further declaration that the ex-parte decree dated 24.09.1984 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, First Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 279 of 1970 was collusive, fraudulent, inoperative and the same is not binding upon the plaintiff stating, inter alia, that the suit land, along with other lands, was acquired by the Government under the Land Acquisition Act, 1870 and possession of the same was delivered to the Railway, the requiring body. The Railway took over possession of the said land by a declaration dated 02.09.1882 and, thereafter, it constructed Dhaka-Joydebpur Rail line which crossed the suit land and other lands. For the purpose of construction of double track rail line, the Railway authority requested the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka to acquire more lands and, accordingly, L.A. Case Nos. 62 of 1964-65 was started for acquisition of more lands. Since the land of Plot No. 121 was acquired in 1882 and the Railway took over possession of the same and Rail line was constructed on the said land and other lands, it was not necessary to acquire the said land again. The defendant Nos. 1 to 3, getting fraudulent ex-parte decree in Title Suit No.279 of 1970, demanded compensation claiming that the Government has acquired the suit land in L.A. Case No.62 of 1964-65 so, according to them, they are entitled to get compensation due to such acquisition. Meanwhile, the Railway constructed double track rail line which crossed the suit land and other lands. In Title Suit No.279 of 1970, the defendant Nos. 1-3 claimed that they got settlement of the suit land from Bhawal Raj Estate. In C.S. operation, the land of Plot No.121 was duly recorded in the name of Railway. In S.A. operation, the same was again recorded in the name of Pakistan Railway. Neither the Railway nor the Government surrendered their right in the disputed property in favour of Bhawal Raj Estate. The story of settlement by Bhawal Raj Estate in favour of the defendant Nos. 1-3 is absolutely false and concocted. Hence, was the suit. 

 3. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 contested the suit contending, inter alia, that the suit was not maintainable and the same was barred by the provision of res-judicata and also barred by limitation. They further contended that the suit land originally belonged to Bhawal Raj Estate. It permitted the then East Bengal Railway Company to use the said land for alignment of Dhaka- Mymensingh Railway line. In S.A. operation, the same was recorded in the name of the Railway. Thereafter, the Railway surrendered 5.14 acres of land in favour of Raja Rajendra Narayan Roy Chowdhury in 1914. Thereafter, Bhawal Raj Estate settled 3.54 acres of land in favour of Feroja Begum, Anwar Hossain and Badruddin on 09.03.1938 receiving salami of Tk. 460/-. S.A. record of right was prepared in their names in S.A. khatian No.199. At the time of constructing Dhaka- Tongi one track Railway into two track, the Railway took over possession of 5.14 acres of land from Firoza Begum, Anowar Hossain and Badruddin in L.A. Cases No.62/64-65 and 14/65-66. The defendants were under impression that the said land of Plot No. 121 was duly acquired in L.A. Case No.62 of 1964-65 as such they were entitled to get compensation. These defendants and Firoja Khatun, claiming title in the suit land, filed Title Suit No. 279 of 1970 in the First Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for getting compensation. The defendant of that suit, that is, the plaintiff of this suit, appeared in the said suit and contested the same. In written statement of the said suit, they admitted that the Railway surrendered 5.14 acres of land and, thereafter, the Government acquired 4.94 acres of land for construction of double track rail line. The learned Subordinate Judge dismissed the suit. These defendants, who were the plaintiffs in that suit, preferred First Appeal No.68 of 1972 in the High Court Division which was remanded to the Subordinate Judge. In the said suit, the present plaintiff appeared but finally did not contest the same. Accordingly, the suit was decreed ex-parte on 24.09.1984. Since the present plaintiff in earlier Title Suit No.279 of 1970 admitted the story of surrender of the suit land in favour of Bhawal Raj and the defendants took settlement of the said land from Bhawal Raj and that the plaintiff of this suit, knowing fully well about the said Title Suit No. 279 of 1970, appeared in the same and finally did not contest when the same was taken up for hearing and consequently, the said suit was decreed ex-parte, this suit should be dismissed. 

 4. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, learned Senior Counsel appearing with Mr. Shahed Alam learned Counsel for the appellant, submits that the suit land along with other lands were acquired by the Government in 1882 and the Government handed over possession of the said land to the Railway and the Railway, taking over possession of the same, constructed Rail line which crossed the suit land. In C.S. operation, the suit land was recorded in the name of Railway Department. Neither the Government nor the Railway surrendered the suit land in favour of Bhawal Raj Estate. The claim of the defendants, so far the story of relinquishment of title and possession in favour of Bhawal Raj Estate, is absolutely false and that the defendants' claim of taking settlement of the suit land from Bhawal Raj Estate is also false and fabricated. He further submits that in Title Suit No.297 of 1970 the Railway appeared and filed written statement. Both the parties adduced evidence in support of their respective cases and the trial Court on consideration of the evidence on record, dismissed the suit. In the First Appeal, the present defendants, who were the plaintiff-appellants in the said appeal, filed application for admitting additional evidence and the High Court Division remanded the suit for consideration of the application for additional evidence. In view of such circumstances, the trial Court was not authorized to decree the suit ex-parte. Mr. Mahbubey Alam lastly submits that the defendants, in collusion with some officials of the Railway, made an attempt to grab the Railway property and created some papers inasmuch as there was no provision in law to surrender of the acquired property, the learned courts below committed error of law in not holding that suit land is the property of the Railway. 

 5. Mr. A.J. Mohammad Ali, learned Senior Counsel appearing for the respondents, submits that it is true that the Government acquired the suit land for Railway but the Railway did not use the said land and the same remained fallen. At one stage, the Railway surrendered the suit land in favour of Bhawal Raj Estate. 'Thereafter, in 1938 Bhawal Raj Estate settled the suit land to the defendants. The Government, admitting the story of surrender and subsequent settlement, prepared a proposal for acquiring the same for the purpose of construction of double track rail line in 1964-65 and accordingly, these defendants and Firoja Khatun, claiming title in the suit land, instituted Title Suit No.297 of 1970 for realization of compensation and got decree. Mr. A.J. Mohammad Ali submits that in view of the admission of the Railway in the written statement submitted in Title Suit No.297 of 1970 and in different documents, the Railway is not legally permitted to say that the Railway did not surrender the suit land in favour of Bhawal Raj Estate who settled the same to these defendants, the learned courts below rightly dismissed the suit. 

 6. Admittedly, the suit land along with other lands were acquired by the Government for the purpose construction of Rail line, that is, the same was acquired for public purpose and public interest. Exhibit-1 is attested photostate copy of Calcutta Gazette dated 06.09.1882 regarding acquisition of the suit land. P.W.1 proved the Ext. 1 and the defendants did not raise any question regarding genuineness of Ext. 1. It is also admitted that the Railway Department, taking over possession of the suit land, constructed rail line thereon which crossed the same and a portion of the disputed plot remained as unused. It is the case of the defendants that the Railway surrendered the suit land in favour of Raja Rajendra Narayan Roy Chowdhury in 1914. In support of the claim of surrender the defendants failed to produce any instrument of surrender or any other evidence. Mr. A.J. Mohammad Ali submits that the Railway admitted that it surrendered the title and possession of the suit land in favour of Bhawal Raj Estate. Mr. Mahbubey Alam submits that the defendants, in collusion with some dishonest officials of the Railway, created those papers admitting the story of surrender inasmuch as there was no law to effect such surrender. 

 7. We have gone through the related laws. Those are the Land Acquisition Act, 1870 and the Land Acquisition Act, 1894. Section 16 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1870 provides that when the Collector has made an award under section 14 or a reference to the Court under Section 15 of the said Act he may take possession of the land, which shall thereupon vest absolutely in the Government free from all encumbrances. It is the case of the defendants that the Railway surrendered the suit property and officials of the Railway admitted so in different letters. But we do not find, within four corners of the Land Acquisition Act, 1870, any such provision of relinquishment/surrender of title and possession of the acquired land rather it is provided that after completion of acquisition the right, title and possession of acquired land shall be vested in the Government free from all encumbrances. In such circumstances, the only way was to transfer the acquired land to the incumbent by the Government by executing an instrument of transfer. Similar provision was provided in Section 16 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 which stated that when the collector made an award under Section 11 of that Act he may take possession of the land, which shall thereupon vest absolutely in the Government free from all encumbrances. In the case of Fruit and Vegetable Merchants Union Vs. the Delhi Improvement Trust reported in AIR 1957 SC 344 it was observed that in the cases contemplated under sections 16 and 17 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 the property acquired becomes the property of the Government without any condition or limitations either as to title or possession. The legislature has made it clear that the vesting of the property is not for any limited purpose or limited duration. Section 16 clearly lays down that after making an award, the Collector may take possession of the land which shall thereupon vest absolutely in the Government free from all encumbrances. We do not find any such provision in those laws, exercising which, the Railway Authority or the Government was permitted to surrender the title and possession of the acquired land in favour of original owners or to any one. Where Government took over possession of the land soon after the award they are not at a liberty to withdraw from the acquisition of the land. There is no provision by which land statutorily vested in the Government reverts to the original owner. (ref: AIR 1970 SC 1576, Lt. Governor of Himachal Pradesh and another Vs. Sri Avinash Sharma). In absence of any such provision in the aforesaid laws, it is difficult to accept that the Railway Authority legally surrendered title and possession of the suit land in favour of the Bhawal Raj Estate. The only course open to the Government or Railway after possession has passed on to it is to retransfer it to the original owner or someone else, with his consent, in the regular mode in which transfers are effected. If any attempt was at all made to surrender the suit property, the same was a nullity. The land having once vested in the Government, the Government cannot divest itself of it withdrawing from the acquisition which is already complete. Once possession of the land is taken by the Government, the fact, that owner of the land entered upon land and resumed possession, does not have effect of obliterating consequences of vesting. 

 8. Thus, the position stands that the suit land was acquired by the Government and possession of the same was handed over to the Railway and, in such view of the matter the title and possession of the same was vested in the Government free from all encumbrances. There is no instrument in the record to prove that the Government/ Railway surrendered the suit land and even there was no such law of surrendering acquired land. Accordingly, C.S. khatian was rightly prepared. 

 10. These defendants earlier filed Title Suit No.297 of 1970 for getting compensation stating that the suit land was acquired in 1964-65 in the L.A. Case No.62 of 1964-65 and 14 of 1965-66. It appears from the materials on record that the said suit was dismissed and the trial Court specifically found that these defendants committed gigantic fraud for grabbing the suit land and that the suit land was acquired land for the Railway. These defendants preferred appeal which was remanded by the High Court Division for consideration of the prayer for admitting additional evidence filed by these defendants, that is, the plaintiffs of that suit. 

 73 24.9.84 plaintiff files hajira. The suit is taken up for ex-parte hearing. The plaintiffs have filed suit for declaration of their title to the suit property and for further declaration that they are entitled to receive proper compensation for acquisition of the suit property in L.A. Case No.62/64-65 and 14/65-66. Previously, the suit was dismissed on contest against the defendant No.1 and ex-parte against the rest vide judgment dated 24.08.1971, but on appeal the Hon'ble High Court in F.A. No. 62/72 was pleased to set aside the said judgment and decree and thereby remanded the suit to this court for fresh trial with a direction to accept some documents as additional evidence on behalf of the plaintiffs. But lastly the defendants did not come to contest the suit. 

 The plaintiffs claim title to the suit land by way of rayati settlement from the ex-land lord Bhawal C/W estate. Previously the plaintiff No.1 Badaruddin Ahmed was examined as P.W/ 1 and some documents were marked as exts.1, 1(a), 1(b),2-2(b),3,4,5,6-6(a) and for identification as X,X(1), Yand Y(1). Today, another P1W, i.e. P/W.2 Moslehuddin Ahmed is examined and some other documents marked as exts. 7, 8, 9-9(a) and 10-10(a). Now, from the evidences on record it appears that the plaintiffs have proved their alleged rayati settlement in the suit land. Thus they acquired title to the same by operation of law with the coming into force of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The case is, therefore proved. Court fee paid is correct. Hence, Ordered. 

 That the suit be decreed ex-parte without any cost. It is declared that the plaintiffs having sixteen annas right, title and interest in the suit property are legally entitled to receive proper compensation in L.A. Case No. 62/64-65 and 14/65-66 of the L.A. Collector, Dhaka." 

 14. Furthermore, the present defendants in that suit sought for declaration of their title and compensation for acquisition of suit land in L.A. Case No.62 of 1964-65 and 14/65-66 but actually the same was not acquired in those L.A. Cases so the question of entitlement of getting compensation does not arise. Thus the said suit itself was misconceived and the same was filed by misrepresentation of facts and by suppression of material facts. The defendant-respondents got decree for realization of compensation stating that the suit land was acquired by the Government in the aforesaid L.A. cases but they failed to produce any papers regarding acquisition of disputed plot in those L.A. cases. Moreso, we have already held that the Land Acquisition Acts do not authorize the Government to surrender the acquired land and that if any such event ever occurred, the same was inoperative and a nullity, we are of the view that the defendants have had no title in the suit land. 

 15. In the case of S.P. Chengalvalvaraya Naidu V. Jagannath (1994)1 SCC I it was observed that the principle of "finality of litigation' cannot he pressed to the extent of such absurdity that it becomes an engine of fraud in the hands of dishonest litigants. The Courts of law are meant for imparting justice between the parties.----we have no hesitation to say that a person, whose case is based on falsehood, has no right to approach the court. He can be summarily thrown out at any stage of litigation." The High Court Division, in our opinion, committed error of law in shutting the doors of justice in view of the discussions made above. 16. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, we are of the view that the title and possession of the Railway in the suit land remained intact in view of the acquisition of 1882, the courts below committed error of law in not decreeing suit holding that the Railway had has lawful title and possession in the suit land.

parties:
Government of Bangladesh others ------ Appellants
Vs
Musammat Amikun ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
3. Since the property was listed as abandoned building, the writ petitioner filed a case before the Court of Settlement seeking release of the building and the same was dismissed on the finding that the writ petitioner is not "aware to (sic) the relevant facts about the particulars of the original allottee and as such her statement to the effect that she is the daughter of Nazir cannot be reliable", that "it is evident from her own application that she was not in possession of the case house and as such applied for release of the property from the abandoned property list. Therefore, the claim of the petitioner about physical possession in the case property appears to be false", that "at present one Harunur Rashid is in possession of the house", that "neither the petitioner has been able to prove that she is the daughter and heir of the original owner Md. Nazir, nor she has possession in the case property. Rather, it appears from the Government files and records that the property of Md. Nazir was found abandoned after commencement of P.O.16/72 and the Government took control and management of the property from the very beginning. There is no evidence before us to show that Md. Nazir died in this country and that he was available after the war of liberation". Then the writ-petitioner filed the aforementioned writ petition upon which Rule Nisi was issued. 

 7. Mr. A.M. Aminuddin, learned Senior Advocate appearing for the respondent made submissions in support of the impugned judgement and order of the High Court Division. He submitted that at the time of hearing, the respondent was examined as P.W.1 on 27.2.1994, while she was very sick and extremely nervous on that date, she made some statements by way of her deposition which were apparently inconsistent with her stand in the case and that accordingly an application was made on her behalf soon thereafter on 3.5.1994 with a prayer for her re-examination in the case by cancelling her earlier deposition on 27.2.1994, and as such the Court of Settlement being satisfied vide order dated 3.5.1994 allowed the prayer for re-examination. Although a consider-able time had elapsed, her deposition was not taken on re-examination, rather the hearing of the case was concluded ultimately dismissing the case on the basis of her initial deposition, although the Government acting through the Ministry of Works failed to produce any material on the basis of which, the building in question could be regarded as an abandoned property. He submitted that the Court of Settlement dismissed the case of the respondent on the finding that she was not the rightful claimant of the building in question and she was not the legal heir of the original allottee, late Md. Nazir and also held that the respondent could not prove that she was in possession of the building in question, and relying on the Government assertion to the effect that one Harunur Rashid was in possession of the building for the Government, as such the Government treated the same as abandoned property since 1972, as a matter of course. These findings of the Court of Settlement were arrived at obviously on the strength of certain observations, annotation, addendum and commentary in the concerned files of the Government and not on the basis of any valid evidence, documentary or otherwise rather these findings are contrary to the available documentary evidence on record. He submitted that the respondent conversely has been able to prove her title to the building in question, on the strength of Lease Agreement dated 19.4.1962, letter of possession dated 20.6.1962 (Annexures-A and A-1) demonstrating grant of lease of the said building in favour of her father, Md. Nazir. The respondent in the memo of the instant writ petition has also annexed letter dated 4.3.1982 vide Annexure-C, issued by the Mohammadpur Housing Estate, which makes it obvious that all the Government dues up to 1982 so far as it relates to the building in question were already paid by said Md. Nazir. The respondent also annexed a Succession Certificate and a certificate from the Chairman of Ward No.12 concerned, in which the building is situated vide Annexure-E and E-1, which revealed that the respondent was the lone legal heir of said Md. Nazir as his only daughter. All these Annexures are in original and were very much available before the Court of Settlement. He submitted that Annexure-E and F are the Government letters in original addressed to the respondent showing the said building as her address and that possession of all these original papers/documents provided a valid rebuttable presumption that the respondent is the genuine claimant of the building in question as the heir of said Md. Nazir vis-a-vis the respondent's consistent claim to be in possession of the building, although the Government claims that the same was in possession initially through Chand Mia and presently through one Harunur Rashid, but the Government could not produce any of them before the Court of Settlement, in spite of Court's order passed on 31.12.1994 in this regard. He submitted that the Court of Settlement arrived at the aforesaid finding that the petitioner/respondent is not the heir of Md. Nazir, merely on suspicion, caused by some of her oral testimony which she made, because of her illness and fright, in utter disregard to the documentary evidence, viz. Annexure-B and D, i.e. Affidavit dated 09.04.1964 sworn before the Magistrate, First Class as well as Succession Certificate obtained from Third Court of the then Subordinate Judge, Dhaka. He submitted that the Court of Settlement having passed the order on 03.05.1995 to re-examine the respondent, deprived her of a hearing by the order dated 23.11.1995 and thus the same is violative of practice and is clearly violative of the law and the principles of natural justice as well. He submitted that the Court of Settlement was satisfied that the deposition of the petitioner/respondent was not correctly recorded and as such passed the order dated 03.05.1994 allowing re-examination of the petitioner, but ultimately passed the impugned decision on the basis of the said incorrect initial deposition. He submitted that the Court in order to ascertain the factum of possession passed an order on 03.12.1994 to issue notice upon the persons claimed by the Government to be in possession of the building in question and also passed an order for personal attendance of the respondent, but ultimately passed the impugned decision without recording any satisfaction in respect of service of notice upon them, or without hearing any of them, which is neither proper nor legal. He submitted that the Court of Settlement arrived at the iniquitous and wrong decision only on consulting the Government records, without giving the respondent any opportunity and access to that. Conversely the Court of Settlement felt the necessity of ascertaining the factum of possession by examining persons alleged to be in possession of the building in question, but without examining any such per-son came to finding in respect of possession of the building on the basis of Government records concerned. 

 9. On perusal of the decision of the Court of Settlement, we note that the Government challenged the identity of the petitioner before the Court of Settlement, Musammat Amikun (respondent herein). It was claimed by the Government that the petitioner before the Court of Settlement was a fictitious person. Upon considering the oral testimony of the petitioner, the Court of Settlement noted that she was not aware to the relevant facts about the particulars of the original allottee, and as such, her statement to the effect that she was the daughter of Md. Nazir was not reliable. In this regard, we also note that before the Court of Settlement, the petitioner deposed that she was born in Mymensingh, whereas in her petition filed before the Chairman of the Court of Settlement, she had stated that she was born in Dhaka. 

 11. The High Court Division reversed the decision of the Court of Settlement taking into consideration that the petitioner before the Court of Settlement (respondent herein) was in possession of all the original papers which in its estimation "raises valid equitable presumption that the petitioner is the genuine claimant of the house as the heir of Md. Nazir." The High Court Division observed that the Court of Settlement arrived at the finding that the petitioner is not the heir of Md. Nazir only on suspicion caused by some of her oral testimony which she made because of her illness, nervousness and panic, in utter disregard of the documentary evidence. At this stage, we have to say that we do not find any evidence to suggest that the petitioner before the Court of Settlement was suffering from any illness, nervousness or panic at the time when she deposed before the. Court of Settlement. 

 13. With regard to the original documents, which the High Court Division relied upon in finding that the respondent herein was in possession of the case building, we are constrained to hold that in the facts of the present case, simply being in possession of the original documents relating to a building which has been declared abandoned, does not ipso facto prove the entitlement of the possessor of the original document to be entitled to a declaration that the building was not lawfully declared as abandoned. Merely proving the title of Md. Nazir does not help the petitioner before the Court of Settlement in establishing that the building was not lawfully declared abandoned when she made fundamental errors about her predecessor and her own place of birth. We also note that the respondent herein firstly claimed that she had acquired the building in question by way of gift from her father. But subsequently, she attempted to prove her ownership by way of inheritance by producing a succession certificate. We also note that the respondent filed Succession Case No.111 of 1984 when Md. Nazir is claimed to have died in 1971. All these facts tend to support the view taken by the Court of Settlement that the respondent, Most. Amikun was not a genuine heir of Md. Nazir. 

 14. By the impugned judgment, the High Court Division reversed the decision of the Court of Settlement as if it was sitting in appeal. In the case of Mostafa Kamal (Md.)-Vs-First Court of Settlement and others, 48 DLR(AD)61, this Division endorsed the legal principle that the High Court Division in exercise of its writ jurisdiction cannot sit as a court of appeal over the judgement of the Court of Settlement for re-settling the questions of fact. In that case also the Court of Settlement on consideration of the materials on record arrived at a finding that the petitioner in that case was not the daughter and heir of the original lessee and that she had not been in possession of the house in question at the relevant time. The respondent herein had to prove not only her title in the building but also that she was the genuine and legal heir of the original allottee of the building. 

 15. It has been held time and again that when a building is declared abandoned, the onus is on the claimant of the building to prove that the building is not abandoned. In the instant case, the respondent failed to prove her claim to be the heir of the original allottee and also that the building was unlawfully declared abandoned. She could not prove that she was in possession of the building. We note from annexure-F that the letter dated 7 September, 1982 from the Section Officer of the Ministry of Home Affairs addressed to the applicant's mother that she was living at 6/3 Champatali Lane, Sowari Ghat, Dhaka, which is the address given by the claimant as her husband's address. That would mean that the applicant's mother was at that time with her son-in-law and not in the case building. The Court of Settlement, having called the relevant records for the building in question, came to a finding that the building was in the possession of the Government and declared it as having been lawfully declared as abandoned property.

3. The material facts, relevant for disposal of the Writ Petitions Nos. 6082 of 2015 to 2085 of 2015 succinctly, are that:— The respondent No. 2 being the Original lessee owner as Claimant claiming the case properties filed 4(Four) applications under section 7(1) of the Ordinance, LIV of 1985 before the First Court of Settlement and those were registered as Settlement Case Nos. 652 of 1988, 48 of 1992, 49 of 1992 and Case No. 50 of 1992 respectively for exclusion of the said property from the 'Ka' list of Abandoned Buildings listed under the provision of section 5(1)(a) of the Said Ordinance, LIV of 1985 and those 4(Four) cases were heard analogously and disposed of by a single judgment and order by the respondent No.l. It is stated that the properties in questions were allotted to Mr. Waqar Ahmed by the then Governor of the East Pakistan. Thereafter on behalf of the Government Lease Agreements were executed in favour of Waqar Ahmed. The Registered Lease Deed No. 14568 dated 23-10-1963 pertaining to Holding No. 140, Motijheel C/A. Dhaka, the Registered Lease Deed No. 1480 dated 8-2-1960 pertaining to Holding No. 104, Road No. 3, Dhanmondi R/A, Dhaka, the Registered Lease Deed No. 2582 dated 8-2-1960 pertaining to holding No. 10, Motijheel C/A, Dhaka and the Registered lease. Deed No. 7488 dated 17-5-1963 pertaining to Holding No. 64, Dilkusha C/A, Dhaka in favour of the allottee for the period of 99 years. After Independence of Bangladesh the Original Lessee had been ceased to occupy. supervise and manage the case property in person and his whereabouts was not known to the Government, as such, the case property assumed abandonment Character under Article 2(1) of the President's Order No. 16 of 1972 and the said property have been vested in the Government under Article 4 of the President's Order No. 16 of 1972 and the Government has been administering, Controlling and Managing the abandoned property through tenants. 

 6. The Respondent No. 1, the First Court of Settlement by its judgment and order dated 14-10-2010 allowed the cases and accordingly directed to exclude the case property from the 'Ka' list of abandoned buildings finding that the Title Suit No. 660 of 1985 is still pending before the Third Court of Sub-Judge, Dhaka for a declaration that the buildings in the 4(four) cases are not abandoned property and since it was filed before publication of the notification in the Official Gazette showing the case properties as abandoned ' properties in violation of Proviso (b) of Article 5 of the Ordinance No. LIV of 1985 and also ordered that as the question of abandonment is to be decided in the above civil suit, and thus, the Court can not say anything about the abandonment or otherwise of the properties in question and thus the Court of Settlement has committed illegality based on no evidence and acted without jurisdiction and the Court without ascertaining the whereabouts of the Claimant Waqar Ahmed at the material point of time i.e. on 28-2-1972 the respondent No.1 heard Settlement Case No. 652 of 1988 analogously with other 3 cases and passed the impugned Judgment and order and thus the petitioner impugned the Said Judgment and order in the Writ Petitions bonafide. It is stated that the Claimant Waqar Ahmed filed 4(four) applications under section 7(1) read with section 8(1) of the Ordinance LIV of 1985 for excluding his 4 houses from the abandoned buildings wherein he mentioned the Title Suit No. 660 of 1985 that was filed challenging the auction sale of 4 houses published in the Daily Ittefaq on 1-9-1985 filed by him on 11-7-1985; it is mentioned here that the elder son of the Original Allottee named Feroz Ahmed also filed an application under section 7(1) of the Ordinance, LIV of 1985 for excluding his property situated at 12-13, Baro Katara, Police Station-Lalbag, Dhaka listed in the 'Ka' list of abandoned property and published in Bangladesh Gazette (Extraordinary) dated 23-9-1986 at page 9762(13) SL. No, 112 and the application was registered as settlement Case No. 683 of 1988 and he lost his case before the Court of Settlement and against which he filed Writ Petition No. 1500 of 2003 as false personification and in the midst of hearing the Rule on behalf of the Respondent No.1-Government filed an application enclosing the reports of CID regarding whereabouts of Feroz Ahmed for having personal appearance before this Hon'ble Court but the petitioner Could not produce him before this Hon'ble Court and ultimately on 16-5-2013 the Rule was discharged for default when the matter was taken up for hearing and till to day no restoration application has been filed to restore the Rule that since Feroz Ahmed and his father Waqar Ahmed left Pakistan and used to live in Pakistan and acquired domicile of Pakistan under the Pakistan Citizenship Act, 1951 and they permanently resided at Pakistan as Pakistani National at the address No. House No. C-50, Block-A, KDA Co-operative Society, Karachi, Pakistan. 

 10. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, the learned Attorney-General with Sukumar Biswas, Assistant Attorney-General appearing on behalf of the petitioners in all the writ petitions have submitted that the Court of Settlement while passing the impugned judgment and order has miserably failed to apply its judicial mind to appreciate the relevant provisions of President's Order No. 16 of 1972 and arrived at a wrong finding for exclusion of the property from the `Ka' list of Abandoned Property on relying .upon the pending suit before the Sub-Judge, Dhaka for declaration of title that the 4 houses are not abandoned property, therefore, the impugned judgment and order is liable to be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 11. He has further Submitted that under the provision of section 5(1)(a) of the Ordinance LIV of 1985, the inclusion of the property in the list so published is called the conclusive evidence of facts under section 5(2) of the Ordinance and the same has been vested in the Government with effect from 28-2-1972 under the provision of Article 4 of President's Order No. 16 of 1972, that the respondent No. 2 having failed to rebut this legal presumption of law and facts by producing and examining his positive evidence regarding whereabouts of the original owner (alleged claimant Waqar Ahmed) at the material time that is, on 28-2-1972, therefore, the impugned judgment and order is liable to be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 12. He has further argued that in view of the definition of the abandoned property under Article 2(1) of the President's Order No. 16 of 1972 the Respondent No. 2 has failed to prove that he was present in Bangladesh, his whereabouts was known to the Government or he did not cease to occupy supervise or manage the cease property in person and thus the legal presumption of correctness of abandonment under section 5(2) of the Ordinance No. LIV of 1985 stands unrebutted, and thus, the respondent No. 1 has acted without jurisdiction relied upon only the suit pending before the Court of Civil Jurisdiction therefore, the impugned judgment and order is erroneous and not justified in the eye of law. He has also submitted that the Respondent No. 2 as Claimant has failed to discharge his onus by producing his Original Documents and giving oral evidence in respect of title, possession and whereabouts of the Claimant at the relevant time i.e. on 28-2-1972 which is the main essence of President's Order No. 16 of 1972, as such, the Court of Settlement has acted without jurisdiction which is liable to be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 13. He has further added that by dint of fraudulent judgment and decree dated 28-4-1993 passed in Title Suit No. 72 of 1992 and the judgment and order dated 14-10-1992 passed in Settlement Case Nos. 652 of 1988, Case No. 48 of 1992, Case No. 49 of 1992 and Case No. 50 of 1992 the alleged Waqar Ahmed very recently by using the present address behind the backed by the land grabber is making continuous pressure upon the respondents to release the houses in question, as such, the Secretary, Ministry of Housing and Public Works sent the Nathi to the Office of the Attorney-General for filing Writ Petition on 28-4-2015. The learned Attorney-General endorsed Mr. Sukumar Biswas, the learned Assistant Attorney-General to make a draft of Writ Petition and the learned Assistant Attorney-General after collecting necessary document from here and abroad filed the same on 28-5-2015 and since the aforesaid judgment and order is obtained fraudulently, it vitiates everything; that since fraud has been detected after the passing of the impugned Judgment by the Government agencies and the fraud is apparent on the face of the record that the plaintiff being a fake person filed the above cases and suit. Since, fraud has been committed, the petitioner shall not be debarred to file writ petition and, as such, to protect the interest of the Government these Writ Petitions were filed. 

 14. The writ petitioner by filing the Supplementary Affidavit added some facts and information. Learned Attorney-General argued that the petitioner filed 4 Writ Petition being Nos. 6082 of 2015, 6083 of 2015, 6084 of 2015 and 6085 of 2015 respectively challenging the legality and propriety of the impugned judgment and order dated 14-10-1992 passed by the First Court of Settlement in Settlement Case No. 48 of 1992, Ka-22, page-9762(6) pertaining to House No. 140, Motijheel Commercial Area, Dhaka (heard analogously with Settlement Case No. 652 of 1998 (Ka-4, Page 9762(6), Motijheel Commercial Area, Dhaka), pertaining to house No.10, Motijheel Commercial Area, Dhaka, Case No. 49 of 1992, Ka-29, Page-9762(6), pertaining to House No. 64, Dilkusha Commercial Area, Dhaka and Case No. 50 of 1992, Ka-16, Page-9762(14), pertaining to House No. 104, Road No. 03 (New-08), Dhanmondi Residential Area, Dhaka) allowed the cases and directed for exclusion of the 4 houses mentioned in the cases from the `Ka' list of the Abandoned Buildings prepared and published in the Bangladesh Gazette (Extra-Ordinary) on 23-9-1986) (Annexure-'C' to the Writ Petition) and obtained Rules and an order of Status quo on 17-6-2015 were served on the address of the respondent but he did not appear before the authority claiming that he has filed the suit. On perusal the cause title of the suit it appears that one Mr. Md. Waz Uddin as Attorney filed the suit on behalf of the respondent No. 2. So, he assiduously try to heckling the judgment of the Settlement Court saying the same is nothing but a judgment obtained by personification which is per in-curiam. 

 15. The respondent No. 2 by filing Affidavit-in-Oppositions contested all the Rules, through a power of Attorney named IVY Real Estate Limited represented by its Managing Director Mosfiqur Rahman of House No. 19, Road No. 1, Dhanmondi residential Area, Dhaka-1205, contending, inter alia, that the statement made in the Writ Petition which has not admitted by the instant respondent No. 2 deem to have been denied. Therefore, the attorney of the respondent No. 2 has admitted some statement stating those are matter of facts, however, some statement were denied. The deponent categorically stated that the judgment and order passed by the Court of Settlement as challenged in this Writ Petition has already been merged and got validated into the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court in the title suit No. 660 of 1985 the appellate Court and the Hon'ble Appellate Division in the aforesaid cases. As such, this Writ Petition is not maintainable, and the Rule is liable to be discharged for ends of justice. 

 16. It has further stated that the Court of settlement has committed no illegality in passing the judgment and order in question, and in the judgment the Court correctly observed that since the aforesaid title suit was filed before publication of the gazette notification showing the case properties as abandonment properties in violation of the proviso (b) of Article 5 of the Ordinance No. 54 of 1985 and the question of abandonment and declaration of title is to be decided in the above civil suit. As such, this writ petition is not maintainable, and the Rule is liable to be discharged for ends of justice. 

 17. Mr. Shah Monjurul Huq the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent No.2 on the other hand, sincerely said, that the judgment pronounced by the Court of Settlement is innocent judgment though in the judgment the Court opined the following: "It appears from the papers filed by the petitioner that he filed Title Suit No. 660/1985 in the Third Court of Sub Judge, Dhaka for a declaration that the buildings in the 4 (Four) cases are not abandoned property and it is still pending. As the petitioner filed the above suit against the Secretary, Ministry of Works and others for a declaration that the cases buildings are not abandoned property, prior to the publication of the notification in the official Gazette, showing the case properties as abandoned properties in violation of prevision (b) of Article 5 of Ordinance No. 54 of 1985, we are of opinion that the cases should be allowed." So, the fate of the above mentioned property would be decided in the Title Suit No. 660 of 1985, In view of the above observation Mr. Hoq find Afficulties to support the Judgment of the Court of Settlement as there was no discussion regarding adducing the evidences and produced the document examining the witness to satisfy the Court.

full_judgment:
2. The facts necessary to dispose this appeal are that the appellants and respondent Nos. 3 and 4 as the plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 612 of 1977 in the Court of Munsif, third Court, Narail (now the Assistant Judge) for declaration of title to the suit land on the averment that the suit land originally belonged to Abhoy Charan Bhattacharay and Prabol Chandra Bhattacharaya, two full brothers under erstwhile landlords, Babu Dhirendra Nath Roy and others at a jama of Rs. 13/1/3 paisa and was recorded and finally published in their names in CS Khatian No. 348 of mouza Bhowakhali. Subsequently, Abhoy Charan Bhattacharaya died leaving behind his only son, Manindra Nath Bhattacharaya who also died unmarried leaving behind his uncle Prabol Charan Bhattacharaya as his heir and thus, Prabol Charan became the sixteen annas owner of the suit land. Prabol Charan later died leaving behind his only son, Harendra Nath Bhattacharaya as his heir who had been impleaded in the suit as pro-forma defendant No. 3. Harendra Nath Bhattacharaya gave oral settlement of the suit land in favour of the plaintiffs on 7th Magh, 1355 BS corresponding to 21-10-1949 on receipt of an amount of Rs.1,500 as salami at an annual rental of Rs. 10-00 and granted receipts for those. Ever since the settlement, the plaintiffs had all along been in continuous and peaceful possession of the suit land for long over twelve years and thus, had also acquired statutory title by adverse possession. During the last rent roll operation, the suit land was wrongly recorded in the names of Harendra Nath Bhattacharaya and deceased Manindra Nath and in such circumstances, the plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 204 of 1976 in the 3rd Court of Munsif, Narail and the suit was decreed ex-parte in their favour. Thereafter, on the basis of the said decree, the plaintiffs went to mutate their names by filing an application before the Circle Officer (Revenue), Narail and from the report of the Tashilder concerned, as submitted to the Circle Officer (Revenue), it came to the light for the first time that the suit land was enlisted as enemy property. The defendants had no title or possession in the suit land but out of greed of grabbing the suit land, they filed Miscellaneous Case No. 367 of 1969 in the 3rd Court of Munsif, Narail under section 143A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (the Act, 1950), but when the plaintiffs, on being added as parties, filed written objection, the defendants had created two forged kabalas, purportedly form Harendra Nath Bhattacharaya and Manindra Nath Bhattacharaya through false personation. The former had left this country and settled in India long ago and the latter died long ago. Late Manindra Nath and Harendra Nath were railway employees in India and never executed the kabalas. When the plaintiffs on the basis of the decrees obtained by them, went to mutate their names and filed an application for that purpose, they came to learn that in the meantime, defendant Nos. 1 and 2 had managed to get their names mutated on the strength of their forged kabalas and the Circle Officer (Revenue), Narail refused to allow the mutation in the names of the plaintiffs on 2-11-1977 and being emboldened thereby, defendant Nos. 1 and 2 on 8-11-1977 denied lawful title of the plaintiffs in the suit land, giving rise to the plaintiffs' cause of action and hence the suit. 

 3. Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 contested the suit by filing a joint written statement denying all the material statements made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that Harendra Nath Bhattacharaya and Man indra Nath Bhattacharaya gave oral settlement of the suit land in favour of defendant No. I at a salami of Rs. 1,500 and at a rent of Rs. 10/4/annas on 18th Magh, 1358 BS and granted a receipt for the amount of salami and rent. But during preparation of the rent roll, the record at the preliminary stage was prepared in the names of Manindra Nath and Harendra Nath Bhattacharaya whereupon defendant No. I filed an objection under section 19(1) of the Act, 1950, but the same was rejected. Subsequently, he filed Miscellaneous Case No. 367 of 1969 in the 3rd Court of Munsif, Narail for correction of the record under section 143A of the Act, 1950 and the question of title having been involved the said case was withdrawn. Thereafter, for avoiding complication, he obtained two kabalas, one in his name and another in the name of his wife, defendant No. 2, from Manindra Nath and Harendra Nath who themselves executed the kabalas. Subsequently, on the basis of the said kabalas, they mutated their names. The settlement in favour of the plaintiffs was forged, fraudulent and ante-dated. The defendants initiated a proceeding under section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure against the plaintiffs which was made absolute. The plaintiffs had brought this suit on false allegations in collaboration with certain persons of Bhowalkhali. The suit was barred under the principles of estoppel, waive? and acquiescence and limitation and was also bad for defect of parties and, as such, the same was liable to be dismissed. 

 4. The trial Court by its judgment and decree dated 30-3-1989 dismissed the suit. Against the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the plaintiffs filed Title Appeal No. 60 of 1989 before the District Judge, Narail and the learned Subordinate Judge, Narail by his judgment and decree dated 30-8-1992 dismissed the appeal. The plaintiffs then filed the above mentioned revision before the High Court Division and a Single Bench of the High Court Division by the impugned judgment and order discharged the Rule as stated hereinbefore. Against the judgment and order of the High Court Division, the plaintiffs filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 699 of 2008 before this Court and leave was granted to consider the submission of the learned Counsel for the appellants to the following effect: 

 "Mr Mahbubey Alam, learned Counsel, appearing for the petitioners submitted that the High Court Division committed error that the plaintiff-respondents having filed necessary papers to show the decree passed by a competent civil Court in their favour in Title Suit No. 204 of 1976 and Title Suit No. 506 of 1976 and the Courts below having dismissed the plaintiffs' suit without considering those decree passed in respect of the suit land. The learned Counsel further submitted that by expunging the observation of the Courts below regarding the ownership of the suit land the High Court Division virtually made the Rule absolute in Civil Revision No. 1432 of 1994 and thereby granting relief to the defendants. The learned Counsel finally submitted that the High Court Division expunging the observation regarding the ownership of the suit land and thereby has created a bar to the plaintiffs to protect their possession by making representation to the Government for obtaining lease from the Government." 

 8. Since the plaintiffs failed to prove their title to the suit land by virtue of their oral settlement thereby their right to the suit property was not established. We do not find anything on their part to be aggrieved due to the expunction of the observations of the Courts below that the suit property vested in the Government as vested and non-resident property. So far as the non-consideration of the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 506 of 1976 is concerned, it is by now a well settled legal principle that the finding in a suit for permanent injunction cannot be binding in a suit for title. So far as the ex parte decree passed in Title Suit No. 204 of 1946 of the Court of Munsif, third Court is concerned that suit was filed for correction of the record, the trial Court and the Appellate Court rightly refused to rely upon it as the plaintiffs failed to prove their title to the suit land on the basis of their oral settlement as decided in the instant suit. 

 Therefore, we do not find any substance on the point of non-consideration of the judgment and decree passed in the said two suits (Title Suit Nos. 204 of 1976 and 506 of 1976) on which leave was granted. Since the plaintiffs failed to prove their title in the suit land by virtue of their oral settlement, the Courts below as well as the High Court Division did not commit any error of law in passing the impugned judgment and order calling for interference by this Court.

With
