parties:
Government of Bangladesh and others -------- Appellants (in both CA No. 88-89 of 2011)
VS
Md Alamgir Hossain and others  ------------Respondents (In both the appeals)
full_judgment:
That the respondent No.1, as plaintiff, instituted Other Class Suit No. 97 of 1997 for declaration of title and mandatory injunction in respect of 3500 Ajutangsha of land (as described in the schedule of the plaint) in CS Plot No. 1219 RS Plot No. 3818 appertaining to CS Khatian No. 588, MRR Khatian No. 829, RS Khatian (attested) No.3860 of Sutrapur Mouza within Bogra Pourashava, District-Bogra, contending intern alia that the suit land originally belonged to Md Haider Ali Khan Panni who possessed the same by constructing building and planting various type of frees. On the death of the said Md Haider Ali Khan Panni his two sons, namely, Mohammad Ali Khan Panni @ Sayeed Ali Khan Panni and Mehedi Ali Khan Panni have been possessing the same as their guest house. Sayeed Ali Khan Panni, who was in possession of the suit land died leaving behind proforma defendants No. 5 to 9 as his legal heirs, who while jointly possessing the same for over 12 years, made some renovations in the suit land including erecting boundary walls and planting trees of various types. Subsequently, they transferred the suit land by two registered deeds No. 14492 and 14493 both dated 31-8-1997 to the plaintiff and handed over the possession thereof. It is alleged that inspite of the fact that the Government has no right, title and interest in the suit land had been trying to Dispossess the plaintiff from the same, Hence the suit. 

 3. Defendants No. 1, 2 and 4 contested the suit, by filing written statement, denying all the materials allegation and contending inter alia that the suit land along with other lands was requisitioned in 1957 for Agricultural Extension Department in accordance with law and possession was handed over to the requiring body on 8-5-1958. Since then the same is being used by the aforesaid defendants for more than 12 years. In the meantime, the Government having decided to acquire the property finally and took all steps in accordance with law and by final publication of the same in the Gazette Notification publishing on 4th May, 1961 0.62 acre of land in CS Plots No. 1210, 1216 and 1219 were finally acquired the Agricultural Department after taking possession of the said acquired land including the suit plot (CS Plot No. 1219), constructed several structures on the same upon obtaining permission from the Bogra Paurashava. The defendants paid tax, electric and telephone bills to the respective authority by opening separate khatian No. 4671 in the name of defendant No. 2 lawfully. Thus the plaintiff or the proforma defendant who were stated by heirs of Haider Ali Khan Panni have no right, title and interest in the suit land. The alleged- deeds of the plaintiff are forged, fabricated and manufactured by which no title and possession vested upon the plaintiff. 

 11. Mr Mahabuby Alam, the learned Attorney General, appearing on behalf of the appellants as well as for the petitioner submits that the suit land has been finally acquired which has been notified in the gazette date 4th may, 1961 and these being legal bar in challenging such acquisition in suits; the trial Court as well as the High Court Division committed error of law in decreeing the suit. He submits that the said factual and legal position also has not been considered by this Division while dismissing the leave petitions. Thus the said judgment of this Division is required to be reviewed. He further submits that earlier in Title Suit No. 148 of 1965, instituted by Mehadi Ali Khan Panni, alleged predecessor of the plaintiff, prayed for his tittle in Plot No.1216 and obtained decree and in another suit being Title Suit No. 42 of 1979 filed by one Ramoni Madhab Das, notice dated 8th January, 1979 for eviction of the occupants of Plot No. 1210 has been declared illegal. But since plot Nos. 1210, 1216 and 1219 are maintainable under section 14A of the Specific Relief Act and, as such, dismissal of the leave petitions, which relates to Plot No. 1219, is required to be reviewed and, as such, the instant appeals should be allowed. He next submits that this Division, while affirming the decree of mandatory injunction, did not consider that there is no allegation made in the plaint that the government made construction on the suit land during the pendency of the instant suit, which is an error apparent on the face of the record. Hence dismissal of the leave petition is thus erroneous and the judgment complained of herein is required to be reviewed. He finally submits that admittedly the plaintiff of the instant suit is not in possession of the suit plot and he having not prayed for recovery of possession, as consequential relief, decreeing the suit upto this Division is erroneous and, as such, the judgment passed by this Division is required to be reviewed and thereby both the appeals should be allowed. 

 12. Mr Sharifuddin Chaklader, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of plaintiff-respondent No.1 submits that the Government has miserably failed to prove by producing any evidence that the suit land was ever acquired nor they could prove; that any prior or subsequent notice for requisition and acquisition, in prescribed form, was ever served upon the plaintiff. They even failed to produce any material to show that there was proposal of the Deputy Commissioner for requisition or acquisition of the suit land or initiation of any LA case or payment of compensation etc. Therefore, he submits that the alleged bar to file a suit on the plea of requisition or acquisition does not arise at all. He next submits that the trial Court as well as the High Court Division concurrently found that the suit of the plaintiff-respondent No. 1 is competent and maintain-able under sections 42 and 55 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 and, as such, the impugned judgment and decree calls for no interference by this Division. He next submits that there is no overriding public purpose/interest or national/public interest to defeat the lawful right, title, interest and possession of the plaintiff-respondent No.1, which has been accrued by dint of two duly registered sale deeds in 1997. He finally submits that the appellants are under a legal obligation to remove the illegally constructed structures from the suit land and, as such, there is no merit in the appeals and therefore, the same are liable to be dismissed. 

 13. Having considered the submissions of the learned Advocates of both the sides and on perusal of the judgment under review and other materials on record it appears that the appellant/petitioner claim that the three plots being CS Plot Nos. 1210, 1216 and 1219 subject matter of three suits have been acquired by the government which have been published in the gazette notification dated 4-5-1961. Thus the points to be determined are whether (i) on the face of section 5(7) read with section 14A of the (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948 a suit, in respect of an acquired properly, is maintainable; (ii) Plot No. 1210 being not the subject matter of earlier Title Suits, wherein the title of the plaintiffs of those suits have been declared along with injunction, decreeing those suits subject matter of which are finally acquired by the government, decreeing the suits and dismissal of the civil petitions are erroneous; (iii) in the absence of any construction being made by the appellants in the suit land during the pendency of the suit granting of mandatory injunction is justified; and (iv) whether in the absence of seeking consequential relief by way of recovery of possession the present suit is maintainable under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act . 

 20. In the present cases question may arise who are the affected persons and who can claim or be paid compensation pursuant to such acquisition of the lands described in the gazette notification dated 4-5-1961. By filing additional paper book dated 7-2-2017 the appellant (government) stated that suit plot no. 1219 was the land of the Waqf Estate from whom the same has been requisitioned first and then acquired by the government and the same has been notified in the gazette on 4-5-1961. But on perusal of the judgment of the trial Court dated 30-11-2003 passed in Other Class Suit No. 97 of 1997 it appears that the suit plots belonged to Zaminder Haider Ali Khan Panni of Korotia. But, Exhibit-'Ka' dated 17-2-1955, upon which, the defendant relied to claim that the suit plots are waqf property 'is not a deed of waqf and it does not contain any description of any property. Such paper has no relevancy about the ownership/title of any property. Considering all these aspects both the courts below held that 'the plaintiff respondent herein has lawful right, title and interest in the suit property'. So the claim of the government-appellant that 'admittedly the property was the land of an Waqf Estate' is not at all sustainable. Since none, but the subsequent purchasers/ transferees' of the original owner have come and instituted the suit claiming their title in the suit plots, they should not be deprived of adequate compensation. Hence we are of the view that the plaintiff-respondents are entitled to receive the compensation of the land which have been acquired by the government as a matter of their constitutional right.

full_judgment:
9. In support of the instant Rule the categorical assertion of the accused petitioners is that earlier in the year 2001 the executant of the deed of power of attorney namely Mrs Delwara Begum, the mother of the informant along with others instituted Title Suit No. 131 of 2001 in the Court of learned Assistant Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka impleading the defendants, the accused petitioners, for a decree of permanent injunction stating, inter alia that they had purchased the land in question measuring 0.33 acres vide deed No. 1685 dated 1-3-1995 from their predecessors. They accordingly erected their house with boundary wall and got their name mutated with regard to the suit land. However, the defendants (the accused petitioners) alleged to have threatened to dispossess them from the suit land in the month of April, 2001; hence, the suit. 

 10. The accused petitioners as defendants contested the said suit by filing written statements denying all the material averment so made therein stating, inter alia, that in 1933-34 the properties of Baunia Mouza under CS Khatian No.202 comprising CS Plot Nos. 1520, 1521, 2288, 2302, 2313 measuring 15.19 acres were put into auction for arrear of rent under Certificate Case No.255DW/1933-34. One Khetro Mohan Barai and Rahman Box Bepari purchased the suit land and ultimately, the auction sale was confirmed in their .favour on 30-8-1934. Thus, the right, title and interest of Keti Bibi and others were extinguished. It has also been contended therein that one Falu Miah purchased 1.72 acres of land from one Khetro Mohan Barai on 28-1-1946 vide deed No.574 and Falu Miah and his brothers had purchased 3.15 acres of land on 24-8-1960 vide deed No. 10946. They, however, had purchased another 1.901/2 acres of land on 27-9-1960 vide deed No. 12307 from one Rahman Box Bepari with possession thereof. Accordingly, they had been paying rent to the authority concern. 

 14. The plaintiff-being the judgment-debtor namely Mrs Delwara Begum and others being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with preferred Title Appeal No. 359 of 2003 before the learned District Judge, Dhaka which was ultimately heard by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka who upon hearing both the parties had allowed the appeal and had sent back the case on remand vide judgment and decree dated 29-6-2006. The defendants-respondents, the accused petitioners in the present case, accordingly preferred Civil Revision No. 4308 of 2006 before this Court. Upon hearing the respective contending parties the Rule so issued was ultimately made absolute vide judgment and decree dated 19-2-2009. Said judgment and decree passed in Civil Revision No. 4308 of 2006 is still in force. 

 15. At this juncture, Mr Md Zakir Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing for the accused petitioners categorically submits that.in the suit for permanent injunction, instituted by the mother of the informant Mrs Delwara Begum and others, they had measurably failed to prove their prima facie title and possession over the suit property (the case land). On the contrary considering Exhibit-ka, the "boinanama," which is the subject matter of the instant criminal case, the civil court found that the auction purchase of the predecessor of the accused petitioners had been proved and had ultimately dismissed the suit on the ground that the plaintiffs had failed to specify the boundary in the respective deeds as relied upon them. 

 17. He lastly submits that the informant opposite party No. 2 is admittedly the son of the plaintiff No.1 named Mrs Delwara Begum of Title Suit No. 131 of 2001 as such, it was within his knowledge that alleged "boinama" was produced in evidence in the said suit. Therefore, since no complaint has been made by the said court concern, the instant case is barred under section 195(1)(c) of the Code. But the revisional court while disposing of the revisional application filed by the informant had failed to consider the said factual as well as legal position of the case and thus, has occasioned miscarriage of justice. Accordingly, he submits that upon striking down the impugned order dated 27-6-2016 passed in Metro Criminal Revision No. 129 of 2015 the instant Rule is liable to be made absolute. 

 18. Conversely, Mr Mansur Habib, the learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party No. 2 by filing a counter affidavit submits that Title Suit No. 131 of 2001 was a suit for a permanent injunction, not for declaration of title over the land in question. He also submits that in the said title suit no issue was framed with regard to the title of the plaintiffs in connection with the suit land. As such, he submits that the observations and findings so mad by this Hon'ble Court while disposing of Civil Revision No. 4308 of 2006 cannot go to have any bearing whatsoever in determining the issues as have been agitated in the instant criminal case. 

 19. Further, he submits that admittedly in Title Suit No. 131 of 2001 a photocopy of the "boinama" was given in evidence by the defendants, the accused petitioners. As such, he submits that vide the decisions of the case of Moklesur Rahman Sharif vs State, Jamiruddin Sharif reported in 47 DLR 229 since the original has not been produced in evidence section 195(1)(c) of the Code of Criminal Procedure is not attracted in the instant case. 

 23. It appears from record that earlier in the year 2001 the mother of the informant one Mrs Delwara Begum along with others instituted Title Suit No. 131 of 2001 before the court concern for a decree of permanent injunction impleading the accused petitioners as defendants, having been threatened by them to be dispossessed from the suit property. The petitioners as defendants contested the said suit by filing written statement. During the course of trial both the parties adduced evidence both oral and documentary. The petitioners, however, in support of their claim had produced the alleged "boinama" in connection with Certificate Case No. 255/1933-34 which was given in evidence and marked as Exhibit-'Ka'. The trial court upon hearing both the contending parties ultimately dismissed the suit for the failure of the plaintiffs to prove their prima facie title and possession over the suit property. But at the same time made certain observations to the effect that by Exhibit 'Ka' the auction purchase of the suit property by the predecessor of the defendants i.e. the accused petitioners had been proved. The appeal preferred by the plaintiffs as appellants though was allowed in Title Appeal No. 359 of 2003 but it was sent back on remand. The High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 4308 of 2006, preferred by the defendant respondents i.e., the accused petitioners, on the other hand had set aside the judgment and decree dated 29-6-2006 passed in the said appeal and thereby had affirmed the observations and findings of the trial court. 

 24. In view of the above position of facts, the accused petitioners have assailed the impugned order dated 27-6-2016 passed by the revisional court setting aside the order dated 27-11-2014 passed by the learned Magistrate concern allowing the application of the petitioners under section 241A of the Code on two counts. Firstly, since alleged "boinama" in question was given in evidence in Title Suit No.131 of 2001 and marked as Exhibit-'Ka' and that the plaintiffs had never raised objection as to its genuinely nor the trial court made any complaint to that effect hence, the instant case is barred under section 195(1)(c) of the Code. Secondly, the trial court (the civil court concern) had categorically observed while dismissing the said suit that the auction purchase of the property in question, vide the said alleged "boinama," had been proved and that said observation is still in force. In the stated position of facts and law placing the petitioners to face trial under sections 406/420/467/468 and 471 of the Penal Code is nothing but a glaring instance of miscarriage of justice. 

 25. During the course of hearing of the instant Rule, the accused petitioners by filing supplementary affidavit have annexed the copy of the alleged "boinama", which was earlier given in evidence in Title Suit No. 131 of 2001 and marked as Exhibit-Ka. From perusal of the same it appears that, in fact, a photocopy of the said "boinama", which was subsequently notarized by the officer concern, was given in evidence and was marked as Ext. 'ka'. 

 "the words "produced or given in evidence" in section 195 refers to the production of the original and not the production of a copy and this is for a very sound reason that the court before which a copy of the document is produced is not really in a position to express any opinion about the genuineness of the original documents." It was held in this decision that "the language used in section 195(1)(c) was deliberate in excluding the copies of the forged document." 

 "the absence of complaint by the court cannot stand as a bar to the trial of the accused petitioner for forgery if the original of the alleged forged documents is not used or given in evidence in the court." 

 28. In agreement with the above observations and findings one of the Benches of this Division also observed in Moklesur Rahman Sharif vs State reported in 47 DLR 229 at para-graph 12 "when the original forged instrument is not used in the court section 195(1)(c) is no bar to a proceeding for forgery". 

 29. We find no reason to depart from the observations of the Privy Council so made in the cases as referred above and also by one of the Benches of the High Court Division. Accordingly, it is our concerned view that since the original "boinama" has not been produced in evidence in Title Suit No. 131 of 2001, but a photocopy of the same, therefore, section 195(1)(c) of the Code of Criminal Procedure is not attracted in the instant case. 

 30. As to the second contention of the accused petitioners we are of the view that the instant criminal case, launched by the opposite party No. 2 as informant against the accused petitioners, is independent of producing the photocopy of the document in question in evidence in Title Suit No. 131 of 2001. Moreover, there is no bar to file a criminal case alleging genuinely of the said document on the plea that photocopy of the same has been given in evidence in connection with a civil suit.

parties:
Ashwini Kumar Singha ------ Petitioner 
Vs
Shushi Singha and others ------- Opposite-Parties
full_judgment:
Khizir Ahmed Choudhury J: In this revisional application rule has been issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 4-3-2014 passed by learned Additional District Judge, 5th Court, Sylhet in Title Appeal No. 274 of 2009 dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree dated 26-7-2009 passed by learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Sylhet in Title Suit No. 208 of 2005 dismissing the suit should not be set aside. 

 2. The petitioners herein as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 208 of 2005 before the learned Assistant Judge, Sadar, Sylhet impleading the present opposite parties as defendant praying for declaration that they are entitled to hold and possess the 2nd schedule land which is within first schedule land and the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 12 of 1992 being affirmed In Title Appeal No. 199 of 1996 are void, ineffectual and plaintiffs are not bound by those decrees. 

 3. The case of the plaintiffs in brief, is that, first schedule land belonged to Sree Sree Gobinda Jew Deity within which Gandha Singha was jote tenant whose behalf his son Krishna Kumar Singha built a seemi pacca structure. Thereafter, Gandha Singha transferred the 2nd schedule land to his sister Sharna Kumari by oral gift and left for India. Sharan Kumari while performing Seba Puja died leaving son Monoronjon Singha and daughter Monika Debi. Monika Debi after marriage went to her husband's residence and, as such, Monoronjon Singha became exclusive possessor over the 2nd schedule land. Thereafter, Monoronjon Singha transferred the said land to Dr Motilal Singha by deed dated 8- 1071966 and Dr Motilal Singha continued to perform Seba Puja and other the rituals over the 2nd schedule land. Dr Motilal by receipt dated 11-9-1989 transferred 2nd schedule land and structure thereon to plaintiff and since then the plaintiff are performing Seba Puja and other religious formalalities by residing with family members therein. He also paid municipal holding tax and other taxes. Defendant No. 1 as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 97 of 1985 before the Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Sylhet for declaring his right of shebapuya, maintenance and administer the affairs of the deity. Father of defendant Nos. 2-3 Navo Kumar Singha was defendant No. 2 and defendant Nos. 4-8 was also defendant that suit, the suit was transferred to Artha Rind Adalat, Sylhet renumbered as Title Suit No. 12 of 1992. Utpal Singh, proforma defendant No. 9 as plaintiff also filed a title suit being Title Suit No. 11 of 1992 for declaration of title of deity and for recovery of khas possession. Both the suits were heard analogously and the trial Court dismissed the suits. Defendant No.1preferred Title Appeal No. 199 of 1996 before the District Judge wherein defendant Nos.1-8 filed a solenama with collusion with each other and by that solenama defendant Nos. 1-8 a partitioned the suit properties amongst themselves which is illegal, ineffectual and not binding by the plaintiff. In both suits the plaintiffs were not made parties and, as such, the findings and reasonings of those suits are not binding upon the plaintiff. 

 6. Mr Md Mahbub Ali, learned advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that admittedly the plaintiffs are in possession of the suit land and they have been residing therein with their family members by raising structures. He also submits that original owner of the suit land Garidha Singa has established deity and by successive transfer Monoronjon Singha got the Suit land and he sold the possessory right of the suit land to the present plaintiff on 8-10-1996. He next submits that admittedly the Plaintiffs are occupant in the suit land along with other 20 families and according to the admission of the defendants the present plaintiff used to pay rent to them and the plaintiff are in possession of the suit land. He next submits that in the earlier suits solenama has been filed by the plaintiffs and defendants of that suit collusively beyond the knowledge of the present plaintiffs and since they are not parties in the earlier suits they are not bound by the findings of the suits. He next submits since the plaintiff are in possession in the suit land, he was necessary party therein for resolving the disputes completely and effectually and, as such, the present plaintiffs are not bound by the decrees. He averred that Meanwhile the defendants have filed title Suit No. 51 of 2015 before the Joint District judge, 2nd Court, Sylhet impleading the present petitioner as defendant praying for declaration of title and for recovery of khas possession and as such, question of title and possession and dispossession are to be adjudicated in that title suit. He next submits since the defendants have filed title suits and, as such, until and unless they can get a decree in that suits they cannot claim the office of shebiet legally. He finally submits that the present petitioners are not claiming title in the suit land rather their claiming their possessory right over there and if they can prove possession in the suit land for quite long period they can get a decree in respect of their possessory right. 

 7. The opposite party Nos. 2-4 filed a counter affidavit denying the claim of petitioner. Mr Md Mustaque Ahmed, learned advocate appearing for the opposite parties submits that admittedly suit land belonged to the predecessor of the present opposite party namely Gandha Singha who after purchase of the suit land established deity namely Sree Sree Gobinda Jew Deity and he himself remained as Sebayet of the deity and continued administer Seba Puja and other religious rituals by himself. On the death of Gandha Singha, eldest brother Bhim Singha and thereafter Radha Charon Singha and on his death Pitambar Singh became heirs of the original owners and like their predecessor they have been performing Seba Puja in the suit premises as legal heirs of the original owners. He next submits that the plaintiff were not inducted into possession by the present opposite party rather one Motilal Singha inducted the present plaintiff in the suit land who has got no title over there and the said Motilal Singha was neither Sebayet nor any way related with the deity and, as such, he possession of the present plaintiff cannot be termed as lawful one He next submits that record of right has been prepared in the name of the predecessor of the present opposite parties in the SA record as well as the present record of right from which it can be inferred that the defendants have got absolute right as Sebayet of the deity. He further submits that when dispute arose between the defendants they filed the suit and ultimately they resolved the disputes by compromise where the plaintiffs have got no right to be impleaded as they are in no way related with the deity or the property of the deity and, as such, the decree as granted by the Courts below cannot be set aside at the instance of the present plaintiffs. He next submits that the opposite parties are paying rents record of right has been prepared in their names and municipal holding and other papers are in their names and, as such, the present petitioners claim of possessory right is not sustainable. He finally submits that the plaintiffs are living in the suit land as trespasser as they are not paying rents for quite long period and, as such, their suit is not maintainable in its present forum. 

 8. Having gone through the pleadings, evidence, exhibits and other materials it appears that suit property belonged to Gandha Singha who established the deity over the suit land. The claim of the plaintiff is that Gandha Singha orally gifted the suit property to his sister Sharan Kumari and on his death son Monoronjon was heir who transferred the suit land to Motilal who transferred the same to the present plaintiffs. To substantiate such claim, the plaintiffs are required to proof Sharan Kumari's acquiring title in the suit land but fact is that under Hindu Law property cannot be transferred bural gift and it is not also proved how Motilal got the property and whether Motilal has transferable right over the suit land but these facts have not been proved by the plaintiffs by convincing evidence. 

 9. On the other hand the defendants by showing record of right and other documents tried to establish that they are the lenient descendants of Gandha Singha and they being the Sebayet got right to hold and possess Debutter property. On going through the supplementary affidavit submitted by the opposite parties it appears that record of right has been prepared in the name of the predecessor of the present opposite parties although in the record of right the name of the deity is absent but from admitted fact from both the parties it appears that the suit property comprises homestead, garden, and mondir. The plaintiff are also not claiming title over the suit land, but their specific contention is that they are in possession of the suit land for quite long period and they have got possessory right over the suit land along with other families as Pujaries of the deity. It is also facts that till date not step has been taken for evicting other occupants who are residing in the suit land for quite long period. 

 10. So far possessory right is concerned, persons who claim possessory right cannot claim it against lawful owner as possessory right can be claimed against persons who have no title over the suit land. In the case of Alexander vs Nair Service Society Ltd. AIR 1966 Karala 286 it is held that, 

 "just as a true owner who is dispossessed can, within the period limited by law, being a suit for possession against the person in possession notwithstanding that the latter is not the immediate but only a subsequent intruder, irrespective of the number of nature of the intervening adverse possessory titles, so can a possessory owner against all but the true owner. Does it make any difference then that, in between, there was an interval during which the true owner was in possession? Would that extinguish the title of all earlier possessory owners so as to entrench a subsequent trespasser and give him good title against all but the true owner? We think not. For, the title of a possessory owner springs from the fact of his possession and that is not erased by the true owner regaining possession. The possessory owner's title continues to exist; only it is an imperfect title which is of no avail against the perfect title of the true owner; but against the inferior title of any subsequent possessor, it is a good title. Halsbury (Simonds Edition, Bo. 24 paragraph 492 at page 255) says on the authority of Asher vs Whitlock, (1865) 1 QB 1 and 1907 AC 73." 

 11. Here the questions of title have not been resolved completely in the earlier suit as well as in the appeal. Earlier suits between the defendants opposite parties ended with compromise decree and by virtue of solenama, opposite parties got right to perform puja and other religious rites. The contention of the opposite parties is that since the present plaintiffs have no title over the suit land, they were validly left out from being added as defendants. 

 12. It appears that the present opposite parties has filed a suit being Title Suit No. 51 of  2015 before the Joint District Judge 2nd Court, Sylhet seeking declaration of title and recovery of khas possession by evicting the present plaintiffs. Since the defendants have filed a title suit for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession, this aspect of the matter will be dealt with by the competent Court at the time of peremptory hearing of the suit. 

 13. Admittedly till date no steps were taken by the opposite parties for eviction of the present petitioners, this aspect will also be considered and adjudicated in Title Suit No. 51 of 2015. The petitioners although claimed that they are in possession of the suit land by a deed dated 8-10-1966 from Dr Motilal Singh, the title of Motiall has not been proved in the Courts below, so only their claim is left.regarding their possession, as such all these points will be decided in Title Suit No. 51 of 2015. 

 14. In the above facts and circumstances, since a suit has been filed in competent Court seeking title and recovery of khas possession, all the aspects will be decided and resolved in that suit. Accordingly, the instant rule is disposed of in the terms and observation made herein before. Findings made herein will have no bearing in deciding Title Suit No. 51 of 2015, pending in the Court of Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Sylhet.

parties:
Bangladesh Machine Tools Factory Limited ------- Petitioner
VS
Registrar, Joint Stock Companies and Firms and others -------- Respondents
full_judgment:
2. It has been alleged, amongst other, in the petition that the Petitioner is a public company limited by shares, incorporated under the Companies Act, 1994 (the Act). It is engaged in the business of manufacturing tools and machineries etcetera for meeting the local needs. It is a state owned company run, operated and managed by Bangladesh Army from 2000. The Government of Bangladesh published gazette notification in this respect and thereafter handed over the petitioner company from Ministry of Industry to Bangladesh Army and Bangladesh Army engaged in different productive business scheme to 'make the company profitable; that the Respondent No. 1 is the statutory government authority entrusted with the responsibility of registering and recording keeping of private and public companies, Respondent No. 2 is a private company, limited by shares; that, Respondent No. 3 to 6 are the directors and shareholders of the Respondent No. 2 company; that as part of the business, on 3-11-2013 the Petitioner signed a Memorandum of Agreement with the Respondents No. 3 to establish a poll factory in the BMTF premises and according to the terms of the said agreement, on 10-12-2013, the Petitioner and Respondent No.3 to 6 formed a company called Power Backbones Limited and duly incorporated in the Registrar Joint Stock Companies, Dhaka Annexure-A; that, the company has been formed for producing pre-stretched concrete poles to be supplied mostly in the public sector. That, the Petitioner and the Respondents on 3-11-2013, signed a Memorandum of Understanding, herein referred as `MOU'. That, under the said MOU, Respondents Nos. 3 to 6 should invest 10 (ten) Crore Taka for setting up the said poles factory in the Petitioner's premises in Joyedebpur. The authorized capital of the company is 10,00,00,000 Taka and Respondents No. 3 to 6 holds 85% shares of the company and the Petitioner hold the remaining 15% shares of the company (Annexures-"B and B1"; that, the petitioner then approached the Respondent Nos. 3 to 6 for setting up the factory in the petitioner's premises; that, the Petitioner invested its own money to set up the factory and also purchased all machineries and boiler; that, after the formation of the company Respondent No. 3 was elected as a Chairman and Respondent No. 4 was elected as Managing Director of the Respondent No. 2 Company. That, the Respondent No. 3 and 4 unethically misused the fund of the Respondent No. 2 company account and the Petitioner became highly prejudiced; that, for running the factory, the Respondents Nos. 3 to 6 did not invest any money but unethically withdrawn dividend, salary and other remuneration monthly wise from the company account; that, this stalemate condition created a dispute between the Petitioner and the Respondent No. 3 to 6; that, under this compelling circumstance, the Petitioner formed an inquiry committee to unveil the truth about the misappropriation of the fund by Respondent No. 3 to 6; That, the committee found that, the Respondent No.3 was supposed to pay Taka 5.5 Crore, the Respondent No. 4 was supposed to pay 1.5 Crore, Respondent No.5 to pay 1 Crore and Respondent No. 6 to pay 0.5 Crore. However, Respondent No. 3 actually paid 55 Lac Taka and Respondent No. 4 did not pay any money; that, under the MOA, the Respondent No. 3 was supposed to bear all cost for setting up the factory and also invest for production shade, inspection room, warehouse and commission all the equipment at their own cost and management but the Respondent No. 3 did not invest any money, instead asked for cash loan support from the petitioner and opened L/C by violating the agreement; that, under this compelling circumstance, the petitioner invested Taka 7,69,42,969 for the construction of the company; that, the factory came into operation from April 2015. From April 2015 to October 2015, the factory supplied total 17822 poles to different government departments and during this period total Taka 31,76,62,112 was credited into the account of Respondent No. 2 company, but surprisingly Taka 31,76,56,824.38 was debited from the account; that, the Respondents for their personal gain withdrawn total Taka of 16,25,66,969 under the head of personal payment, dividend, monthly salary, petty cash, remuneration and miscellaneous from the company account; that, the Petitioner asked the Respondent No. 3 to 6 for resigning from the company and also signed Form 117 in this respect. That, on 10.08.2015, the Respondent No. 3 to 6 signed Form 117 and also signed affidavit in this regard Annexure-C Series; that, the respondent No. 3 to 6 sign consent from and thereafter, the Petitioner submitted Form 117 and the affidavit before the Respondent No: 1 for completion of the said share transfer. That, the Respondent No. 3 to 6 did not appear physically before the Respondent No. 1 to complete the said transfer procedure, but on 13-3-2016, Respondent No.3 to 6 made an application before the Respondent No. 1 for not executing the said transfer Annexure -D Series; that it is submitted that the Respondent No. 3 to 6 signed the consent form and also signed the Form 117 with sound knowledge and mind and as such, the said share transfer documents are valid, lawful and legal documents. That, for ulterior motive, the Respondents No. 3 to 6 did not appear before the Respondent No. 1 and as such, this Court should pass an order upon the respondent No.1 for intimation of transfer of shares and update its record and issue its certified copy; that, it is further submitted that Respondent No. 3 to 6 malafidely and with ulterior motive did not appear before Respondent No. 1 and most illegally misused and misappropriated the company fund and as such, the Petitioner has no alternative, but to file this company matter for securing its right and entitlement and as such, this Court should pass an order upon the respondent No.1 for intimation of transfer of shares and update its record and issue its certified copy; that, it is further submitted that Respondent No. 3 to 6 malafidely and with ulterior motive did not appear before Respondent No. 1 and most illegally misused and misappropriated the company fund and as such, the Petitioner has no alternative but to file this company matter for securing its right and entitlement and as such, this Court should pass an order upon the respondent No.1 for intimation of transfer of shares and update its record and issue its certified copy. 

 5. Learned Advocates Mr A SM Shahriar Kabir, Ms Shamima Akther, Ms. Zareen Rahman appeared for the petitioner. He, having placed the petition, first of all submits that the respondent Nos. 3-6 were shareholders of the respondent No. 2 company i.e. Power Backbone Limited (PBL), but they did not make subscription of even one Taka against the shares they have agreed to subscribe by signing theirs names in the Memorandum of Association (MOA). As such, none of the shares registered in the name of the petitioners are paid up shares. However, they are shareholders of PBL because of signing in the MOA. He next submits that the respondent Nos. 3-6, all have executed separate instruments of transfer of share (Form 117) on 10-8-2015, and both the transferor and transferee have executed each share transfer instruments. As such, the learned Advocate proceeds on, the respondent Nos. 3-6 have transferred their one but entire shares to the petitioner BMTF Limited on 10-8-2015 and had transferred one share to the nominee of the petitioner. Moreover, the learned Advocate further submits that, in order to complete the transfer, and to convey title in the said shares, the respondent Nos. 3-6 have handed over the original share certificates to the transferees in respect of total 85,00,000 number of shares held by them. Besides, the board of directors, then including the respondent Nos. 3-6, adopted a resolution on 10-8-2015, whereby the board has unanimously resolved and approved the said transfer of shares and transferor-directors, thereafter having no share (though all unpaid), had tendered resignation by separate letters, vide Annexure-D series to the petition. The learned Advocate continues that, all these documents were placed before the RJSC for the purpose of noting the transfer of shares, but the respondent No. 1 did not record the transfer of said shares in view of the objection placed by the respondent Nos. 3-6, vide a letter dated 11-3-2016 (Annexure-IV to the affidavit-in-opposition). He also submits that the RJSC has no power or authority to refuse the recording of the transfer of shares which have been done and completed upon compliance of all legal formalities as per provisions of section 38 of the Companies Act, 1994. But, the respondent No. 2 company is not rectifying its register of members in respect of 85,00,000 shares, by deleting the names of the respondent Nos. 3-6 and by recording these 85,00,000 numbers of shares in the name of the petitioner and its nominee. He further submits that the petitioner has a clear case to get the relief prayed for and as such, the petition may be allowed. 

 9. I also find that, in order to complete the transfer and to convey title in 85,00,000 shares transferred by the respondent Nos. 3-6, all of them have handed over the original share certificates being Nos. 02 to 05 respectively, to the transferees in respect of total 85,00.000 (eighty five lac shares) held by them in the PBL. 

 18. Hence, based on the evidence and the materials on record, it is found that the petitioner and its nominee has acquired title in 85,00,000 number of shares shown to be held, hereto before by the respondent No. 3 to 6 in the PBL and they have also handed over the original share certificates to the transferees, i.e. to the petitioner and to its nominee Ms. Nasima Ahmed with intent to pass the title in these shares to the transferee as at the time of delivery of the shares certificates. The intention of the respondent Nos. 3-6 to confer title in the transferred shares as on 10-8-2015 is manifest from their acts, conducts and the circumstances of this case. Therefore in exercise of the authority vested in this Court under sub-section (3) of section 43 of the Act, I hold that the petitioner BMTF has acquired title and is owner of 84,99,999 shares in the respondent PBL and that its nominee Major Farhana Akhter, DGM, BMTF has acquired title in and is owner of 1(one) share in PBL, by way of transfer in the manner aforesaid. The respondent Nos. 3-6 have no share in PBL. The Register of members of the respondent No. 1 company shall be rectified accordingly. 

 25. In view of the situation of this case and of the claim and counter claim made by and between the parties and their willingness to refer their rival monetary claims to arbitration tribunal, with reference to the arbitration clause in the MOU dated 19-10-2013 (Annexure-B), the parties may (if the arbitration agreement exists) appoint arbitrator in accordance with the provisions of Arbitration Act, 2001, to decide about their monetary claim and counter claim, if any, not to decide the title, nor the question of legality of transfer of those shares, which are matters falling within the statutory jurisdiction of this Court to decide and, has therefore, been decided by this judgment and order. In this respect I shall refer to the judgment passed by the Supreme Court of India, passed in Special Leave Petition (Civil) 3695 of 1999, between Haryana Telecom Limited vs Sterlite (India) Limited, wherein the Supreme Court of India has held that, "it is not within the competence of the arbitral tribunal to adjudicate and grant any statutory relief". 

 It is, therefore, held and declared that the title to the aforesaid 84,99,999 number of shares belongs to the petitioner and 1(one) share to Ms. Farhana Akhter (DGM, BMTF, at the relevant time) as nominee of the BMTF.

parties:
Jibran (Md) --------- Petitioner (In both the writ petitions)
VS
Bangladesh represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Housing and 
Public Works and others ----- Respondents (In both the writ petitions)
full_judgment:
The petitioner has no locus standi to file this writ petition. His claim that he is a successor of one of the partners of Bangladesh Industries (Previously known as EAST PAKISTAN INDUSTRIES) is yet to be established by an order of a competent court after taking evidence. He has applied for mutation of the plot No. 266, Tejgaon Industrial Area, in the name of alleged successors of partners of Bangladesh Industries. However, he has not produced any power of attorney duly executed by the alleged successors empowering him to apply for mutation on their behalf. The alleged letter head containing the list of successors cannot be taken as succession certificates of alleged successors. The documents produced by the petitioner are in no way can be sufficient proof of title to get the mutation of the said property. Unless and until an undisputed title is established, application for mutation cannot sustain. The Hon'ble High Court Division in exercise of its special original jurisdiction under Article 102 of the constitution cannot declare title in favour of any party relying on highly disputed documents and thus the present writ petition for direction for mutation is not maintainable. 

 17. On the face of the facts and circumstances of the case the title of the petitioner is clouded and not free from dispute and thus the appropriate forum for the petitioner is to seek title in the civil court which has the power to take evidence to resolve disputed question of fact. Once the petitioner will be able to establish his title by way of obtaining a decree from a competent civil court, he will be entitled to get the property mutated in his name. Since there is alternative remedy available under the law the present writ petitions are not maintainable. The issue raised in the instant writ petition is a highly disputed question of fact which cannot be decided under writ jurisdiction of this Division.

parties:
Mst. Roushan Ara and another ------ Appellant
Vs.
Md. Alauddin ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
02. The short facts, for the disposal of this appeal, are that the plaintiff-respondent failed other class Suit No. 135 of 1997 in the court of senior Assistant Judge, sadar, Rajshahi for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession starting, inter alia, that the suit land originally belonged to Adul aziz. S.A khatain No. 810 was pre-pared in his name. He sold the suit land of kazemuddin and other by a registered deed dated 21.01.1963. Kazemuddin got 16 annas shares of the suit land. While he was in possession, R.S. Khaitain No. 395 was correctly prepared in his name. Thereafter, he sold .0350 acre of land from suit plot on 05.10.1983 to one Rabbel Ali who took over possession of the same. The plaintiff purchased .0330 acre by a registered sale deed dated 16.11.1983 from kazemuddin. Rabbel Ali sold .0080 acre of land out of .0350 acre to the plaintiff by a registered deed dated 28.02.1984 and, thus, the plaintiff became owner of .0410 acre of land. He got his name mutated and paid rent to the government. The defendants, claiming title in the suit land, dispossessed him from the same on 15.04.1997 and 22.04.1997. Hence, was the suit. 

 03. The defendant Nos.1 and 2 contested the suit by filling written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint contending that the suit was not maintainable and that the suit land originally belonged to Zamindar Naresh Chandra. One Abdul Aziz was a korfa raiyat under the said Zaminder. In S.A. operation, the suit land was recorded in the name of Abdul Aziz. Thereafter, he sold the same to Kazemuddin by a registered kabala dated 21.01.1963. In revisional settlement operation the suit land and other lands measuring an area of .0812 acre were recorded in the name of said kazemuddin in R.S. Khaitian No. 395. Kazemuddin transferred .0350 acre of land to Rabbel Ali by a registered deed dated 05.10.1983 and, thereafter kazemuddin transferred .330 acre of land to the plaintiff by a registered deed dated 16.11.1983. The plaintiff purchased .0080 acre from the suit plot from Rabbet Ali who received tk.4000/- from kazemuddin and executed and registered a sale deed dated 28.02.1984 to the plaintiff. There was an statement in the recital of the said deed about the reason of transferring the said land to the plaintiff, that was, to adjust .0080 acre of land which kazemuddin failed to hand over possession to the plaintiff earlier. 

 07. Mr. A.J. Mohammad Ali, learned senior Counsel appearing for the appellants, submits that the plaintiff-respondent is entitled to get decree to the extent of .0330 acre of land only in view of the contents of the deed dated 28.02.1984 executed by Rabbel in favour of the plaintiff, the High Court Division erred in law in discharging the Rule. 

 09. It appears from the materials on record that total land appertaining to C.S. khatian No. 891, S.A khatian No. 810, R.S khatian No. 395, S.A. plot No. 4643 is measuring an area of .0812 acre. Admittedly, the said land originally belonged to Kazimuddin. Kazimuddin, on 05.10.1983, transferred .0350 acre of land to Rabbel Ali. Thereafter, he sold .0330 acre of land to plaintiff Alauddin by another sale deed dated 16.11.1983. According to the plaintiff, Robbel Ali sold .0080 acre of land to plaintiff Alauddin by a kabala deed dated 28.02.1984. Thus, the plaintiff acquired title in .0410 acre of land out of the total land of the disputed plot. The plaintiff claimed title in the suit land and prayed for recovery of khas possession in respect of .0080 acre of land out of the total land. 

 13. Since recital of the deed is binding upon the parties to the deed, we are of the view that, in fact, in order to make the title of the plaintiff perfect to the extent of .0330 acre of land out of the total land of the disputed plot, Robbel Ali executed the deed dated 28.02.1984 in respect of .0080 acre of land at the instance of the Kazimuddin, the executants of the kabala deed of the plaintiff dated 16.11.1983. Kazimuddin failed to hand over possession of that .0080 acre of land which is apparent from the recitations of the deed dated 28.02.1984 and for that reason , kazimuddin himself paid consideration of taka 4000/- to Robbel Ali, who in his turn, executed and registered deed dated 24.04.1984 in favour of the plaintiff. 

 14. Thus, the plaintiff has acquired title to the extent of .0330 acre of land (.0330-.0080+.0080) of the disputed plot.

full_judgment:
Md Mozibur Rahman Miah, J: At the instance of plaintiff No. 2, this rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the Judgment and decree dated 7-5-2012 passed by the learned Special District Judge, Faridpur in Title Appeal No. 64 of 2010 dismissing the appeal and affirming the Judgment and decree dated 16-3-2010 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Faridpur in Title Suit No. 264 of 2009 dismissing the suit should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

 The present-petitioner No. 1 and another as plaintiffs originally filed a suit being Title Suit No. 130 of 1989 on 26-7-1989 in the court of learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Faridpur for declaration to the effect that, the registered deeds dated 18-7-1989 and 20-7-1989 executed and registered by the defendant No. 1 in favour of defendants No. 2-6 so mentioned in schedule "Ka and Kha" to the plaint are illegal, void, bassles, false and the same is not binding upon them with a further prayer that, the plaintiffs are entitled to 8 an a share to the land in question by way of partition (buy back) in -the form of preliminary and final decree under section 4 of the Partition Act so had been transferred to the defendants No. 2-6 measuring an area of 12 decimals of land. 

 3. The case of the plaintiffs as has been described in the plaint in short is that, One Sk Shahabuddin originally belonged to 7 decimals of land out of to 32 decimals of land of SA plot No. 29 and 5 decimals of land out of 18 decimals of plot No. 30 in total 12 decimals of land and SA khatian being khatian No. 320 was correctly prepared in his name. During enjoying title and possession over the said properties, Sk Shahabuddin transferred the said 12 decimals of land in favour of Syed Kashem Ali the predecessor of the plaintiffs and defendants No. 1,7,8 by registered kabala dated 19-11-1973 and accordingly he was inducted into possession by the said vendor. After the demise of said Kashem Ali, on 22-1-1978 the plaintiffs and the defendants No. 1, 7 and 8 inherited the same but the said properties were not partitioned through metes and bounds. It has also been stated in the plaint that, before partition, Kashem Ali had been residing in Murshidabad, India and serving in the postal department and after partition he gave option to live in this country and had since been residing in Faridpur. The plaintiff and the defendant No. 8 had been in service at different places of this country before the demise of their father, Syed Kashem Ali while the defendant No 1 along with defendant No. 7 had been residing in the disputed property in Faridpur. After defendant No. 7 got married to one, Syed Nurul Azim, the nephew of Syed Kashem Ali they started living in the suit land. However, in order to maintain the suit properties so left by Syed Kashem Ali, the plaintiff and defendants No, 7 and 9 executed and registered a power of attorney in favour of their mother, the defendant No. 1 on 15-3-1978. After that, the defendant No. 7 being emboldened with the advice of her husband and father-in-law started locking in to bickering with defendant No. 8 on various issues including transfer of 15 decimals of land by the defendant No. 1 in favour of defendant No. 7 and her husband at throw way price on 22-3-1979. For the sake of protecting the paternal property, the plaintiff No. 1 then appeared before the notary public, Dhaka on 7-5-1979 and that of the plaintiff No. 2 as 3-3-1981 respectively and revoked the said power of attorney they had executed and registered on 15-3-1978 and the notice of revocation was duly been served upon the defendant No. 1 that is, the mother 'of the plaintiffs and defendant No. 7 and 9. Subsequently, the defendant No. 1 informed the plaintiffs that, she transferred the suit land to the wife of one, Rais Uddin and the defendant No. 3-6 that is, sons of Rais Uddin. Having been informed, the plaintiff No. 1 then on 23-7-1989 obtained the certified copy of the alleged deeds and came to learn that the suit properties have been transferred in favour of defendants No. 2 and 3-6 in collusion with the husband of the defendant No. 7 and her father-in-law dated 18-7-1989 as well as 20-7-1989 allegedly exerting the authority so have been given through the power of attorney. It has further been stated in the plaint that, by virtue of the alleged deeds the defendants No. 2-6 never acquired any right, title and possession over the said suit property who are mere strangers in the suit land for which the plaintiffs are entitled to get their share in the suit properties on invoking the jurisdiction of section 4 of the Partition Act so left by their father, Syed Mokshed Ali. It has further been stated in the plaint that, the plaintiff No. 2 also revoked the power of attorney on 3-3-1981 which was duly conveyed to his mother, the defendant No. 1 on 6-3-1981 and the defendants No. 2-8 were quite aware of the said revocation and on such assertion, the plaintiff finally prayed for decreeing the suit. 

 4. The defendants No. 1-6 in order to contest the suit though filed a joint written statement but eventually they did not contest the said suit. The present-opposite party No. 1 who was 'defendant No, 7 only contested the said suit by filing a written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that, the husband of the defendant No. 1 that is, her father and that of the plaintiffs, Syed Kashem Ali was the national of Murshidabad, India and after partition he opted for the then east Pakistan and rolled in to this country and stated stayed in Faridpur and before setting for this country, Syed Kashem Ali handed over all his property of Murshidabad in favour of his two sons the defendants No. 8 and the plaintiff No. 2 who has been enjoying the same. It has further been stated that, Syed Kashem Ali had purchased lands in different Mouzas in Faridpur out of which he transferred 14/15 acres of land to defendant No. 1 by way of registered deed and handed over the same to the recipient No. 1 in exchange for paying her dower money. After the demise of Syed Kashem Ali, his successors executed and registered a power of attorney in favour of defendant No. 1 on 15-3-1978 stipulating some terms and -conditions therein. The plaintiffs did never reside in the' suit land and the defendant No. 7 used to take care of her mother. It has further been stated therein the written statement that, earlier the plaintiff No. 1 claimed to have got the suit land from his father for his Wife vide an "Osywatnama" and prayed for probate before the then learned Subordinate Judge, Faridpur without any knowledge the of the defendants No. 1 and 7 which was ultimately dismissed though exparte. The suit properties has duly been transferred in favour of the defendants No. 2-6 by the defendant No. 1 by registered kabalas dated 18-7-89 and 20-7- 1989 within the very knowledge of the plaintiffs and defendant's and the purchasers got possession therein accordingly. The defendant No. 7 subsequently purchased 10 decimals of land out of 12 decimals of land on 6-11-1983 from the defendants No. 2-6 within the knowledge of the plaintiffs and she had also been inducted into possession of the demised property. It has further been stated that, the plaintiffs have got no title and possession over the suit land and, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed with costs. 

 5. In view of the said pleadings, the suit was at first heard by the learned Assistant Judge, and by Judgment and decree dated 6-3-1997 the suit was decreed against the defendant No. 7. Against the said Judgment and decree, the defendant No. 7 then preferred an appeal being Title Appeal No. 33 of1997 and the said appeal was on transferred heard by the learned Additional. District Judge, Faridpur who allowed the same and sent back the case on remand to the trial court by his Judgment and decree dated 12-7-1999. 

 10. Challenging the said Judgment and decree so passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, the present-petitioners as appellants then preferred an appeal being Title Appeal No. 64 of 2010 before the learned District Judge, Faridpur. The said appeal was on transferred heard by the learned Special District Judge, Faridpur. The learned Judge, after hearing the parties to the appeal then dismissed the appeal and thereby affirmed the Judgment and decree so passed by the trial court consequent to dismissed the suit. 

 "Since we brothers and sister almost always remain outside from this place on our respective place of business and service and as we are unable to maintain and look after the property, make, constitute and appoint our widow mother Mst. Ashrafunnessa wife of late Syed kashem Ali of Guhelaxmipur, PO & Dist. Faridpur, our true and lawful attorney, for us, in our name and on our behalf to grant leases upon such terms and conditions and in such manner as she shall think proper in respect of the house and property, which now do or hereafter shall belong to us or wherein were or any person or persons or body or bodied politic or corporate, in trust for us, now have or has or hereafter shall or may have any title or interest whatsoever, or which we hold or shall hereafter hold in trust for any person or persons or body or bodies politic or corporate whomsoever." 

 147. Revocation of powers: A principal desiring to revoke an authenticated power should, if it is available, produce it before the registering officer with an application in order to get it cancelled. The Registering officer should then enter in red ink the words "power revoked, see page of the file of revocation of powers" above the original entry in the register of power of attorney authenticated and also on the power itself, if it is presented with the application. The date and signature of the registering officer should invariably be given in such cases. 

 69. Perhaps, the learned counsel could not comprehend what is the claim of the plaintiffs in the suit. In the instant suit the plaintiffs -plainly claimed title so far as to regards to their respective share in the suit properties so there has been no occasion for the plaintiffs to claim the ownership of the properties so held by the defendant No. 1 herself. That very cited decision is also contrary to the case of the defendant because the plaintiffs Nos. 1 and 2 revoked the power rested upon the Defendant No. 1 so far as regards to their interest in the suit properties concerned not other co-sharer including their sister, defendant No. 7 it held in the suit lands. So in that regard, the agent or the attorney, defendant No. 1 has got no occasion to be prejudiced in respect of her share of land. 

 78. The case of the plaintiff-petitioner No. 1 has been proved. Hence, the plaintiff-petitioner No. 1 is entitled to inherit the property so left by his father, Late Syed Kashem Ali and to get his due share through partition.

3. The plaintiff's case inter-alia is that the plaintiff-respondent-petitioner and defendant-appellant-opposite party No, 1 were married on 9-8-1995 as per Muslim Shariah Law, fixing a dower of Taka 5,00,001 (Take Five lacs and one) only and they have two daughters and a son out of the wedlock. Somehow, a few years after, differences arose between them out of personal matters and at one stage the defendant appellant opposite party stopped giving maintenance to the petitioner and their children from 6-5-2005 and one stage he divorced the petitioner. Following these incidents, the plaintiff filed a suit for declaration being. Title Suit No. 42 of 2006 for declaration inter-alia that the divorce or "Talak" to be false, fictitious, illegal, unlawful, void and not binding upon the petitioner. But the Trial Court rejected the plaint upon hearing both the parties. Against that order the petitioner as appellant filed an appeal before the court of the Learned District Judge Dhaka which was sent to the Court of learned Additional District Judge 7th Court, Dhaka. That after hearing the appeal against rejection of plaint the appeal was allowed on contest against the present opposite party No. 1 and expartee against the rest by setting aside the judgment and decree of TS No, 42 of 2006, dated 21-5-2007 and the Title Suit No. 42 of 2006 was restored to its original number and file and it is still pending in the relevant court for disposal thereof. 

 4. The plaintiff-respondent-petitioner filed Family Case No. 735 of 2006 for trial and maintenance in which learned senior Assistant Judge after hearing both the parties passed the judgment and decree dated 11-2-2009 and declared that the suit be decreed on contest against the opposite party No. 1 and expartee against rest without any cost and ordered that the suit be decreed (Partial) against the defendant No. 1 for dower and for maintenance without any money as to cost and further ordered that from the date of passing of the Decree, the defendant No. 1 shall have to deposit and amount of Taka 2,50,000 (Taka two lacs fifty thousand) only as dower and for maintenance Taka 84,000 (Taka eighty four thousand) only as arrear for the Plaintiff-Petitioner, and maintenance for 3 (three) minor children Taka 2,52,000 (Taka two lacs fifty two thousand) only in total maintenance for Taka (84,000+2,52,000) = 3,36,000 that is total maintenance for Taka 3,36,000 and for dower Taka 2,50,000 —Taka 5,86,000 (Taka five lacs eighty six thousand) only in favour of the plaintiff-petitioner within 40 (forty) days from the date of declaring the decree without fail. The learned trial court in the decree declared that the defendant No. 1, shall have to pay Taka 3,000 (Taka three thousand) only for each month for the plaintiff and for her 3 (three) minor children for each month Taka 9,000 (Taka nine thousand) only that is Taka 12,000 (Twelve thousand) only for 4 (four) persons for every month till the period they are legally entitled. That the learned Court further declared that the defendant No. 1, be directed to pay the money for maintenance to the plaintiff and her children within 10th day of each calendar month and further declared in the decree that this amount of maintenance would be enhanced at the rate 10% at the end of each calendar year. 

 10. He further asserts that whether there was a valid divorce or any divorce at all depends on the outcome of the declaration Title Suit No, 42 of 2006 and therefore the issue of divorce is still pending and not final. He further argues that the modification of the decree by the Appellate Court dated 25-5-2010 of the earlier decree by the learned Assistant Judge 11-2-2009 was erroneously given and erroneously modified by the Appellate Court upon misconception of facts and law and consequently the Rule bears merits and ought to made absolute.
