parties:
Most. Mariam Begum and others ------ Petitioners
Versus
Nuijahan Begum and others ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
Mr. Borhanuddin, J :- This Rule was obtained by the plaintiffs upon making a revisional application under Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure against judgment and decree dated 08.05.2008 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 8th Court, Dhaka, in Title Appeal No. 405 of 2006 affirming those of dated 10.07.2006 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Court, Dhaka, in Title Suit No.451 of 2005 decreeing the suit. 

 2. Facts relevant for disposal of the rule are that plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.79 of 1990, renumbered as Title Suit No.451 of 2005, in the Court of learned Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka, for setting aside preliminary decree dated 05.06.1979 passed in Title Suit No.118 of 1963, renumbered as Title Suit no.20 of 1967, and final decree dated 08.12.1988 signed on 26.01.1989 pursuant to preliminary decree and also for declaration that those are not operative against and binding upon the plaintiffs contending inter alia that plaintiff no.1 Kalu Khan is a non Bengali Bangladeshi who cannot sign his name in Bengali; Said Kalu Khan purchased 5(five) kathas of land from C.S. Plot No.137 under C.S. Khatian no.167 vide registered kabala dated 05.12.1956 and has been residing therein by erecting houses; Plaintiff nos. 2 and 3 purchased 10 decimals of land from Abu Sayed Farajee and Nilufar Begum on 25.02.1971 and residing therein by erecting houses; said Abu Sayed and Nilufar Begum purchased the land on 05.11.1964 from Badrunnessa Chowdhury who purchased the same vide registered kabala dated 20.12.1961 from Anwaruddin Ahmed and Khandker Kamrul Huda; Father of plaintiffs no.4 and 5 Hafez Sarkar purchased 2 gondas of land from C.S. plot no.125 under C.S. Khatian No.167 vide registered kabala dated 19.04.1961 and residing therein by erecting houses; After his expiry, his share devolved upon his wife, three sons and four daughters; Plaintiff no.6 Abdus Sobhan purchased 2 gondas of land from Md. Abdul Hafiz vide registered kabala dated 09.03.1965 from C. S. Plot No.139 and possessing the same through tenants; Abdul Hafiz purchased 5 gondas of land from C. S. Plot No.139 vide registered kabala dated 25.01.1962; on 28.03.1990 defendant no.3 informed plaintiff no. 5 that they obtained decree relating to the lands of plaintiffs; On query through their advocate plaintiffs for the first time came to know about the judgment and decree under challenge and after procuring certified copy of the same filed the suit. 

 3. Defendant Nos. l, 3-7, 21 and 22 contested the suit by filing written statement denying material allegations made in the plaint and contending inter alia that the suit is not maintainable and bad for defect of parties. Further contending that summons of Title Suit no.118 of 1963 were duly served upon all the defendants, some of them contested the suit by filing written statement and some others prayed saham; On the expiry of defendant no. 93 Fazlur Rahman, suit was abated but abatement order was cancelled in Miscellaneous Case No.10 of 1974; Summons of said miscellaneous case also served upon all the opposite parties; Predecessor of defendant nos.16-21 along with five other defendants filed Title Suit No.16 of 1978 against exparte decree; Father of plaintiff nos.4 and 5 i.e Abdul Hafiz, who was impleaded as defendant no.54 in the Title Suit, along with other two filed Miscellaneous Case No.11 of 1978 which was allowed and the exparte decree was set aside; Thereafter, preliminary decree passed on 05.06.1979 in presence of contesting defendants and subsequently final decree drawn up in accordance with law; Plaintiffs of the present suit and their predecessors has/had prior knowledge about preliminary decree and final decree passed in the Title Suit; Present suit filed only to harass the defendants; Suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 6. Being aggrieved, defendants as appellants filed Title Appeal No.451 of 2006 in the Court of learned District Judge, Dhaka. On transfer, said appeal was heard and disposed of by the learned Additional District Judge, 8th Court, Dhaka, who after hearing the parties and reassessing evidence on record disallowed the appeal and thus affirmed findings of the trial court. 

 8. Mr. Abdul Quiyum, learned advocate for the petitioners submits that admittedly plaintiff of original suit no.118 of 1963 Adam Ali was owner of 1/3rd share of the suit land by inheritance and the suit was decreed allowing saham to the plaintiff accordingly as such, appellate court below committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in not holding that plaintiffs are not aggrieved by the impugned judgment and decree. He also submits that appellate court below committed an illegality in not holding that if the summons were not served upon some of the defendants that was mere irregularity which cannot be ground for setting aside a decree under Section 99 of the Code of Civil Procedure. He next submits that the court below committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in not considering that original suit was filed in the year 1963 before promulgation of S. A. and R. S. record as such, mentioning number of unborn S. A. and R. S. khatian relating to suit plots were not possible. He also submits that plaintiff nos. 2, 3, 7-18 are not parties in the original suit and as such allegation of non-service of summons against them is not tenable in the eye of law. He submits that plaintiff nos.1, 4-6 were impleaded as defendants in the original suit as such, burden of proof lies upon them to prove that summons were not served. He lastly submits that appellate court below committed an illegality in not holding that the suit is barred by limitation inasmuch as final decree was drawn up on 28.04.1980 and the present suit filed long after 10 years on 08.04.1990 which is barred under Article 91 and 120 of the Limitation Act as such, impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside. In support of his submissions, learned advocate referred to the case of Ratan Chandra Dey and others-Vs- Jinnator Nahar and others, reported in 13 MLR (AD)168, the case of Bhashani Mondal being dead his heirs; Nanda Rani Mondal and another-Vs- Md. Abdus Stikur and others, reported in 18 BLT(AD)497, the case of Girish Chandra Jana-Vs- Kala Chand Maity, reported in AIR 1957 (Calcatta) 242 and the case of Government of Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Forest, Secretariat Building, Dhaka and others-Vs-Md. Osimuddin, reported in 11 MLR (AD)132. 

 9. On the other hand Mr. Md. Mainul Islam, learned advocate for the opposite parties submits that it is evident from record of the Title Suit that when preliminary decree was passed then the suit was not ready for hearing inasmuch as court below fixed 16.06.1979 for submitting written statement but PW.1 Md. Habibullah examined on 01.06.1979 and preliminary decree passed on 05.06.1979 as such, there is nothing to interfere with the impugned judgment and decree. He also submits that record of the Title Suit shows that PW.1 Md. Habib Ullah did not file any document in support of his deposition. He again submits that both the courts below upon assessing and reassessing evidence on record arrived at a concurrent finding that summon of the original suit was not served upon plaintiff no.1 of the present suit Kalu Khan who was impleaded as defendant no.14 in the original suit inasmuch as Mujibul Huq who allegedly received summon on behalf of Kalu Khan had no manner of relation with said Kalu Khan and defendants of the present suit failed to prove that Mujibul Huq was an agent of Kalu Khan. He next submits that plaintiffs having impeached the decree passed in earlier suit on ground of collusion and fraud on the assertion that they are owners in possession of the suit land, they are not required to seek any further relief to their main relief of declaration. He submits that once an amendment is allowed, said amendment relates back to the date of institution of the suit. He lastly submits that there is no question of limitation when it is proved that summons were fraudulently suppressed and limitation will run from the date when the fraud was detected. In support of his contention, learned advocate referred to the case of Abdus Sukur (Md) and others-Vs- Bhasani Mandal' and another, reported in 53 DLR 452, the case of Doon Valley Rice Limited-Vs-MV Yue Yang and others, reported in 48 DLR 531 and the case of Abul Khair Mia-Vs- Abdul Latif Sarder, reported in 32 DLR (AD) 167. 

 10. Mr. A. K. M. Rezaul Karim, learned advocate for the opposite party No.22 by adopting submissions of Mr. Md. Mainul Islam add that plaintiffs of Title Suit no.118 of 1963 obtained the decree by suppressing summons and this finding of fact has been arrived at both by the trial court and appellate court below which is not revisable in this jurisdiction. He again submits that the finding of fact arrived at by the appellate court below which is the last court of fact that summons were fraudulently suppressed. He also relied upon the case reported in 32 DLR (AD) 167. 

 11. Heard the learned advocates Perused revisional application, judgment of the courts below along with lower courts record of the present suit and Title Suit No.118 of 1963 and decisions cited by the learned Advocates. 

 12. Main contention of the plaintiffs in the present suit are that preliminary decree and final decree obtained in Title Suit No.118 of 1963 by suppressing summons fraudulently and also that at the time of passing preliminary decree, original suit was not ready for hearing. Relevant orders from order sheet of Title Suit no.118 of 1963 are reproduced below: "Order no.289 dated 31.5.79: Pltff. and the defdt. nos. 89, 91, 24, 101, 104 and some added defdts. file hajiras. One Gaznafar Ali Chowdhury and two others and one Manjur Murshed Waliur Rahman and two others (all are minors) file two petitioners under order I rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure with a prayer to add them as defendants in this suit on the ground stated in the petition. Copy served upon the pltff. Put up tomorrow for orders. 

 Order no.295 dated 5.6.79: Case is proved. C. F. paid is correct. Hence, Ordered that the suit be decreed in preliminary form on admission with cost against defdt. nos.7, 16(Ka) 16(gha), 18, 26, 46, 95-96, 97, 98-100, 101, 104, 105, 111- 113, who do get their saham as prayed for and exparte against the rest with cost. Plaintiffs do get a saham of 1/3rd share in "C" schedule land. Parties may effect partition amicably within 60 days from today, failing which plaintiffs are entitled to get their saham separated by metes and bounds through court, by appointment of commissioner, who, if appointed and commissioned, is to respect possession and convenience and transfers of by respective parties so far as practicable." From the above orders, it appears that vide order no.290 dated 01.06.1979 though trial court fixed 16.06.1979 for written statement but on the same date i.e. 01.06.79 examined PW.1 Habibullah vide order no. 294. More interesting is that suit decreed on 05.06.1979 though 16.06.79 fixed for written statement. From the above quoted orders it is evident that when preliminary decree passed, suit was not ready for hearing. So, I cannot disagree with finding of the appellate court below that decree was not passed in accordance with law. On perusal of the order sheet, I find that some of the orders i.e. from order no. 247-253 are missing from the record. 

 13. On perusal of the record, it appears both the courts below arrived at a concurrent finding that summon was not served upon plaintiff no.1 Kalu Khan inasmuch as Mujibul Huq who allegedly received summon on behalf of Kalu Khan was not his agent and defendants failed to prove that he had any manner of relationship with Kalu Khan. From the plaint of present suit it also appears that owners of lands namely Anwaruddin Ahmed and Khandker Kamrul Huda who purchased the land on 18.03.1953 and sold the same to Badrunnessa Chowdhury vide kabala dated 20.12.1961 who on her turn sold the land to vendor of plaintiffs no. 2 and 3 were not made party in the original suit. It is also stated in the plaint that predecessor of plaintiff nos. 4 and 5 Abdul Hafiz Sarker purchased the land on 19.04.1961 but he was not made party in the original suit though one Howfader Abdul Hafez Sarker without mentioning father's name impleaded in the original suit as defendant no. 54. Order V of the Code of Civil Procedure deals with the issue and service of summons. 

 14. Finding of facts arrived at by the appellate court below as the last court of fact that summons were suppressed and decree obtained in the original suit fraudulently and collusively are not perverse and based on evidence on record. It is settled that once fraud is established, limitation will run from the date when it was detected. 

 15. It is not clear from the order sheet of Title Suit no.118 of 1963 whether Md. Habibullah who deposed as PW. 1 submitted documents in support of his testimony. Learned Advocate for the petitioners submitted that the plaintiffs of the present suit are not aggrieved by the judgment and decree of the previous suit inasmuch as plaintiff of the original suit allowed saham in respect of 1/31.4 share as claimed by him as C.S. recorded tenant but on perusal of the plaint of Title Suit it appears that contentions of the plaintiff in the suit could be reverted by the defendants by filing written statement and adducing evidence if summons were duly served upon them as such, submission of the learned advocate does not hold water in the present context. 

 16. Under the facts and circumstances of the case and for the reasons stated above, I am of the view that preliminary decree passed in the Title suit when suit was not ready for hearing as such, preliminary decree and subsequent final decree were not passed in accordance with law and summons of the Title Suit no.118 of 1963 were fraudulently suppressed as such, question of limitation does not arise. Furthermore, plaintiff of the Title suit obtained preliminary and final decree without impleading the persons who owned and possessed suit land before institution of Title suit. 

 17. In the present suit, plaintiffs impeached preliminary decree and final decree passed in Title Suit no.118 of 1963 on ground of collusion and fraud on the assertion that they are owners in possession of their portion in the suit land before institution of the Title Suit in the year 1963. 18. Both the courts below found that the plaintiffs are in possession in their portion of the suit land and the predecessor of the defendants obtained the decree collusively and fraudulently. In such view of the matter, plaintiffs are not required to seek any other relief as 'further relief' to their main relief of declaration. 

 21. Impugned judgment and decree dated 08.05.2008 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 8th Court, Dhaka, in Title Appeal No.406 of 2006 is maintained. 

 23. Accordingly, Title Suit No.118 of 1963, renumbered as Title Suit No.69 of 1986, is restored. Court concern is directed to dispose of the suit as soon as possible preferably within 1(one) year from the date of receipt of this judgment. 

 24. It is pertinent to mention here that disposal of the Title Suit should be confined within the present parties without allowing any further application for addition of party, otherwise it will be an unending process.

parties:
Md. Assruddin Biswas and others ------ Appellants
Vs.
Md. Sarfaraj and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Hasan Foez Siddique, J. This appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 15.08.2005 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3362 of 2002 making the Rule absolute affirming the judgment and decree dated 27.05.2002 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Jhenaidah in Title Appeal No. 136 of 1992 reversing those dated 24.02.1992 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Jhenaidah in Title Suit No. 26 of 1986. The short facts, for the disposal of this appeal, are that the appellants as plaintiffs instituted the aforesaid suit for declaration of their title and confirmation of possession stating, inter alia, that the land appertaining to C.S. Khatian No. 50 originally belonged to Nabai Biswas under the landlord Hare Krishna Saha and others. Nabai Biswas died leaving three sons, the plaintiffs No. 1 and 2 and Nasoruddin and wife Kali Bibi, Kali Bibi died leaving his aforesaid three sons. Nasoruddin died leaving three sons, the plaintiff Nos. 3-5 and wife plaintiff No. 6. The plaintiff No. 1 transferred some lands from his share to plaintiff Nos. 2 and 3-6 in different dates. The plaintiff No. 2 sold some land to defendant Nos. 8 and 9. The plaintiff No. 2, constructing dwelling homestead in the land of Plot No. 1383, has been living therein. The plaintiff No. 1 has been living in different village. The plaintiff Nos. 3-6, constructing dwelling homestead in non-suited land, have been living therein. There was graveyard of Nasruddin and his parent in the land of Plot No. 1128. On 5th Kartick, 1390 the defendants denied the plaintiffs, title in the suit land stating that the Khatian had been prepared in their names. Hence, was the suit. 

 2. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 contested the suit contending that the suit was barred by limitation and also barred by provision of res-judicata. They further contended that though the suit land was recorded in the name of Nabai Biswas in Khatian No. 50 but his father Darshan Biswas was the original owner of the said land who died leaving his son Nabai Biswas and daughter Mandu Bibi. The rent receiving interest of the property, in question, was acquired by Ramani Kanta from Hare Krishna and others who instituted Certificate Case Nos. 95/1937-38 and took over possession of the suit land. Ahad Mondal and Kali Bibi took settlement from Ramani Kanta. Kali Bibi died leaving three sons the plaintiff Nos. 1 and 2 and Nasoruddin, predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiff Nos. 3-6. Ahad Mondal died leaving his wife Kumari Bibi, son Kamor Uddin and daughters Safura and Jahura. Kamar Uddin died leaving his mother Kumari Bibi, two sisters Safura and Jahura and two cousins Jobed Ali and Hosen Ali. Jobed Ali died leaving his brother Hosen Ali. Kumari Bibi herself and on behalf of her two minors daughters sold their shares to the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 by sale deed dated 08.05.1950. The plaintiff Nos. 1 and 2 and Nasoruddin took patta settlement from Safura and Jahura on 29.03.1952. Safura and Jahura, after attaining majority transferred their shares to Ekar Uddin Biswas and Rabbani Mondal by a deed dated 24.02.1956 who transferred the said land to defendant Nos. 1 and 2 by the deed dated 26.06.1957 and 04.05.1960. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 have been possessing the suit land. 

 5. Mr. Siddique submits that the High Court Division, without reversing findings arrived at by the last court of facts as to title and possession, erroneously set aside the well reasoned judgment. 

 7. In considering the principle of res-judicata he wrongly discussed the earlier Title Suit No. 52 of 1966 on the same suit property with the instant title suit on considering the facts and circumstances of the case. I am of the opinion that this rule has merit."

2. Facts of the case, in brief, are that the predecessor of petitioner No. 1 Md. Soleman Ali Akand and petitioner No. 2 and opposite party Nos. 4-7 as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 46 of 1989 in the First Court of Joint District Judge, Natore, for declaration of title in the suit land stating, inter alia, that the suit land originally belonged to Jagat Sundori Debbya and Sharat Chandra Chowdhury. Said Sharat Chandra Chowdhury died leaving Jagadis Chandra Chowdhury who transferred the suit land in favour of Bhojohory Sarker by pattan nama. Said Bhojohory Sacker died leaving three sons, namely Puma Orang, Boda Orang and Pocha Orang. Puma Orang sold his share by registered kabala in favour of Abu Sayeed, who sold the same vide registered deed dated 24.10.1978 in favour of Abdul Kader. Abdul Kader sold some portion of his share to Aitan Bibi. Thereafter, Aitan Bibi sold her share to Samad Sarker. Puma Orang also sold his share to Soleman Ali Akand and Jainal Abedin Akand. Boda Orang also sold his share to Solaiman and Jainal Abedin Akan, Pocha Orang also sold his share by registered kabala deed dated on 22.08.1972 in favour of Jamal Uddin and the said Jamal Uddin sold one part of his share to Abdus Satter. In this way the plaintiffs inherited the suit land and have been possessing the same constructing but in a part of the suit land. In 1395 B.S. the plaintiffs came to know that R.S. Khatian was wrongly published in the name of the defendant, Government of Bangladesh and hence the suit. 

 5. Against the said judgment and decree passed by the trial Court defendant Nos. 7-9 preferred Title Appeal No. 82 of 2003 before the Court of District Judge, Natore. Eventually, the case was transferred to the Court of Additional District Judge, Natore, who upon hearing the parties and considering the materials on record, allowed the appeal setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court. 

 10. The High Court Division observed that the plaintiffs did not file their documents of title and, thereby, failed to prove their title and possession over the suit land. It was further observed upon perusal of the L.C.R that the plaintiffs produced a copy of the C.S. Khatian No. 256 as Exhibit- 1, but the suit land is of C.S. Khatian No. 258 and no other documents were exhibited by the plaintiffs although reference was made in the plaint to a Pattannama and various kabala deeds. The High Court Division held that as the plaintiffs failed to produce the documents in support of their alleged title to the suit land, it must be held that the suit land is the khas land of the Government as per the admitted S.A. and R.S. record. As such the High Court Division disregarded the admission of D.W. 2 with reference to possession by the plaintiffs. 

 11. We find from the judgment of the appellate Court that the claim by the plaintiffs is that they took pattan from the C.S. tenant Brojo Hori, but they could not produce any document to substantiate their claim. Although the appellate Court did not advert to the admission of D.W. 2 with regard to possession of the suit land by the plaintiffs, the High Court Division observed that in the absence of any evidence as to how the plaintiffs got title to the suit land and considering the fact that the S.A. and R.S. records are in the name of the Government, the admission by D.W. 2 regarding possession by the plaintiffs is of no help to the plaintiffs.

full_judgment:
2. Facts of the case, in brief, are that one Pran Bollav Sarker as plaintiff filed Title suit No. 143 of 1969 in the First Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka, praying for declaration of title and further declaration that the ex parte decree dated 13.09.1967 passed by the same Court in Title Suit No. 166 of 1966 is void, illegal, fraudulent, inoperative and has no legal effect. 

 3. The case of the plaintiff was that he owned and possessed 16 annas share comprising an area of 1.73 acres of land of Mouja Dania and 0.30 acre of land of Mouja Matuail by way of inheritance and by purchase. One Md. Tayab Ali, the original defendant, on the basis of an agreement for sale obtaining an arbitration award instituted Title Suit No. 166 of 1966 in the First Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka and obtained an ex parte decree. Subsequently, he filed Title Execution Case No. 57 of 1967 procuring a forged Vokalatmana in the name of Pran Bollav Sarker and collusively sup-pressing all process of this suit obtained an order of attachment of the suit land on 19.04.1969. Hence, the plaintiff filed the instant suit. 

 4. Defendant No. 1 filed a written statement denying the statements in the plaint, contending, inter alia, that the plaintiff entered into an agreement with Md. Tayab Ali and a dispute arose whereupon an arbitration was held which ended in an award. The award was placed before the Court in Title Suit No. 166 of 1966. Pran Ballav appeared by filing a Vokalatnama. The case was thereafter transferred to the Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka. During pendency of the suit, by a registered kabala No. 4183 dated 01.03.1971, one Md. Imam Uddin, the predecessor of respondent Nos. 1-8 purchased the entire suit land and got himself impleaded as plaintiff No. 2 in the suit. 

 5. The suit proceeded and the trial court fixed 20.02.2001 for arguments and, thereafter, decreed the suit in part declaring the ex parte decree dated 13.09.1967 passed in Title Suit No. 166 of 1966 as not binding upon the plaintiff and refused the prayer for declaration of the right, title and interest of plaintiff No. 2 in the suit land on the ground of his failure to produce the deed of purchase dated 01.03.1971. 

 6. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and decree Md. Imam Uddin filed Title Appeal No. 202 of 2001, renumbered as Title Appeal No. 1 of 2005. Sharafat Ali the defendant No. 9 and Harun-Or-Rashid predecessor of the petitioners herein filed Title Appeal No. 160 of 2001, renumbered as Title Appeal No.1 of 2004 before the District Judge, Dhaka. The learned District Judge transferred both the appeals to the Court of Jananirapatta Bighnakari Oparadh Daman Tribunal for disposal. 

 7. On 15.05.2007 the said Imam Uddin filed an application in Title Appeal No. 1 of 2005 for producing the aforesaid sale deed dated 01.03.1971 as additional evidence whereupon the defendant raised objection in writing and on hearing both the parties the appellate Court rejected the application for production of additional evidence by order dated 18.01.2010. 

 13. Having perused the evidence and materials on record, we note that the basis of claim of the added plaintiff is the document of the year 1971. Without such evidence the plaintiff will not be able to establish the genealogy and his claim to title in the property.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 3218 of 2014
parties:
Mossammat Anjuman Ara Begum and others ------ Petitioners.
Vs.
Md. Abul Hossain and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Abdul Wahhab Miah, J. This petition for leave to appeal at the instant of the defendants has been filed against the judgment and decree dated the 20th day of May, 2014 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 7 of 2012 dismissing the same. Facts essential for disposal of this petition are that respondent Nos. 1-5 as the plaintiffs filed Title suit No. 163 of 2005 in the Court of Joint District Judge, First Court, Dhaka for declaration that the preliminary decree dated 03.05.2000 and the final decree dated 23.11.2000 passed by the learned Subordinate judge, First Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 254 of 1996 were void. The main allegation in the plaint for declaring the said decrees void was that the decrees were obtained by the plaintiffs by suppressing the summonses of the suit upon the defendants. 

 2. The suit was contested by the defendants, i.e. the plaintiffs of Title suit No. 254 of 1996 by filing written statement contending that the summonses of the suit were duly served upon the defendants, but since they did not appear, the suit was decreed ex-parte. 

 6. From the judgment and decree of the trial Court, it appears that it set aside the decree of Title Suit No. 254 of 1996 on the clear finding that summonses of the suit were not served upon the defendants of that suit, i.e. the plaintiffs of the instant suit. The High Court Division being the last Court of fact also affirmed the said finding of fact of the trial Court. 

 7. Mr. Bivash Chandra Biswas could not also show from the record that the finding of fact arrived at by the trial Court and affirmed by the High Court Division is the result of gross misreading of the evidence on record or otherwise perverse Therefore, we find no ground to interfere with the impugned judgment and decree of the High Court Division. However, neither the trial Court nor the High Court Division gave any direction to proceed with the suit in accordance with law. With the setting aside of the decrees passed in Title Suit No. 254 of 1996, the suit has been restored to its original position, so it should be proceeded with and disposed of in accordance with law and accordingly, the trial Court is directed to proceed with Title Suit No. 254 of 1996 and dispose of the same in accordance with law. The ordering portion of the judgment and the decree of the trial Court stands modified accordingly.

Mr. A.K.M. Abdul Hakim, J. :- These three Rules were issued in Civil Revision No.4082 of 2004, Civil Revision No.4092 of 2004 and Civil Revision No.07 of 2005 at the instance of defendant Nos.2-10 of Title Suit No.85 of 1993 (plaintiffs of Title Sun No.69 of 1993) and defendant Nos.1-6 of Title Suit No.69 of 1993 (plaintiffs of Title Suit No.85 of 1993) and defendant Nos.l4, 15 and 17 of Title Suit No.69 of 1993 respectively, directed against one and same judgment and decree dated 17.07.2004 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Additional Court, Sylhet in Title Appeal No.55 of 1997 (heard analogously with Title Appeal Nos.64 and 65 of 1997) dismissing the appeals and reversing the judgment and decree dated 30.01.1997 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge. Additional Court, Sadar, Sylhet in Title Suit No.69 of 1993 and Title Suit No.85 of 1993. 

 3. The opposite party Nos.1-6 as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.284 of 1986 in the 

 Court of Sadar Munsif, First Court, Sylhet on 20.09.1986 for partition of the suit property claiming an area of 0.11 acres land impleading the present petitioners as defendant Nos.2-10 and other defendants. Subsequently, the said suit transferred to the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Additional Court, Sadar, Sylhet and renumbered as Title Suit No.85 of 1993. 

 4. The defendant Nos.2-10 of Title Suit No.284 of 1986 as plaintiffs instituted Title 

 Suit No.261 of 1986 on 21.12.1986 for partition in respect of 0.15 acres of and against the plaintiffs of Title Suit No.284 of 1986 in the Second Court of Sub-Judge, Sylhet. The suit was renumbered as Title Suit No.69 of 1993 of the same Court. 

 5. Plaintiffs case of Title Suit No.85 of 1993 in short, are that suit land measuring 1 

 plaint originally belonged to Morium Nessa Chowdhurani, the predecessors of the defendant Nos.16 and 17. She settled 1 Powa, 4 Jashti equivalent to 0.1177 acres out of schedule I land to Bosai Mia predecessor of the plaintiffs and Swab Mia, the predecessor of the defendant Nos.18 and 19 by Hukumnama dated 1 Srabon, 1320 B.S.; that Bosai Mia died leaving the plaintiffs and Swab Mia who subsequently died leaving defendant Nos. 18 and 19; that Bosai Mia during his life time and after his death his heirs have been possessing the schedule-3 of the suit property on payment of rents to Monirunnessa Chowdhurani: who died subsequently leaving two daughters (1) Mahebbadon Chowdhurani, defendant No.16 and (2) Helalbadon Chowdhirani, Vs. Marad 

 heirs of Bosai Mia; that defendant Nos.l-6 of Title Suit No.69 of 1993 (plaintiffs of Title Suit No.85 of 1993) in their written statement stated that Abul and Amar Chand filed Objection Case No.1860 of 1961 under Section 19(1) of the SAT Act which was dismissed. The plaintiffs are in ejamli possession, since they are possessing less share they claimed partition of their share of 

 0.11 acres in the schedule 3 of the suit land requested the defendants to partition of their share in the schedule land but they refused to do so. Thus the plaintiffs were compelled to file the present suit for partition. The defendant Nos.2-10 and the plaintiffs of Title Suit No.69 of 1993 have no right, title and interest in the suit land. 

 7. Defendant Nos.2- 10 of Title Suit No.85 of 1993 contested the said suit by filing joint 

 written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that the schedule I land belonged to Monirunnessa Chowdhurani. She settled 0.30 acres of land out of schedule I by a registered Kabuliyat dated 4' Magh, 1328 B.S. to (I) Sk. Abdul and (2) Rahim Box; that Abdul died leaving three sons namely, Lal Mia, Reaz Mia and Siraj Mia. Lal Mia died leaving three sons defendant Nos.3-5, four daughters defendant Nos.6-9 and wife defendant No.10; that Siraj Mia died unmarried, so, his shares devolved upon the defendant Nos.2-10. These defendants claimed that the alleged Hukumnama of the plaintiff dated 1 Srabon, 1320 B.S. is fictitious and the predecessor of the defendants had no knowledge about the Objection Case No.990 of 1961 under Section 19(1) of the SAT Act. Accordingly, the defendant Nos.2-10 claimed separate saham 0.15 acres of land out of schedule I. During last settlement operation part of the suit land was wrongly recorded in the name of the defendant's predecessor and since there is no partition between the plaintiffs and defendants, now they are claiming partition by filing Title Suit No.69 of 1993. 

 8. Defendant Nos.16 and 17 of Title Suit No.85 of 1993 and defendant Nos.I2 and 13 of Title Suit No.69 of 1993 are same. Their positive case is that their mother -Monirunnessa settled the schedule 3 land to predecessor of plaintiffs Bosai Mia. These defendants denied right, title and interest of the defendant Nos.2-I5. Defendant Nos.2-I5 were given yearly lease by Monirunnessa Chowdhurani and since they failed to pay rents accordingly they were evicted and possession taken by the lessor Monirunnessa Chowdhurani. These defendants are claiming saham of 0.17 acres in the suit land. 

 9. Heirs of Suratunnessa defendant Nos.I2 and 15 of Title Suit No.85 of 1993 and also defendant Nos.9 and 10 of Title Suit No.69 of 1993 in their written statement stated that the Monirunnessa Chowdhurani settled 0.0425 acres of land out of schedule I in favour of Suratunnessa mother of the defendant Nos.11-15 in the latter part of 1948 and they have been possessing the same by constructing huts. Their further case is that the predecessor of the defendant Nos.2-10 were evicted from their land as they failed to pay rent. So, the defendants are entitled to get separate saham for an area of 0.0425 acres of land in the suit land. Defendant Nos.I4, 15 and 17 of Title Suit No.69 of 1993 contested the suit by filing joint written statements claiming that their predecessor Rahim Box and the predecessor of the plaintiffs jointly look settlement of 0.30 acres of land by erecting their habitual huts thereon and they also claimed separate saham for an area of 0.15 acres of land in the suit land. 

 12. The trial Court on consideration of the evidence and materials on record decreed the Title Suit No.85 of 1993 in part and also decreed the Title Suit No.69 of 1993 in part by a single judgment dated 30.01.1997 allotting saham to Murad Mia and other plaintiffs of Title Suit No.85 of 1993 and defendant Nos.l-6 of Title Suit No.69 of -1993 share of 0.0425 acres out of 0.11 acres and decreed the Title Suit No.69 of 1993 in part allotting a saham of 0.0850 to plaintiff of Title Suit No.69 of 1993 and defendant Nos.2-10 of Title Suit No.85 of 1993. Further allotted 0.0425 acres to the heirs of Suratunnessa, defendant Nos.11-15 in Title Suit No.85 of 1993 defendant Nos.9 and 10 of Title Suit No.69 of 1993 and also allotted saham 0.17 acres to Jamindar, Monirunnessa Chowdhurani, predecessor of defendant Nos. 16(Ka) and 1 6(Kha) in Title Suit No.85 of 1993 and defendant Nos.I2(Ka) and 12(Kha) in Title Suit No.69 of 1993. Against the aforesaid judgment and decree Vs. Mend Mia & Ors (A.K.M. Abdul Hakii..11435 of the trial Court defendant Nos.2-10 of Title Suit No.85 of 1993 preferred Title Appeal No.64 of 1997, plaintiffs of Title Suit No.69 of 1993 preferred Title Appeal No.55 of 1997, defendant Nos.I4, 15 and 17 of Title Suit No.69 of 1993 preferred Title Appeal No.65 of 1997 before the learned District Judge, Sylhet. 

 13. It may be noted that no appeal was filed by the plaintiffs, Murad Mia and others against the part decree passed in Title Suit No.85 of 1993. Subsequently, all the appeals were transferred to the Court of Joint District Judge, Additional Court. Sylhet who upon considering the evidence and materials on record, finding and decisions of the trial Court dismissed all the appeals and decree the Title Suit No.85 of 1993 allotting saham of 0.11 acres in favour of the plaintiffs Murad Mia and others by judgment and decree dated 17.07.2004. 

 14. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree dated 17.07.2004 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Additional Court, Sylhet defendant Nos.2- 10 of Title Suit No.85 of 1993 filed Civil Revision No.4082 of 2004 and plaintiffs of Title Suit No.69 of 1993 filed Civil Revision No.4092 of 2004 and defendant Nos-14, 15 and 17 of Title Suit No.69 of 1993 filed Civil Revision No.07 of 2005 and obtained the present rules and stay. 

 17. Mr. Golam Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing in 4082 of 2004 for defendant petitioners and 4092 of 2004 for the plaintiff petitioners submits that both the Courts below committed gross error of law in not allotting saham in their favour on the basis of the registered Kabuliyat. He further submits that both the Courts below failed to consider the local investigation report which was proved by the Advocate Commissioner and in the report it was found that the suit land is identical with the kabuliyat land and the petitioners predecessor are in physical possession of the said land. He next submits that the trial Court rightly found the unregistered Hukumnama cannot be the document of title and possession and considered the Hukumnama as forged one but the appellate Court erroneously enhanced the share of the opposite party plaintiffs of Title Suit No.85 of 1993 without considering the aforesaid aspect as found by the trial Court. He also submits that the appellate Court erroneously allotted the entire saham of 0.11 acres of land in favour of the plaintiffs in Title Suit No.85 of 1993 and failed to consider the fact that they did not prefer any appeal against the part decree allotting a saham of 0.0425 acres of land. He finally submits that the judgment of the appellate Court is not a proper judgment of reversal and accordingly prayed that the rules should be made absolute. In support of his submissions Mr. Golam Ahmed cited the decisions reported in 17 BLD (AD)36, 12 BLD(AD)203 (1992), 47 DLR (AD) 163. 

 18. It appears that the Civil Revision No.07 of 2005 was originally filed by the learned Advocate Mr. Osman Gani and subsequently Mr. Golam Ahmed filed fresh power on behalf of the petitioners. At the time of hearing of the revisional application he submits that due to bonafide mistake he filed power on behalf of the petitioners. Subsequently, he issued no objection certificate and Ms. Rani Akhter filed fresh power on 06.04.2015. At the time of hearing, she supported the submissions advanced by the learned Advocate for the petitioners in Civil Revision No.4082 of 2004. 

 19. Mr. Md. Delwar Hossein, the learned Advocate with Ms. Salma Begum, Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party Nos.I-2(a)-2(e), 3-6 in Civil Revision No.4082 of 2004, opposite party Nos.1, 2(a)-2(e), 3-6 in Civil Revision No.4092 of 2004 and opposite party Nos.I5, 16(a)-10(e), 17-20 in Civil Revision No.07 of 2005 submits that the appellate Court after considering the oral and documentary evidence on record rightly reversed the findings of the trial Court and as such the judgment passed by the appellate Court is a proper judgment of reversal. Learned Advocate by referring paragraph No.7(Kha) of the written statement filed by the defendant Nos.I6 and 17 heirs of Zamindars submits that in their written statement they clearly admitted that their mother Monirunnessa Chowdhurani settled of I Powa, 4 Jashti equivalent to 0.11 acres land to Bosai Mia, predecessor of present plaintiffs to Title Suit No.85 of 1993 by a Hukumnama dated l' Sraban, 1320 B.S. and this fact of possession was also admitted by DW.I Rear. Mia. DW.2 Yusuf for defendant Nos.2-10 and Salina Khatun, DW.I for defendant No.15, Dewan Ferdous Ahmed, DW.I who deposed on behalf of the defendant Nos.16(Ka) and 16(Kha) also admit the same. Since this facts of possession and settlement by the Zamindar in favour of the predecessor of the plaintiffs are admitted by the Zamindar, the same need not required to be proved tinder Section 58 of the Evidence Act. In this respect learned Advocate refers the case of Nurul Islam Vs Jamila Khatun and others reported in  53 DLR (AD) 45. He further submits that since the predecessor of the defendants Nos.16 and 17 admitted the settlement of 0.11 acres of land to Bosai Mia predecessor of the plaintiffs by Hukumnama and their possession thereon and accordingly the plaintiffs predecessor paid rent to the Zamindar. So, the allegation as raised by the defendants that Hukumnama and rent receipts are forged does not arise at all. In reply to the submission made by the learned Advocate for the petitioners since Hukumnama is a unregistered document and not marked as Exhibit. But the Court considered this as evidence and marked as 'X' but the defendants did not take any step to prove that the same is forged one. In this connection Mr. Delwar cited a decision reported in 2 MLR (AD) 291. The learned Advocate for the petitioners vehemently submits that the trial Court on the basis of S.A. Khatian rightly allotted saharn for 0.0850 acres to the defendant Nos.2-10 of Title Suit No.85 of 1993 and plaintiffs of Title Suit No.69 of 1993. In reply Mr. Delwar for the opposite party submits that the record of right is not a document of title. It does not create or extinguish title to land. He submits that the S.A. Khatian clearly shows the name of the plaintiffs predecessor Bosai Mia was recorded for 0.0425 acres of land in less share. Thus for non recording entire share claimed by the plaintiffs on the basis of the settlement of 0.1177 acres by Zamindar in favour of the plaintiffs predecessor Bosai Mia and subsequently payment of rent exhibit-2 series does not extinguished their right, title in the suit land. In this connection learned Advocate refers case of Lal Mia being dead his heirs Vs. Haji Md. Ibrahim Mia and others reported in 28 DLR(AD) 61. The learned Advocate for the opposite parties by referring Order XLI. rule 33 of the Code of Civil Procedure submits that non filing of appeal by the plaintiffs of Title Suit No.85 of 1993 against the part decree passed in that suit for an area of 0.0425 acres, yet the appellate Court has jurisdiction to pass proper Order in the appeal filed by the defendants. In this respect the learned Advocate for the opposite parties refers the decision reported in 37 DLR (AD) 63 and 3 BLC 131. He lastly submits that finding of fact whether concurrent or not arrived at by the lower appellate Court is binding upon the High Court Division except in certain well defined circumstances. 

 20. Ms. Shirin Akhter Chowdhury, learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party Nos.I7- 19, 21-26 and 28-33 submits that the predecessor of these defendants, Monirun Nessa settled the schedule suit land to the plaintiffs predecessors, Bosai Mia and these defendants denied right, title and interest of defendant Nos.2-15. She further submits their predecessor gave yearly lease to the predecessor of defendant Nos.2-15 but for non payment of rent they were evicted and possession was taken back by the Zamindar, lessor Monirum Nesa. She finally submits that both the Courts below rightly gave saham of 0.17 acres in the suit land in favour of these defendants. 

 21. It appears that regarding settlement of land by Zamindar to the predecessor of the plaintiff Bosai Mia defendant Nos.16-17 in Title Suit No.85 of 1993 they categorically admitted settlement of 0.11 acres of schedule Ill land in paragraph No.7(Kha) of their written statement, which reads as under: উত্তর দায়ক ১৬/১৭ নং বিবাদীগণের মাতা জনাবা মুনীরুননেছা চৌধুরানী নালিশী ভূমিসহ অপরাপর ভূম্যাদি পূর্ববত মৌরসী মালিক সূত্রে ভোগ দখল করিতে থাকাবস্থায় বাদীগণের পূববর্তী বছই মিয়া খাজনাই প্রজা হিসাবে নালিশী ভূমির উত্তর পশ্চিমাংশে বাদীগণের আরজীর ১ম তপশীল মোট মোং ১/৪/এক কেদার এক পোয়া চারি যষ্টি ছয় পন ভূ্ম্যাদির মধ্যে দক্ষিণ পূবাংশে/১ কেদার ভূমি ব্যতিত অবশিষ্ট ভূমি জোত বন্দোবস্ত প্রাপ্ত ক্রমে ভোগ দখল করিতে থাকেন।” which clearly proved that these defendants categorically denied the right. title and interest of the defendant Nos.2-10. Although the learned Advocate for the defendant Nos.2-10 tried to submit that this settlement through Hukumnama is unregistered one and challenged the genuineness of the Hukumnama being forged, fraudulent and collusive one. But they failed to prove by producing any reliable evidence that alleged Hukumnama is fraudulent one. Since the allegations of forgery was alleged by the defendant Nos.2- I 0 of Title Suit No.85 of 1993. same should be proved by them. It is settled principle of law that he who alleges fraud must positively proved the fraud. Reliance is placed in this regard on Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) and Assistant Custodian Vested Property, Dhaka and another Vs. Most. Anju Bibi and others reported in 2 MLR(AD) 291. So. it cannot be said that the learned appellate Court has committed any error of law in allotting 0.11 acres of land in favour of the plaintiffs. In this respect plaintiffs examined 3 witnesses to prove their settlement. Murad Mkt, PW.] in his deposition clearly slated that:“নালিশী জমি থেকে ১১ শং জমি আমার বাবা মুনীরুননেছা থেকে ১৯২০ বাং ১লা আষাঢ় তারিখে বিনা রেজিঃ হুকুমনামা মূলে জোত বন্দোবস্ত গ্রহণ করেন। আমি নালিশী দাগে ১১ শং বাবদ পৃথক ছাহাম চাই। নালিশী জমির মধ্যে আমার ঘর ও খালি জায়গা নিয়া মোট ০৭ শং জমিতে বতমানে দখল আছে।” PW.2 Son Mahar in his deposition stated that “বাদী মুরাদ মিয়া নালিশী দাগে ১ পোযা জমি দখল করে।” PW.3. In his cross-examination he clearly stated that“মুরাদ মিয়া ঘরের জমি অনুমান ১ পোয়া হবে।” 

 22. It further appears from the deposition of OW.1 and DW.2 on behalf of the defendant Nos.2-10 and plaintiffs of Title Suit No.69 of 1993. defendant No.2 who deposed in the suit as DW.I in his cross-examination categorically admitted that “ বাদরি বাবা বছই মিয়াকে নালিশি দাগে এস এ জরীপের আগে ঘর তুলে বসবাস করতে দেখেছি। বতমানে মুরাদ মিয়া নাঃ দাগের একটি ঘর এ বসবাস করিতেছে।" I DW.2 Yusuf Mia although admitted possession not in the entire 0.11 acres, but admitted the possession in respect of 0.0425. In his cross-examination he stated that “বাদী মুরাদ মিয়ার ঘরের জমির পরিমান ৪ 1/2 শং হতে পারে। DW.I Salina Khatun who deposed in the suit for defendant No.I5 of Title Suit No.85 of 1993 in her examination-in-chief stated that " বাদী মুরাদ মিয়া নালিশী দাগে ১১শং পেতে আমার কোন আপত্তি নাই।” in cross-examination she categorically stated that “বাদী মুরাদ মিয়া গং বতমানে ১ পোয়া জমিতে দখলকার।” It further appears that defendant Nos. 16(Ka) and 16(Kha) in Title Suit No.85 of 1993 also admitted the possession of 0.11 decimals of land in the suit schedule 3. Dewan Ferdous Ahmed Chowdhury, DW. I in his cross-examination stated“ আমার মাতা ও খালার দাখিলী W/S টি সত্য হয়। বাদী মুরাদ মিয়া নাঃ দাগের পশ্চিমাংশে প্রায় ১ পোয়া জমিতে দখলকার আছে।” 

 23. The appellate Court on consideration of oral and documentary evidence, admission made by the Zamindar predecessor of defendant Nos.l6(Ka) and 16(Kha) in -their written statement in respect of-settlement of 0.11 acres by executing Humumnama and considering all the evidence and materials on record rightly found that the plaintiffs predecessor of Title Suit No.85 of 1993 took settlement of 0.11 acres of land from Khatian No.2844 Plot No.2234 out of 0.4 acres of land. Further the trial Court erroneously allotted suborn of 0.850 acres in favour of the defendant Nos.2-10 of Title Suit No.85 of 1993 and plaintiffs of Title Suit No.69 of 1993 although they failed to prove their title on the basis of Kabuliyat (Exhibit-A), which was only for one year after expiry of kabuliyat period the contested defendants failed to produce any piece of papers or documents to show that some was extended by the Zamindar. Thus the appellate Court rightly held that the predecessor of defendant Nos.2-10. Abdul and Rahim Box did not extend the period of kabuliyat after one year in respect of the suit land. Thus by recording of S.A. Khatian in the names the defendant Nos.2-10 of Title Suit No.85 of 1993 and plaintiffs of Title Suit No.69 of 1993 did not acquire any title in the suit land. Reliance may he placed in this regard on Lal Mia being dead his heirs Vs. Haji Md. Ibrahim Mia and others reported in 28 DLR(AD) 61. Wherein it has been held that Record of right is not a document of title. It does not create or extinguish title to land. At best, along with other evidence, it may support an evidence of title. By itself it is not an evidence of title. 

 27. In view of the aforesaid discussion and on consideration of the evidence on record. specially Exhibit-A, points of law involved in the case and the decisions cited above. I am of the opinion that the impugned judgment and decree passed by the learned Joint District Judge. Additional Court. Sylhet in Title Appeal No.55 of 1997. 64 of 1997 and 65 of 1997 dismissing the appeals suffers from no illegality. There being no illegality in the impugned judgment. the same calls for no interference by this Court.

full_judgment:
2. The present appellants, as plaintiffs, instituted Other Class Suit No. 123 of 1985 in the Court of the learned Subordinate Judge, Jamalpur for declaration of their title in the suit land. Their case, in short, is that the suit land comprising 1.80 acres out of total 2.87 acres of RoR Khatian Nos. 23, 25 and 26 and CS Khatian No. 20 of Sheikh Shadi mouza, Ps-Melandha, District-Jamalpur along with other land belonged to Bebuillah Sheikh the predecessor of the plaintiffs and Nabu Sheikh, Vadu Sheikh and Gendi and CS khatian was accordingly published. That Babuillah Sheikh died leaving 2 sons Nabu Sheikh and Vadu Sheikh and daughter Gendi as his heirs. Thereafter, Gendi died leaving brothers Nabu Sheikh and Vadu Sheikh. Nabu Sheikh and Vedu Sheikh were in possession of entire 2.87 acres of land. Nabu Sheikh died leaving behind daughter plaintiff No. 1, son. Ayub Ali-predecessor of plaintiff Nos. 2 to 8 and another son named Najimuddin-predecessor of the plaintiff Nos. 9 to 14. Vadu Sheikh died leaving behind 3 daughters and 3 sons, the plaintiff Nos. 15 to 19 and Salimuddin who died leaving behind plaintiff Nos. 20 to 26 as his heirs. Thus the plaintiffs inherited the suit property and enjoyed the suit property continuously for more than 12 years. In suit plot Nos. 384 and 386 the plaintiffs have their homestead and have been residing therein with their families. The plaintiffs have been possessing other lands in ejmali through cultivation. That during RoR operation the suit property was wrongly recorded and only 1.07 acres of land out of total 2.87 acres of land was recorded in Khatian No. 24 in the name of the predecessor of the plaintiffs and the suit land comprising 1.80 acres of land was erroneously recorded in the name of the defendants and thereby a cloud being created the plaintiffs instituted the suit for declaration of their title. 

 4. The trial court, on consideration of the evidence adduced by both the parties, dismissed the suit by the judgment and decree dated 31-7-1993 making observation to the effect that though the plaintiffs have proved their title in the suit land but they could not prove their possession in the suit land and that the suit is also barred by limitation. Against this judgment and decree of the trial court the plaintiffs preferred Other Appeal No. 53 of 1993 before the learned District Judge, Jamalpur who, by the judgment and order dated 29-3-1995, allowed that appeal and set aside the judgment and decree of the trial court and decreed the suit declaring plaintiffs title in the suit land. The appellate court found that the plaintiffs had both title and possession in the suit land and the suit was not barred by limitation. Against this judgment and decree of the appellate court below the contesting defendants preferred the above mentioned Civil Revision No. 2622 of 1995 before the High Court Division and obtained Rule. A Division Bench of the High Court Division, after hearing both the parties, made that Rule absolute by setting aside the judgment and decree of the appellate court below and restoring those of the trial court by the impugned judgment and order. The High Court Division made observations to the effect that the plaintiffs could not prove their possession in the entire suit land and that the suit was barred by limitation. 

 6. Mr Subrata Sana, the learned Advocate for the appellants has made submissions before us to the effect that in this suit both the trial court and the appellate court below, considering the facts, circumstances and the evidence on record, found that the plaintiffs have title in the suit land; that the trial court though found that the plaintiffs could not prove their possession in the suit land, but the appellate court below, on proper appreciation of the evidence adduced by both the parties, rightly found that the plaintiffs have been able to prove their possession in the suit land; but the High Court Division most arbitrarily and abruptly, without making any discussion of any evidence at all and without controverting the findings and decision of the appellate court below and also the trial court made observations to the effect that the plaintiffs could not prove their title and also possession in the suit land. The learned Advocate for the appellants has argued that the High Court Division committed wrong and also great injustice in making the above observation without making any discussion at all and without reversing the clear findings and decision of the appellate court below as to title and possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land and the clear decision of the trial court also as to title of the plaintiffs in the suit land. The learned Advocate has argued also that in this suit it is rather an admitted fact that the plaintiffs predecessors were the original owners of the suit land and the suit land was duly recorded in the CS khatian in the name of the plaintiffs predecessors; that the contesting defendants though have alleged that the predecessors of the plaintiffs defaulted in payment of rent and, as such, the original landlords took back the suit land from them and subsequently they settled the same with different persons including the predecessors-in-interest of the plaintiffs and the predecessors-in-interest of the defendants, but this defence case has not been substantiated at all by any sort of evidence; that both the trial court and the appellate court below, therefore, rightly found plaintiffs title in the suit land, but the High Court Division, ignoring this fact that the defendants could not adduce any evidence whatsoever before court to prove their defence case, most unreasonably and unjustly opined that the plaintiffs could not prove their title also in the suit land. The learned Advocate for the plaintiff-appellants have made submissions to the effect also that this suit is not barred by limitation also as the plaintiffs have proved by sufficient evidence that they knew about the wrong recording of the suit land on 17-10-1985 only and thereafter they filed this suit within a short time; that the appellate court below, on thorough examination and consideration of the evidence adduced by both the parties rightly found that the plaintiffs filed the suit for declaration of their title within the statutory period of limitation and, as such, the suit is not barred by limitation. 

 7. Mr Awlad Ali, the learned Senior Advocate for the defendant-respondents has made submissions supporting the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. The learned Senior Advocate has argued that the High Court Division though did not make elaborate discussion in the impugned judgment, but it examined and considered the evidence on record thoroughly and found rightly that the plaintiffs failed to prove their title and possession in the suit land and the suit is also barred by limitation. The learned Senior Advocate has contended that the findings and decision of the High Court Division being correct this appeal is liable to be dismissed. 

 9. In this suit it is not disputed, rather admitted that the suit land originally belonged to the predecessors of the plaintiffs. In the CS khatian also the suit land was recorded in the name of the predecessors of the plaintiffs. The plaintiffs have claimed that they have acquired the suit land by way of inheritance from their predecessors the recorded owners of the land and have been possessing the same peacefully for more than 12 years. The contesting defendants though have pleaded a case to the effect that since the original tenants of the suit land defaulted in payment of rent the landlords took the entire 2.87 acres of land of the suit plots under their khas possession and subsequently the landlords settled those lands afresh with different persons including the predecessors of the plaintiffs and also the predecessors of the defendants, but this case of the defendants has not been substantiated at all by any evidence. Both the trial court and the appellate court below on consideration of the facts and circumstances and the evidence on record disbelieved this case of the contesting defendants and found plaintiffs title in the suit land. The trial court in his judgment made specific observation to the effect that the contesting defendants could not prove their alleged title in the suit land rather the plaintiffs have got title in the suit land. Against this clear observations and findings of the trial court the contesting defendants did not prefer any appeal or cross appeal. However, considering the evidence on record and the facts and circumstances we also, in agreement with the trial court and also the appellate court below, find that in this suit it has been well proved that the plaintiffs have title in the suit land. 

 11. It appears that in this suit the plaintiffs have examined 4 witnesses while the defendants have examined 3 witnesses. The PW 1 is the plaintiff No. 2 himself. This witness has deposed fully corroborating the plaintiffs case and has asserted also that the plaintiffs are in possession of the entire suit land. The PW 2 has deposed supporting the plaintiffs possession in the suit land. The PW 3 also has deposed supporting the plaintiffs possession in the suit land and has denied the defendants possession in the suit land. The PW 4 also has deposed stating that the plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land and that the defendants do not possess the suit land. On the other hand, the witnesses of the defendants side, namely, the DWs 2 and 3 though in their examination-in-chief has stated that the defendants are in possession of the suit land, but in course of cross-examination the DW 2 has stated that at present the defendants do not possess the suit land and the DW 3 has stated that at present none of the parties possessed the suit land. The above evidence of both the contesting parties coupled with the facts that the plaintiffs are the heirs of the admitted original owners of the suit land and there is no evidence to prove that plaintiffs predecessors title in the suit land was extinguished prove sufficiently that the plaintiffs are in possession of the suit land. The appellate court below on thorough analysis and consideration of the evidence adduced by both the parties and the facts and circumstances rightly found that the plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land. 

 12. The trial court though found that this suit, being not filed within 6 years from the date of the plaintiffs knowledge about recording of the suit land in the name of the defendants, is barred by limitation, but the appellate court below, on careful examination of evidence on record, found that the plaintiffs have proved sufficiently that they could know about the wrong recording of the suit land in the names of the defendants on 17-10-1985 only and, as such, this suit filed within 6 years from 17-10-1985 is not barred by limitation. The appellate court below made observations to the effect also that there is no evidence at all on record to prove that the plaintiffs had knowledge about the wrong recording of the suit land in the name of the defendants before 17-10-1985 and in the circumstances there was no reason not to believe the plaintiffs assertion that they could know about wrong recording of the suit land only on 17-10-1985. We have also examined the evidence on record and found no reason to disagree with these findings and decision of the appellate court below the plaintiffs have title in the suit land and they have also proved their possession in the suit land. The plaintiffs have adduced evidence to prove that they could know about the wrong recording of the suit land on 17-10-1985 only. There is no evidence on record to prove that the plaintiffs had knowledge about the wrong recording of the suit land before 17-10-1985. In the circumstances the appellate court below rightly found this suit for declaration of title not barred by limitation.

parties:
Komola Kanta Mokhupaddaya ------ Petitioner
VS
Salam Jomadder and others ------ Opposite-Parties
full_judgment:
This rule was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1-17 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 15-3-2003 passed by the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Barisal in Title Appeal No. 80 of 2002 reversing those dated 17-3-2002 passed by the Assistant Judge, Bakergonj in Title Suit No. 246 of 1985 dismissing the suit should not be set-aside. 

 2. Facts relevant for disposal of the rule are that the opposite parties as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 246 of 1986 for declaration that the `kha' schedule decree regarding the Ka schedule land is false, fraudulent, collusive, concocted and not binding upon the plaintiff. 

 3. It is stated in the plaint that the suit property was auction sold in Title Suit No. 251 of 1902 and Decree Execution Case No; 79 of 1903 and the possession was delivered on 19-9-1904 by Modhusudon chattapaddya and subsequently one Samcharan Chattapaddya took lease of the said property in 1333 BS in favour of the plaintiffs. Thereafter, the suit land .was recorded in the name of Asmot Ali Jomadder whose name was recorded in RS Khatian being No. 3279. 

 4. It is further stated in the plaint that they came to know from one Muzaffar Howlader on 11-3-1385 BS that the `kha' scheduled land was fraudulently decreed ex-parte on 19-3-1958 in Title Suit No. 333 of 1957 in the Court of Munsif 3rd Court, Barisal suppressing the summons upon the defendants of the aforesaid suit and hence the suit. 

 6. The trial court after, hearing the parties by its judgment and decree dated 17-3-2002 dismissed the suit of the plaintiff against which the defendants as appellants preferred Title Appeal No. 80 of 2002 before the District Judge, Barisal and on transfer it was heard by the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Barisal who by his judgment and decree dated 15-3-2003 allowed the appeal and set-aside the judgment and decree passed by the trial court and decreed the suit of the plaintiff. 

 14. He also submits that the trial court after proper discussion of the evidence found that the defendants have possession in the suit land long before and the appellate court without proper appreciation of the evidence of the D.Ws. wrongly held that the defendants have no title and possession of the suit land. 

 17. He further submits that the appellate court after independent discussion of the evidence on record found that the plaintiffs have title and possession over the suit land and their name was recorded in RS and SA Khatian and they are paying rent to the Government and on considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances the appellate court arrived at a correct decision that the plaintiffs have title and possession over the suit land. 

 18. He also submits that the decree passed in Title Suit No. 333 of 1957 on 19-3-1958 was obtained fraudulently by suppressing the summons and on considering the aforesaid fact appellate court properly found that the plaintiffs opposite parties have no knowledge about the aforesaid ex-parte decree and thus the suit is not barred by limitation. 

 23. The trial court framed as many as 6 issues in the suit. Wherefrom issue No.3- Whether the suit is barred by limitation? Issue No. 4- Whether the plaintiffs have title and possession in the 'ka' schedule land? Issue No. 5- Whether the `kha' schedule decree is liable to be set-aside? These are the main issues framed by the trial court. 

 27. The trial court also discussed that in the original plaint, the plaintiff's claim is that Jagot Chandra Das was the owner of the suit land. Later on it was amended by the plaintiff on 3-1-1979. But PW1 Mozahar Ali Zomadder in his cross-examination admitted that earlier Jagot Chandra Das was the owner and before that Shama Charan was the owner. Trial court found that from the above admission of the PW 1 it appears that Jagot Chandra Das was in possession and he had title in the suit land. 

 30. It is further found by the trial court that from the exhibit-ka the RS Khatian No. 3279, it appears that Shama Charan was the original owner of the suit land and his name was recorded in RS operation which was admitted by the plaintiff. 

 32. On considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances and the evidence on record trial court found that the claim of the plaintiff that Asmat Ali took pattan from Shama Charan has not been proved, rather the claim of the defendant that the ownership of Jagot Chandra by way of kolkarsha and the subsequent transfer to the defendant No.1 has been proved. Thus, the plaintiffs have no title in the suit land. 

 36. Trial court further found that on an application filed by the plaintiff the record of Title Suit No. 333 of 1957 was called for and it appears from the order sheet that the summons were duly served upon the defendants of the aforesaid suit. 

 37. On considering that the plaintiff could not prove the knowledge about the decree of 1958 by adducing witnesses mentioned in the plaint of the suit and on considering that in the order sheet it is found that the summons were duly served upon the defendants, the decree passed on 19-3-1958 was passed in accordance with law and is valid in the eye of law and the plaintiffs claim has not been proved that they had no knowledge about the aforesaid decree. Thus, the present suit which was filed on 3-1-1979 is barred by limitation. While deciding the issue No. 5 trial court found that the notice and summons were duly served upon the defendants i.e. the present plaintiff's in Title suit No. 333 of 1957. 

 38. Moreover, the plaintiff could not prove their title in the suit land and the decree dated 19-3-1958 is not liable to be set-aside and with the aforesaid findings trial court arrived at a decision that the plaintiff could not prove their case by adducing oral and documentary evidence and dismissed the suit of the plaintiff. 

 40. The appellate court discussed the claim of the plaintiff and the defendant. The appellate court found that Shamacharan was the original owner of the suit land and his name was recorded in R.S. operation and the name of Asmat Ali was recorded as tenant under Shamacharan. The plaintiff side produced two rent receipts-one is in 1360 BS and 2nd one is 1384 BS in the year of 1978 from which it appears that the rent was paid up to 1384 BS but no rent receipt was produced by the defendant side that they have paid any rent to the Government. 

 41. The appellate court further found that the defendant could not produce any documents that Jagot Chandra Das took pattan from the original owner thus, by the deed which was transferred to the defendant No. 1 by Sushila Bala, has no basis. There is no existence of title in the name of the defendant No. 1. The findings of the trial court on this regard that the plaintiff could not prove their title by way of inheritance in the suit land, is not correct. 

 43. The appellate court on the aforesaid discussion found that the plaintiffs have title in the `ka' schedule land and the defendant's decree in Title Suit No. 333 of 1957 is liable to be set-aside which was obtained ex-parte. With the aforesaid findings, the appellate court allowed the appeal and set-aside the judgment and decree passed by the trial court. 

 44. At the trial, trial court framed issues on whether the plaintiffs have any right, title, interest and possession in the suit property and also framed issues whether the kha' schedule decree is liable to be set-aside. 

 45. It is decided by the trial court that the suit is barred by limitation. The trial court took decision considering two points-1) The plaintiff could not prove their knowledge about the date of decree dated 19-3-1958. 2) The summons and notices were duly served upon the defendants of the Title Suit No. 333 of 1957. On the other hand, the appellate court reversed the findings of the trial court that PW 4 Mosharaf Hossain proved the date of knowledge and from that date within 1 (one) year the suit was filed. Thus, the suit is not barred by limitation. Now, let us see from the record and the evidence that which findings of the courts below is correct and based oh evidence on record. 

 48. From the order sheet of the Title Suit No. 333 of 1957 found that the notices and summons were duly served upon the defendants. So, the suit was filed after long laps of 21 years of the alleged decree. From the record of Title Suit No. 333 of 1957 and from the order sheet it is found that order No. 4 dated 21-1-1958 plaintiff filed Hazira, summons were served duly but the defendant was absent. Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the suit issued registered card with A/D upon the defendants fixing next date on 11-2-1958 for appearance of the parties. 

 53. From the order No. 4 of Title Suit No. 333 of 1957 it appears that the learned Judge applying judicial mind to the fact passed an order for serving notices upon the defendant by postal A/D and from the order No.8 it appears that the learned Judge confirming the serving of the summons that it was duly served upon the defendants taken up the case for ex-parte hearing. 

 57. Thus, on perusal of the order sheet of the Title Suit No. 333 of 1957 and paragraph-4 of the present plaint and the evidence of the P.Ws. it may be concluded that the plaintiff in the present suit could not prove the alleged date of knowledge which was stated in paragraph-4 and on the other hand from the order sheet of the earlier suit it appears that the notices and summons were duly served and the decree was passed in accordance with law in the earlier Title Suit filed by the defendants. Thus, the appellate court wrongly found that the suit is not barred by limitation and the decision arrived at by the trial court is proper that the suit is barred by limitation. 

 58. Now, if the suit is barred by limitation then the other issues which were decided by the courts below has a little value to be decided, yet from the discussions it appears that the appellate court did not discuss the evidence on record independently while deciding the question of title and possession of the suit in question. As the last court of fact the appellate court without following the provision of Order XLI, rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure passed the impugned judgment and decree in a slipshod manner and the judgment and decree of the appellate court has been passed as a non-speaking judgment, as all the issues framed by the trial court were not discussed and reversed by the appellate court. 

 61. It is discussed above that while deciding the issues of limitation and as well as the main issue that the decree obtained ex-parte is liable to be set-aside. The learned Judge of the appellate court without any discussion and without perusing the documents of the earlier Title Suit No. 333 of 1957 setting-aside the judgment of the trial court and declared the title and possession of the plaintiff in the suit land. 

 62. The trial court discussed the question of title of the parties. The trial court believed the evidence of DW 2 Abdul Ali Zomadder who is the son of Asmat Ali Zomadder and attesting witness of the deed dated 21-4-1942 exhibit-Ka by which the suit land was transferred to the defendant No. 1 by Sushila Bala which is a registered deed. 

 65. From the aforesaid decisions and the deposition of the PW 2 Abdul Ali Zomaddar the son of Asmat Ali Zomaddar who is an attesting witness of the deed dated 19-4-1942 and DW 2 identified the signature of his father, so, it is believable that Asmat Ali Zomaddar knowing fully well about the contents of the deed and signed over it and his son denied the title and possession of the plaintiff in the suit land. 

 66. Thus, this point decided by the appellate court that the plaintiffs have title and possession over the suit land is a wrong finding and not based upon the evidence and documents on records and the exhibits. 

 69. From the evidence it appears that in the plaint, plaintiffs admitted the title of the predecessor of the defendant but after deposition of the PW 1 which was ended on 29-3-1987 and prayer of the plaint was amended on 25-7-2001 and PW 1 in his cross-examination admitted that Jagot Chandra was the earlier owner of the suit land. So, admitting the tile or ownership of any party in evidence, that cannot be denied by an amendment of the paint later on. 

 70. The trial court on considering the deposition of the DWs properly found that Sushila Bala has title and interest in the suit land through Jagot Chandra and the plaintiff could not prove their title and possession on this point and the appellate court on wrong appreciation of the evidence and the documents on record decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff which is liable to be set-aside. 

 74. The impugned judgment and decree dated 15-3-2003 passed by the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Barisal in Title Appeal No. 80 of 2002 is hereby set-aside. The judgment and decree dated 17-3-2002 passed by the Assistant Judge, Bakergonj in Title Suit No. 246 of 1985 is restored.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2547 of 2010
parties:
The Dhaka City Corporation………Petitioner
Vs.
Mohammad Samiullah Miah…….Respondent
full_judgment:
2. Facts of the case, in brief, are that the respondent as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 544 of 1985 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka for declaration of title over the suit property stating inter alia that the suit land originally belonged to Tara Sundari Debi and Moni Gupta.' Their name was recorded in C.S. Khatian. While they had been possessing the, suit land with other property, they gave settlement of the property to one Hamidullah Sarder. Hamidullah Sarder owned and possessed the suit property with the knowledge of all concerned since 1919. Hamidullah Sarder gifted the suit land in favour of his wife Akuti Bibi and 3 grandsons, namely Atikullah Miah, Chan Miah, Sudulah Miah by a registered deed of Heba-bil-Ewaj dated 22.7.1938. Hamidullah Sarder on 22.12.1954 executed and registered a deed of rectification in respect of the suit land in connection with the earlier deed of Heba-Bil-Ewaj dated 22.07.1938. Akuti Bibi died leaving her husband Hamidullah Sarder and four daughters, namely Sonaban, Shahjadi Bibi, Sahara Banu and Tarabanu and three grandsons, namely Atikullah, Chan Miah and Sadullah, Sahera Banu, Sahajadi Bibi, Tara Banu and Chan Miah sold their share to Abdul Matin, who had been possessing the land within the knowledge of all concerned and his name was recorded in the khatian. Abdul Matin died leaving two wives, namely Kulsum Bibi and Afrunnessa, mother Nasimunnessa, brother Abdul Halim, sister Latifanessa and daughter Shahida. The plaintiff purchased the suit land from the heirs and successive heirs of Abdul Matin by several deeds of sale. The plaintiff has been possessing the suit land without any interruption for more than 60 years. The defendant has no right, title, interest and possession, but is claiming the suit land illegally without any document. The defendant was trying to dispossess the plaintiff from the suit land, and as a result the plaintiff was compelled to file the suit. The further case of the plaintiff is that during the pendency of the suit the defendant dispossessed the plaintiff from the 'Kha' schedule land measuring approximately 2 katha adjacent to the road on the east side which is fully described in the schedule 'Ka' of the plaint. 

 3. The defendant contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations of the plaint, stating, inter alia that the suit land described in the schedule of the plaint of Mouza Koratitola of Dhaka City of. C.S. Khatian No. 3930 appertaining to plot No. 1 (part), Sheet No. 68(Ka), Ward-3, was acquired by the Government for Dhaka City Corporation in the year 1923-1924. The plaintiff has no right, title and possession over the acquired land. The plaintiff claimed the suit land, by virtue of false and created documents and was trying to grab the property. The suit land corresponding to S.A. plot No. 8606, 8607 and 8608 belong to the Dhaka City Corporation. Plaintiff has no right and title over the suit property hence the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 4. After hearing the parties and considering the evidence on record the learned Subordinate Judge by his judgment and decree dated 24.04.2006 decreed the suit. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and decree the defendant as appellant preferred Title Appeal No. 343 of 2006 in the Court of learned District Judge, Dhaka, which was subsequently heard by the learned Additional District Judge, 8th Court, Dhaka, who after hearing the parties and perusing the records dismissed the appeal and affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial Court.
