caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1587 of 2011
parties:
Mohammad G.R. Nasir and another ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Mrs. Halima Khatun being dead her heirs 1. (a) Mohammad Afzalur Rahman and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Syed Mahmud Hosain, J. This Petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 08.03.2011 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2460 of 2010 discharging the Rule and affirming the judgment and order dated 24.02.2010 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Seventh Court, Dhaka in Civil Revision No. 153 of 2007 rejecting the Civil revision against order dated 20.03.2007 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 23 of 2003 rejecting an application for the amendment of the plaint. The fact, leading to the filing of this petition for leave to appeal, in a nutshell, are: 

 2. The petitioners herein as the plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 204 of 2002 in the Second Court of the Assistant Judge, Dhaka impleading the respondents as the defendants for declaration to the effect that the revocation of the Power of Attorney dated 12.01.2002 executed and registered by defendant No. 1 in favour of the plaintiffs-petitioners for the purpose of carrying over the construction of a multi-storied Commercial Building on a plot of land measuring 18 Khatas, 3 chhatak in Gulshan-1 area owned by the defendant-respondent No. 1 was unlawful and not binding upon the plaintiffs-petitioners and that the plaintiffs-petitioners had the lawful right to carry out the said work on the said plot of land by virtue of the said power of Attorney executed and registered on 12.01.2002 which was revoked. 

 3. Defendant No. 1 contested the suit by fling written statement denying all the material statements made in the plaint. The aforesaid suit was transferred to the Court of Joint District Judge, First Court, Dhaka and renumbered as Title Suit No. 23 of 2003. During pendency of the suit, the plaintiffs-petitioners on 08.02.2007 filed an application for amendment of the plaint under Order VI Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the defendants contested the application. 

 “বাদীগণের অনুকুলে আর্জির তপসিল-খ তে বর্ণিত সম্পত্তি সংক্রান্ত দখলের ডিক্রি দিতে এবং ১নং এবং ৩নং বিবাদীদ্বয় বাদীগণকে উহার দখল হস্তান্তর না করিলে আদালতযোগে দখল (দখলের) আদেশ দিতে।” The original prayers Ga and Gha were converted to prayers-Ga and Roshoie (B). The cause title relating to valuation was changed from Tk. 2,20,000/- to Tk. 20,36,000/- and in paragraph - 26 the word declaration was proposed to be deleted by adding (সুনির্দিষ্টভাবে চুক্তি প্রবলের) and in the same paragraph the word নির্ধারিত To be deleted by adding আইন মোতাবেক সর্বোচ্চ”। 

 15. In the case of Radha Krishna Jogani (Agarwalla) Vs. Dwarks Das Agarawalla and others, (1984) 36 DLR (AD) 253 a suit was originally filed for declaration of rights and for accounts. By a subsequent prayer and additional ground namely for dissolution of the firm was sought to be included in the suit. Now the question arose whether the amendment sought would alter the nature of the suit so as to substitute one cause of action for another cause in the suit and whether such an amendment may be allowed under Order VI, Rule 17 of the Code of Civil procedure, Relying upon innumerable reported cases this Division found that amendment of such nature in the plaint may be allowed under the provision of law without affecting the nature of the suit. 

 16. In the case of Managing Committee N.M.C. Model High School and other Vs. Obaidur Rahman Chowdhury and others, (1979) 31 DLR (AD) 133, a suit for permanent injunction was filed. Subsequently the plaintiff prayed for converting the suit into one for declaration of title and recovery of possession. 

 17. This Division found that such an amendment would not change the nature and character holding that adding the prayer of declaration of title and recovery of possession may appear to have changed the nature of the suit but a close scrutiny of the original pleading will show that the facts were there in a different form which are not being properly articulated. Apart from this, when the prayer was made for amendment there was no question of limitation and the plaintiff had put in the requisite court fees. In that view of the matter, we do not find that the courts below were in error in making the orders. It is to be observed that one of the fundamental principles governing the amendment of the pleadings is that all the controversies between the parties as far as possible should be included and multiplicity of proceedings avoided. 

 18. In the case of Abdul Motalab Vs. Md. Ershad Ali and others, (1998) 18 BLD (AD) 121, this Division relying upon a number of reported cases came to a finding that a suit for declaration of title and recovery of possession and/or partition is essentially based on a common claim of the plaintiff which may call for different relief or reliefs in different situation and as such, the adding of a relevant new relief by way of amendment does not change the nature and character of the suit when the claim of the plaintiff basically rests on the same foundation. By adding a relief for partition in a suit for declaration of title and possession there is no alteration to the foundation of the suit and the fundamental character of the suit remains the same and as such, the proposed amendment was rightly allowed.

parties:
Subinay Das and others.
Vs.
Md. Intaj Mia and Hormuj Mia being dead his legal heirs: (1) Bozlu Mia and others.
full_judgment:
Soumendra Sarker, J: The Rule issued calling upon the Opposite Party No.1 & 2 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 24.12.1986 & 31.12.1986 respectively passed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, Habigonj in Title Appeal No. 86 of 1984 reversing those dated 31.07.1984 and 07.08.1984 respectively passed by the learned Munsif, 3th Court, Habigonj in Title Suit No.309 of 1976 should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order of orders as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present opposite-parties as plaintiffs instituted the original suit for specific performance of contract being Title. Suit No.309 of 1976 in the 3rd Court of the then Munsif, Habigonj contending inter-alia that the suit property appertaining to CS. plot No.5360 of Mouza Sultan Mamudpur, JL No.17, Chowdhury Bazar, Habigonj town originally belonged to the defendant No.4 Bipin Behari Das and his brother Banka Chandra Behari Das as joint Hindu property. Banka Chandra died leaving the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 as sons and the defendant No.3 as widow. The defendant Nos.l-3 and 4 entered into a contract for sale in respect of the land under plot No.5360 of khatian No.1317 in favour of the plaintiffs at a consideration of Tk. 5,000/-(five thousand). Accordingly; in the month of June, 1970 the defendant Nos.1, 2 and 3 accepted Tk.1550/- as earnest Money and the defendant No.4 took a sum of Tk.1550/- as earnest money for their respective saham in the premises but due to the absence of income tax clearance certificate the kabla deed could not be executed and registered. The defendant No.4 receiving balance consideration amount of Tk.1000/-(one thousand) executed and registered kabla deed in favour of the plaintiffs on 04.04.1973 in respect of his share but the defendant Nos.1, 2 and 3 did not execute and register the kabla deed and meanwhile the war of liberation in the year of 1971 was started. The plaintiffs requested the defendant Nos.1-3 to execute & register the deed after taking the balance amount but the defendants denied. Thereafter the plaintiffs filed the original suit. 

 4. The learned trial court i.e. the Munsif, 3rd Court, Habigonj during trial of the original suit after taking evidence from the sides of the respective parties dismissed the suit on contest vide judgment and decree dated 31.07.1984. 

 5. Being aggrieved the plaintiffs preferred an appeal being Title Appeal No.86 of 1984 in the court of learned District Judge, Habigonj which was heard and disposed of by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, Habigonj and the lower appellate, court by the impugned judgment and decree dated 24.12.1986 allowed the appeal reversing the judgment and dismissal decree of the trial court and decreed the suit. 

 9. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite-parties opposing the Rule submits that the appellate court below in passing the impugned judgment and decree committed no illegality or irregularity. There has been no mis-reading or non-reading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts in deciding the fate of the appeal. The learned Advocate further submits that admittedly one of the owner of the schedule property the defendant No.4 in respect of his particular share executed and registered a sale deed in favour of the plaintiffs and against that deed the defendant Nos.l-3 filed a pre-emption Miscellaneous case being No.145 of 1973 under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The said kabla deed was registered by the defendant No.4 after receiving the consideration money on 04.04.1973. The learned Advocate also submits that the plaintiffs to the suit who are the opposite-parties of this revisional application, by sufficient evidence has been able to discharge their onus in proving their respective case that the defendant Nos. 1-3 after taking earnest money of Tk. 1550/- pursuant an oral agreement for sale in favour of the plaintiffs entered in to a contract but for want of income tax clearance certificate they could not execute and register a sale deed and subsequently when they denied to execute and register the deed the plaintiffs filed the original suit for specific performance of contract. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the appellate court below during disposal of the appeal considering all the facts and circumstance of the case including the evidence adduced from the sides of the respective parties reversed the judgment and decree of the trial court and decreed the suit which can't be interfered with by this court. 

 11. On perusal of the case record it transpires that admittedly the disputed premises is a homestead and belong to the defendant Nos. 1-3 appertaining to C.S. plot No.5360. It is the plaint case of the plaintiffs that they possess the premises on the basis of varatia agreement between them and the defendants and afterwards the defendant Nos.1-3 in respect of the premises corresponding to khatian No.1317 entered into an oral contract of sale and the consideration amount was fixed Tk. 5,000/- (five thousand) equally payable to the original owners i.e. the defendant Nos.1-3 and 4. The defendant No. 4 in respect of his share while executed and registered a sale deed on 04.04.1973 the defendant Nos.1-3 filed a pre-emption case for getting the land pre-empted against that kabla deed. The contesting defendants in their pleadings specifically denied the plaintiff's case of agreement for sale and asserted that they never entered into any oral contract to dispose of the property in favour of the plaintiffs and never took a sum of Tk. 1,550/- as earnest money. The present petitioners most emphatically submits that the plaintiff's case of oral contract and absence of income tax clearance certificate is not proved by a single credible authentic evidence. 

 14. On perusal of the case records & evidence therein it further appears that the original suit is banked upon dubious pleadings of the plaintiffs. In respect of the suit premises admittedly the plaintiffs were monthly tenants under the defendants & the story of oral contract is after thought. Therefore; apparently under the purview of section 103 of the Evidence Act the onus of proof exclusively lies upon the plaintiffs as to their case i.e. the existence of oral contract between the parties and absence of income tax clearance certificate which was the reason for non-execution and non-registration of the kabla deed in favour of the plaintiffs. 

 18. In this context; our Apex court in the case laws reported in 6 BLC (AD) 115 and 45 DLR(AD) 205 held: Once the relationship of landlord and tenant is established between the parties, the tenant is estopped from challenging the title of the landlord without surrendering possession. Section 116 of the Evidence Act is very much clear in this regard. 

 22. In the result; the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The impugned judgment and decree dated 24.12.1986 & 31.12.1986 respectively passed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, Habigonj in Title Appeal No.86 of 1984 is hereby set aside.

parties:
Md. Anwarulla ----- Appellant
Vs.
Mohammad Humayun being dead his legal heirs: 1(a). Abdur Rashid and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Nazmun Ara Sultana J.:- This Civil Appeal, by leave granted in Civil Review Petition No. 16 of 2008, has arisen from the judgment and order dated 29.01.2006 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 504 of 2001 making the rule absolute and thereby setting aside the judgment and decree dated 17.09.2000 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 218 of 1992 affirming those dated 25.06.1992 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 4th Artha Rin Adalat, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 72 of 1992 dismissing the suit. 

 2. Mohammad Humayun-the predecessor of the present plaintiff-respondents herein, as plaintiff; instituted Title Suit No. 224 of 1984 in the 3rd Court of the Sub-judge, Dhaka which was subsequently transferred to the court of Sub-judge and 4th Artha Rin Adalat, Dhaka and was renumbered as Title Suit No. 72 of 1992, for declaration of title, recovery of khas possession and for further declaration to the effect that the expert decree passed in Title Suit No. 231 of 1977 of the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka is illegal and not binding upon the plaintiff. 

 3. The case of the plaintiff, in short, is that the suit property originally belonged to Hazi Abdul Wahab. Hazi Abdul Wahab transferred the suit property in favour of his second wife-who adopted Islam as religion from Hinduism and took the name Nurjahan Begum. The said Nurjahan Begum expressed her desire to take Abdur Rouf, a son of the plaintiff, as her son and Hazi. Abdul Wahab gave his consent to it. When said Abdur Rouf became adult he married a girl of a family of Tongi Area without the knowledge of his father and started living at the residence of his father-in-law and in the meantime Nurjahan Begum died in Dhaka Medical College Hospital on 28.08.1978 without any issue. As a result the heirs of Abdul Wahab got the suit property by the law of inheritance. But Abdur Rouf claimed the suit property on the ground that Nurjahan Begum before, her death, made a gift of the suit property in his favour for which the plaintiff Md. Humayun instituted Title Suit No. 167 of 1975 for partition Abdur Rouf also filed Title Suit No. 165 of 1975 claiming the suit property which was subsequently dismissed for default. The Title Suit No. 167 of 1975 filed by the plaintiff was decreed on compromise on 01.03.1999 and the plaintiff got the suit land in his shaham by the said compromise decree. 

 4. That Abdur Rouf-the proforma defendant No. 2 entered into an agreement for sale of the suit property with the defendant No. 1, on 09.02.1977 and subsequently the defendant No. 1 filed Title Suit No. 231 of 1977 for specific performance of contract against Abdur Rouf and that suit was decreed ex-parte and the defendant No. 1, by filing execution case, got the kabala deed executed and registered through court on 05.02.1979 Thereafter, the defendant No. 1 filed a suit for permanent injunction, that since the decree for specific performance of contract was passed during the pendency of Title Suit No. 167 of 1975 the said decree was barred by the principle of lies-pendency, moreover since the defendant No. 2 had no right, title and interest in the suit property, the defendant No. 1 also could not acquire any right, title and interest in the suit property by that decree That the defendant No. 1 dispossessed the plaintiff from the suit property in the middle of 1979 and hence the plaintiff has filed this suit 

 5. The defendant No 1 contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint His defence case was that Abdul Wahab transferred the suit property in favour of Nurjahan Begum by executing a deed of lease and as Nurjahan Begum had no issue she brought up the proforma defendant No. 2-who had been living with' Nurjahan Begum in the suit property and Nurjahan Begum thereafter transferred the suit property by way of gift in favour of the proforma defendant No. 2 on 20.08.1970 and confirmed that oral gift by executing a written instrument on 23.08.1970 and subsequently died on 28.08.1978. That the plaintiff was fully aware of this fact and he attempted to dispossess the proforma defendant No. 2 from the suit property. The proforma defendant No. 2 then filed Title Suit No. 165 of 1975 for permanent injunction which was subsequently dismissed for non-prosecution. That the proforma defendant No. 2 executed a bainapatra in favour of the defendant No. 1 on 09.02.1977 by taking Tk. 50,000/- out of stipulated consideration of Tk. 80,000/- and handed over possession of the suit property to the defendant No. 1. But since the proforma defendant No. 2 failed to execute the sale deed as per bainapatra the defendant No.1 filed Title Suit No. 231 of 1977 for specific performance of contract and got decree and also the sale deed executed and registered through court and got possession also through court. That as the plaintiff attempted to dispossess the defendant No. 1 from the suit land the defendant No. 1 filed a suit against the plaintiff and obtained an order of temporary injunction. That the plaintiff filed a suit for partition and though all the defendants except the present proforma defendant No. 2 filed compromise petition in that suit but this proforma defendant No. 2 did not sign that compromise petition. That the plaintiff has no right, title interest and possession in the suit property and as such the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 8. Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, the learned Senior Advocate for the defendant-appellant has made submissions to the effect that in this suit the plaintiff has totally failed to prove his possession in the suit land within 12 years prior to institution of the suit and as such the suit for declaration of title and recovery of possession was barred by limitation, that both the trial court and the appellate court below, on thorough examination of the evidence adduced by both the parties, rightly found that the plaintiff could not prove his possession in the suit land and also alleged dispossession therefrom and, therefore, rightly dismissed the suit; that the High Court Division acted in excess of its revisional jurisdiction in decreeing the suit without reversing these concurrent findings of the courts of facts on finding of any misreading or non-reading of the material evidence on record. The learned Counsel for the defendant-appellant has made submissions to the effect also that Civil Revision No. 504 of 2001 was decided by the High Court Division in the absence of the present appellant who was the present appellant-who was opposite party No. 1 in that civil revision; that no notice of that civil revision was served on the opposite party No. 1 of that civil revision and consequently the opposite party No. 1 (the present appellant) did not get any opportunity to contest the rule issued in that civil revision and as a result the High Court Division could not take the right decision and consequently made the rule absolute most unjustly; that the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is not sustainable in law in view of the fact that the High Court Division did not advert to or reversed the concurrent findings of both the courts of facts. The learned Counsel has contended that both the courts of facts, on proper evaluation and appreciation of the evidence adduced by both the parties rightly found that the plaintiff could not prove his possession in the suit land within 12 years prior to the institution of the suit, but the High Court Division without taking into consideration these concurrent findings of the courts of facts made the rule absolute most unjustly and arbitrarily. 

 9. Mr. A. J. Mohammad Ali, the learned Senior Advocate for the plaintiff-respondent No. 1 has made submissions supporting the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. The learned Counsel has argued that the very defence case that the suit property was transferred to Nurjahan Begum by its original owner Abdul Wahab by deed of lease dated 19.03.1958 is not acceptable at all that this alleged lease deed is void because it was created after 16th December, 1955 which is hit under section 75 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The learned Advocate has contended that the said lease deed was a mere paper transaction only which was never acted upon; that the proforma defendant No. 2 Abdur Rouf also could not acquire any right, title or interest in the suit property by virtue of the alleged oral gift made by Nurjahan Begum in his favour. The learned Counsel has argued also that the plaintiff of the present suit filed Title Suit No. 167 of 1975 for partition of the suit property and that suit was decreed on compromise by a competent court of law and so long this decree stands the defendants of the present suit cannot claim any right, title and interest in the suit land. The learned Counsel has argued also that the plaintiff has proved by sufficient evidence that the defendant No.1 dispossessed him from the suit land forcibly after obtaining the decree for specific performance of contract in Title Suit No. 231 of 1977 and as such this suit is not barred by limitation at all. The learned Counsel has contended that both the trial court and the appellate court below committed wrong in making assessment of the evidence adduced by the parties and thus arrived at a wrong findings and decision that the High Court Division assessed the evidence on record and other facts and circumstances properly and thus came to the correct decision. 

 11. Admittedly, the suit land originally belonged to Hazi Abdul Wahab. It is also an admitted fact that Hazi Abdul Wahab transferred the suit land to his second wife Nurjahan Begum by a registered lease deed dated 19.03.1958. The plaintiff, in his very pleadings, has stated this fact and did not raise any question as to the validity of this lease deed. The plaintiff in his plaint, rather, has stated to the effect that since Nurjahan Begum died childless the suit property devolved upon the heirs of Abdul Wahab after her death. The plaintiff, admittedly, did not raise any question as to the validity of this lease deed before any court-either in the present suit-or in any other earlier suits. In this present appeal before this Division, for the first time, the plaintiff has raised this question as to the validity of the lease deed in favour of Nurjahan Begum. However, this is a question of law and as such we entertain this question and hold that this lease deed being created after 16th December, 1955 is hit under section 75A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and as such is not a valid one. 

 12. Now the question is whether Nurjahan Begum acquired title in the suit land by adverse possession on the basis of this invalid lease deed. It is plaintiff’s case that Nurjahan Begum was in possession of the suit land after having this alleged lease deed executed and registered in her favour on 19.03.1958 and remained in possession of the suit land till her death in the year 1978. Both the trail court and the appellate court below, on proper assessment of the evidence on record and the facts and circumstances, found that Nurjahan Begum was in possession of the suit property by exercising her own right and title thereon on the basis of this alleged lease deed till her death in the year 1978. So, Nurjahan Begum acquired title in the suit land by virtue of adverse possession for more than 12 years. The plaintiff himself has admitted in his very pleadings that Hazi Abdul Wahab the original owner of the suit land transferred the suit land to his 2nd wife Nurjahan Begum by a registered lease deed dated 19.03.1958 and after the death of Nurjahan Begum the heirs of Abdul Wahab got the suit land by virtue of inheritance. These very statements of the plaintiff himself prove sufficiently that Nurjahan Begum possessed the suit land by exercising her own right, title and interest thereon on the basis of this registered lease deed dated 19.03.1958 and in the circumstances Nurjahan Begum acquired title in the suit land by virtue of adverse possession for a long period of about 20 years. The plaintiff has claimed that after the death of Nurjahan Begum he along with other heirs of Hazi Abdul Wahab inherited the suit land. But this claim of the plaintiff is not acceptable at all. The plaintiff or other heirs of Hazi Abdul Wahab are not the heirs of Nurjahan Begum. So, at the death of Nurjahan Begum the question of acquisition of the suit property by the heirs of Hazi Abdul Wahab does not arise at all The present appellant, as defendant No.1, in the original suit, pleaded a case that Nurjahan Begum before her death gifted the suit land to Abdur Rouf a son of the plaintiff whom Nurjahan Begum adopted as a son. The plaintiff himself also has pleaded that Nurjahan Begum with the consent of her husband Abdul Wahab Look Abdur Rouf as her son and reared up him. The plaintiff though has pleaded a case that subsequently Abdur Rouf, after attaining his marriageable age, married a girl of Tongi Area and started levity in his father-in-law's house at Tongi, but this case of the plaintiff has not been substantiated. Rather we find that there are sufficient evidence to prove that Abdur Rouf used to reside with Nurjahan Begum till her death. However, admittedly the defendant No.1 filed a suit for specific performance of contract being Case No. 231 of 1977 against Abdur Rouf and got an ex-parte decree and in execution of that ex-parte decree he got the kabala deed executed and registered through court and also got delivery of possession of one of the rooms of the suit property through court. The contesting defendant has adduced some evidence to prove that Nurjahan Begum gifted the suit property to Abdur Rouf orally and Abdur Rouf used to possess that suit property on the basis of oral gift and Abdur Rouf subsequently transferred the possession of the suit land excepting one room only on the basis of bainapatra executed by him in favour of the defendant No. 1. The defendant No. 1 has also proved by adducing necessary papers that after getting the kabala deed executed and registered through court in respect of the suit property he mutated the suit land in his name and paid rent to the government and got rent receipts and he has constructed also a 7 storied building on the suit land. 

 13. The plaintiff though has claimed that he was in possession of the suit property within 12 years prior to institution of the suit, but this claim of the plaintiff even if taken as true, does not entitle the plaintiff to get the decree as prayed for. Because according to the own case of the plaintiff Nurjahan Begum was possessing the suit land till her death in 1978 and this suit was filed in 1984. So, the plaintiff, if at all, took possession of the suit property after the death of Nurjahan Begum he possessed the same only for 5/6 years before filing of this suit. Since we have already found that at the death of Nurjahan Begum the plaintiff could not acquire any right, title or interest in the suit property the alleged possession of the plaintiff in the suit property for 5/6 years only does not entitle him l to get a decree in this suit for declaration of title and recovery of possession. 

 14. Mr. A. J. Mohammad Ali. the learned Counsel for the plaintiff-respondent has argued also to the effect that since the plaintiff- respondent got a decree for partition in respect of the suit land in Title Suit No. 167 of 1975 from a competent court of law his claim of title in the suit property cannot be brushed asides. But we are unable to accept this argument also of the learned Counsel. We have already I found that Nurjahan Begum acquired valid title in the suit property by virtue of long possession of more than 12 years on the basis of an invalid registered lease deed. So, the plaintiff or other heirs of Hazi Abdul Wahab had no right, title and possession in the suit land. The Partition Suit being Title Suit No. 167 of 1975 was filed among the heirs of Abdul Wahab and it was decreed on compromise. The pro-forma defendant No. 2 Abdul Roof though was made a defendant in that partition suit, but admittedly, he was not made a party in that compromise petition and he did not sign that compromise petition. However, where the suit property belonged to Nurjahan Begum this Partition Suit No. 167 of 1975 filed among the heirs of Hazi Abdul Wahab and the decree thereof arc not of any value at all, rather this compromise decree is a nullity. On the basis of this compromise decree the plaintiff or any other of the parties of that compromise acquired no right, title and interest in the suit property and this compromise decree is not binding on Abdur Rouf also-who did not sign the compromise petition. 

 15. However, on careful scrutiny of the evidence on record we find that the trial court and the appellate court below, on correct evaluation and appreciation of the evidence on record, rightly found that the plaintiff never had/has any right title and possession in the suit land. The trial court, therefore, rightly dismissed the suit and the appellate court below rightly affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial court. 

 16. The High Court Division has committed wrong in decreeing the suit of the plaintiff setting aside the concurrent findings and decision of the court of facts. The High Court Division appears to have decreed the suit holding it as not barred by limitation. The High Court Division made observations to the effect that according to the own case of the contesting defendant No.1 he got possession of the suit land partly in the year 1977 when the bainapatra was made and got possession of the rest of the suit land in the year 1979 through court in execution of the decree in Title Suit No. 231 of 1977 and that the present suit .was filed in the year 1984 and as such it was not barred by Limitation. Obviously, the High Court Division did not take into consideration at all the admitted fact that Hazi Abdul Wahab-the original owner of the suit land transferred the suit land to Nurjahan Begum by a registered deed of the year 1958 and since then Nurjahan Begum was in possession of the suit land by exercising her own right and title thereon and thus acquired good title in the suit land by virtue of adverse possession for about 20 years till her death and as such at the death of Nurjahan Begum the heris of Hazi Abdul Wahab including the plaintiff could not acquire any right, title arid interest in the suit land. Nurjahan Begum admittedly, died in the year 1978 and as such the plaintiff though adduced some evidence to prove that he possessed the suit land for some period after the death of Nurjahan Begum in the year 1978 but this fact does not entitle him to get a decree for declaration of title and khas possession. The High Court Division took into consideration the alleged sloe decree passed in Partition Suit No. 167 of 1975 and opined that by virtue of this decree the plaintiff has got the suit property in his share ignoring the fact altogether that the plaintiff and the other heirs of Hazi Abdul Wahab did not acquire any right, title and interest in the suit land at the death of Nurjahan Begum-who acquired valid right, title and interest in the suit land by virtue of long possession for more than 20 years on the basis of a registered lease deed, though invalid. The High Court Division's further findings that the decree passed in Title Suit No. 231 of 1977 for specific performance of contract is hit by section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act since it was obtained during pendency of the partition suit-also is not correct. Since the decree of the Partition Suit No. 167 of 1975 is a nullity, doctrine of lis-pendency will not hit the decree passed in Title Suit No. 231 of 1977.

Sharif Uddin Chaklader J: This Rule, at the instance of defendant, directed against judgment and decree dated 7-11-2012 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Khulna Allowing Title Appeal No. 401 of 1997 thereby decreeing Title Suit No. 200 of 1980 on reversing those dated 5-10-1997 passed by the learned the then Sub-ordinate Judge now Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Khulna. 

 3. Plaintiff opposite party No. 1 instituted Title Suit No. 200 of 1980 in the court of Sub-ordinate Judge, 1st Court, Khulna against petitioners and others for establishment of title and recovery of khas possession and compensation on the allegation contending inter alia that the land under CS khatian No. 1001 of Mouza Baniakhamar, Police Station Khulna, District Khulna originally belonged to Poilan Sheikh, Badulla Sheikh and Shahamatullah Sheikh in equal share in rayioti right and their names were recorded properly. Of them, Shahamatullah was in exclusive possession of plot No. 3642, Badullah in plot No. 3643 and Ahadullah Sheikh and others were in possession in plot No. 3644 as a right of exchange and their names were mentioned in remark column in the khatian that there was an exchange in between Ahadullah Sheikh and Poilan Sheikh and Ahadullah Sheikh got the land of plot No. 3644; Rahamatullah and others filed Title Suit No. 184 of 1914 and in that suit Ahadullah Sheikh and others were defendant Nos. 1-3 and Poilan Sheikh and others were defendant Nos. 4-10 and they compromised by filing compromise petition separately and in that suit the exchange of Ahadullah Sheikh was admitted and the land Poilan Sheikh got, was admitted; the land which Poilan Sheikh got was again exchanged with Kutubullah Sheikh and others and transferred the land of plot No. 3644 to Heralal Datta by kabala dated 13-9-1927; on the same date, Heralal Datta transferred 1.20 acres of land by patta to Ismail Sheikh including the suit land; for arrears of rent, Heralal Datta filed Rent Suit No. 1782 of 1942 in the court of the then Munsif, 3rd Court, Khulna, the said suit was dismissed for non prosecution. It is further case of plaintiffs that Ismail Sheikh had title over the suit land of plot Nos. 3671 and 3670/4246 under CS khatian No. 2666 and the said land has been situated adjacent south-east side of the suit land; in the year 1954 AD Ismail Sheikh reconstructed the houses on the suit plot and also constructed more 3 rooms and those were tenanted and thereafter, he shifted his house on the land of plot Nos. 3671 and 2670/4246. In SA record the suit land was recorded in SA khatian No. 1015 and the tenant, defaulted to pay rent and Ismail Sheikh filed two SCC Suit being Nos. 108 of 1958 and 71 of 1059 and those were decreed. Momin Mollik also defaulted to pay rent and the landlord, Ismail Sheikh filed Money Suit No. 12 of 1960 and the suit was decreed. Momin Mollik filed Money Suit No. 34 of 1960 which was allowed and thereafter, defendant Nos. 1-6 got possession of the suit land and houses there on. Thereafter, Ismail Sheikh filed Title Suit No. 263 of 1966 which was transferred to the court of Sub-ordinate Judge, Additional Court, Khulna and the same was dismissed. Against which Ismail Sheikh filed Appeal from Original Decree No. 127 of 1976 before in the High Court Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh. The suit having running with formal defects, plaintiffs of that suit filed application for withdrawal of the suit with permission to sue afresh. The application was allowed on 7-4-1980. Before that date, the instant suit was filed on 13-3-1980. Momena Bibi and Jomiron Nessa transferred some decimals of land from plot No. 3643 along with other land to Heralal Datta by Kabala dated 9-6-1931 and thereafter, the said land was transferred to Paban Sheikh, son of Poilan Sheikh by a registered lease deed on 26-3-1942 and on that deed there was a statement that Ismail Sheikh is in possession on plot No. 3644 and adjacent west side of plot No. 3643. Title suit No. 208 of 1961 filed by heirs of Shahamatullah was dismissed and in that suit, right of Ismail Sheikh was admitted that the suit land was investigated. Title suit No. 33 of 1963 was filed by defendant Nos. 1-6, was dismissed for default, hence the suit. 

 5. Trial court dismissed the suit holding that plaintiffs failed to prove the factum of dispossession on 12-2-1962 and possession before that date; it has been proved that no exchange could be possible; the report of Commissioner in another suit cannot be treated as evidence of another suit without examining the Commissioner. Title Suit No. 263 of 1966 was filed on 16-5-1966 for khas possession and it was alleged that the plaintiffs were dispossessed on 12-6-1962 and thereafter the said suit was renumbered as Title Suit No. 65 of 1971 and when the matter was pending before the High Court Division and application for withdrawal of the suit to file afresh was filed on 11-3-1980 but though the instant suit was filed on 10-3-1980 but it will be treated that the suit was filed on 7-4-1980 and since the date of dispossession on 12-6-1962 the instant suit is barred by limitation. Appellate Court allowed the appeal and decreed the suit on the finding that the Commissioner's report was acceptable, that the suit is not barred by limitation. 

 9. While Title Suit No. 337 of 1963 was withdrawn on 7-4-1980 in allowing application for withdrawal filed in Appeal From Original Decree No. 127 of 1976 the High Court Division passed the order as:— 

 16. In the earlier suit, plaintiffs sought relief for declaration of title and for recovery of khas possession. Two suits are for two different district relief but cause of action has been shown as same. In earlier suit title by adverse possession was claimed but in the instant suit, recovery of khas possession has been sought for. Question is when plaintiffs were dispossessed. But curious enough that no fresh cause of action has been shown. Let us see the application for amendment of the plaint put forwarded before us by learned Advocate for the opposite parties, we may quote the relevant portion of the application of the amendment of the plaint which runs as follows:— 

 20. Judgment and decree passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Khulna decreeing Title Suit No. 200 of 1980 is set aside and those passed by the learned Sub-ordinate Judge, 1st Court, Khulna in title Suit No. 200 of 1980 is restored.

2. The short facts for disposal of the revisional application is that the petitioners as plaintiffs instituted Other Class Suit No. 8 of 1997 in the Court of the Assistant Judge, Madhupur for decree of permanent injunction against the defendant opposite parties restraining from disturbing their peaceful possession stating inter alia, that. the land of C.S. Plot no.4 1 1 under C.S. Khatian No. 155 corresponding to S.A. No. 276 of mouja Madhupur belonged to Roy Mohan Tepal who was succeeded by his son Kokaram Tapal. Kokaram Tepal sold entire plot No. 411 measuring 1.01 acres of land while exercising title and possession Manindra, Amarendra and Upendra Chandra Bhowmik by registered sale deed dated 25.2.1943. 

 3. Upendra Chandra Nath Bhowmik, Amarendra Nath and Mahendra Nath Bhowmik while exercising right title and possession sold the entire land or case plot No.41 1 and other land measuring 2.15 acres to the plaintiffs petitioners by 3 sale deeds dated 7.2.1965 handed over possession. The case land was correctly recorded in S.A. operation of 1962 in the names or the plaintiffs petitioners who have been in peaceful possession paying regular rent and taxes to the Government and other authorities. The plaintiffs have 4 residential houses in the case land with 25 dwelling huts. 

 4. The defendants have no title or any possession in the suit land but they threatened the plaintiffs for dispossession on 12-1-1997 hence they constrained to file the instant suit for permanent injunction against the defendants opposite parties. 

 5. The defendant nos. 1-2 and 4-6 contested the suit by filing written statements contending inter alia, that the plaintiffs suit was not maintainable and the plaintiffs have no title and interest in the suit land that the original owner Kokaram sold the entire 1.01 acres of land of suit plot no. 411 to Manindra, Upendra and Amerandra on 25.2.1943 and they appointed peari Mohan as constituted attorney and the said constituted attorney sold .12 decimals of land of case plot along with another 1.15 decimals to Mir Muksed Ali on 7.2.56 and said Moksed Ali being dead the defendant nos. 1-3 and 4 sold .01 decimals of land to defendant no. 6 and defendant nos. 4 and 5 sold .02 '/2 decimals to defendant no.6. In this way defendants have been possessing .12 decimals of case land the purchase of the plaintiffs are illegal and invalid and they cannot get decree in the suit and their suit is liable to be dismissed with costs. 

 8. The trial Court on perusal of the oral and documentary evidences of PWS and DWS was pleased to pass a decree in favour of the plaintiffs restraining the defendants from disturbing the plaintiffs in exercising their title and possession by judgment and decree dated 23.09.1998. 

 9. Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and decree of the trial Judge the defendants preferred Title Appeal before the District Judge and the same was heard and disposed of by the Subordinate Judge, Tangail and who by his Judgment and decree dated 11.11.1999 and 19.11.1999 respectively was pleased to allow the Appeal and set aside the judgment and decree of the trial Judge by his impugned Judgment and decree dated 11.11.1999 and 19.11.1999 respectively. 

 11. Dr. Md. Abul Basher, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners submits that petitioners prima facie proved their title, possession and interest over the suit land by adducing oral and documentary evidence in accordance with law. 

 12. He also submits that all the P.WS proved the title and possession over the suit land. 

 13. He next submits that the exhibited documents of the plaintiffs in respect of their title and possession clearly proved their title and possession over the suit land on the basis of the S.A. Khatian and subsequent Khatians. The rent receipts and other Taxes in the name of the plaintiffs also proved the title and possession of the plaintiffs in the suit property.

full_judgment:
2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the opposite party nos. 1 and 2 being plaintiff instituted the original Other Class Suit No. 68 of 2004 in the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Charfashion, Bhola for a declaration of permanent injunction and declaration contending inter alia, that the plaintiffs obtained the suit land by Settlement Case No. 806F/99-2000 followed by kabuliyat from the Government. Therefore, the plaintiffs erected house in plot NO. 3567 under khatian no. 587 and the remaining plot being no. 3690/1 and 3690/2 are cultivable land. The defendant no.1 took settlement of .40 acres of land in plot no. 3567 in Miscellaneous Case No. 42F/2000-2001 and the defendant no.2 took settlement of .20 acres of land in plot no. 3690 and .50 acres of land in plot no. 3567 in all .70 acres from the government collusively. The further case of the plaintiff is such that the defendants threatened the plaintiffs in the month of Chaitra 1490 B.S. at which the plaintiffs instituted the original suit. Subsequently the plaintiffs by filing an amendment petitioner challenging the settlement of the defendants and declaration of title with a further declaration that the order described in schedule “Kha” in respect of the land described in schedule “Ka” of the plaint is fraudulent, illegal and ineffective. 

 3. The contrary case of the defendants in short is thus that the properties measuring an area 1.50 acres of land is under khatian no. 318 and it is earlier plots were 1751/13, 1361/1and 1775/3 . The defendant no.1 for getting the land settlement from the government prayed for settlement and in settlement case No. 562A/69-70 he obtained settlement followed by a registered kabuliyat. The settlement khatian No. 18 was opened in favour of the defendant no.1 and possession was handed over. Subsequently the settlement holder defendant no.1 constructed his residence therein. The defendant no.2 in another settlement case no. 1366F/77-78 took settlement from settlement khatian no. 1296 for 1.50 acres of land under plot no. 496/1 and 558/1 . A separate khatian was opened in his name and possession was handed over. The further case of the defendant is such that .40 acres of land of plot no. 1775/3 under khatian no. 318 corresponds to Diara plot no. 1661/1and 1451/13 measuring 1.10 acres of land under khatian no. 3567 and .40 acres of land of plot no. 558/1 under khatian no. 1296 corresponds to Diara plot no. 5567 measuring an area .50 acres and .20 acres of land in plot no. 3690 comprising an area of .30 acres of land. The defendant no.1 after settlement filed a Miscellaneous Case No. 43F/2000-2001 before Assistant Commissioner (Land), Charfashion, Bhola opened khatian no. 581 in the name of the defendant no.1 which was approved by Deputy Commissioner, Bhola and the defendant no.2 after his settlement filed a file Miscellaneous Case No.30F/99-2000 before the same authority and the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Charfashion, Bhola opened khatian no. 584 in the name of defendant no.2 which was also approved by the Deputy Commissioner, Bhola. The plaintiff to the suit after granting a collusive khatian no. 587 in Dokar settlement case no. 806F/99-2000 tried to grave the property but in fact the settlement of the plaintiffs not at all affected by genuine transaction or delivery of possession. Knowing about the false settlement case the defendant applied to the Deputy Commissioner, Bhola for cancellation of the settlement of plaintiff no.1 on 12.02.2004 and thereafter after due enquiry and process of law the settlement of the plaintiffs were cancelled. The plaintiffs having no manner of right, title interest and possession in the suit land filed the suit on false allegation. 

 4. During trial original suit the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Charfashion, Bhola after taking evidence dismissed the suit on contest on 31.03.2008. Being aggrieved the plaintiffs preferred an appeal being Civil Appeal No.17 of 2008 in the Court of learned District Judge, Bhola which was heard and disposed of by the learned Joint District Judge, Court No.1 and Artharin Adalat, Bhola and the learned lower Appellate Court allowed the appeal reversing the judgment and dismissal decree the suit by the impugned judgment and decree dated 27.01.2010. 

 7. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the learned lower appellate court during passing the impugned judgment and decree committed gross illegality and irregularity resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate further submits that the learned appellate court below without considering the settlement cases marked exhibit-“Gha” (O) and “Cha” (Q) and evidence of P.W.1 the plaintiffs in holding that the plaintiffopposite parties obtained settlement for the suit land earlier to the defendant, committed error of law and misconstrued the facts of the case. The defendant-petitioners obtained settlement of the suit land in the year 1969-70 and in the year 1977-78 vide exhibit-“Ga” and “Chha” (R) while the plaintiffopposite parties got settlement in the year 1999-2000 vide Annexure-“Ja”. Therefore, obviously after the settlement of the defendants the plaintiffs obtained the settlement which is no doubt Dokar settlement in favour of the plaintiffs. But the learned appellate court below erroneously held hat the plaintiffs to the case obtained settlement prior to the defendant which is apparently an error of law resulting in an error in the decision. The learned Advocate also submits that the plaintiffs-opposite parties in settlement case no. 806F/99-2000 obtained settlement as alleged which was fraudulent, collusive and not acted upon. The findings of the trial court not at all rebutted or reverse by the appellate court below after assessment of the evidence and appreciation of law. Without discussing the evidence on record properly in its true perspective and without reversing the observation and findings of the trial court especially on the point of possession the learned appellate court below committed gross illegality which is violative to the provisions laid down in Order XLI rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The impugned judgment and decree is not a proper judgment of reversal in as much as without discussing the evidence on record and reversing the findings of the trial court the learned Joint District Judge, Bhola decided the merit of the case arbitrarily and thereby in decreeing the suit there has been miscarriage of justice. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the decision of the trial court on possession over the suit land is based on the deposition of the witnesses adduced from the cites of the respective parties which is not at all considered by the trial lower appellate court and there is total non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. There is no rent receipt from the side of the plaintiffs from 2000-2004 which has cast a serious doubt in believing the plaintiffs case, especially on their alleged possession after their alleged settlement. In this context; it is clear findings of the trial Court that the plaintiffs have totally failed to prove their prima-facie title and possession to the suit land and this decision was passed on preponderance of evidence and scanning of the deposition given by both the parties. The said observation and decision of the learned Assistant Judge, Charfashion, Bhola is not rebutted referring evidence of the parties which has resulted in an error in the decision. In view of the facts and circumstances of the case the learned Appellate Court below is misconceived in holding that the burden of proof in proving the respective case of the plaintiffs is shifted to the shoulder of the defendants. The original suit as it was found is not maintainable and there is a specific remedy lies upon the respective parties in the Bangladesh Bhumy Babosthapona Manual, 1990 (বাংলাদেশ ভূমি ব্যবস্থাপনা ম্যানুয়্যাল, ১৯৯০). Under Section 67 of the said manual reads as follows: 

 8. Apparently the matter in dispute lies on settlement which is guided by the special provisions laid down in the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. Under section 76 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 “No Civil Court shall entertain any application or suit concerning any matter relating to the settlement and 76(2) of the aforesaid Act is a barring Clause upon the Civil Court to entertain such dispute. In this regard the learned Advocate Mr. H.S. Deb Brahman has referred several decisions of our Apex Court including the BAR Act. In the instant case without existing the provisions which are expressly provided in the relevant law the plaintiffs to the suit instituted the original suit which is apparently barred by law. 

 9. As against the aforesaid submission advanced from the side of the learned counsel for the petitioners the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties opposing the Rule submits that the learned appellate court below committed no illegality or irregularity in deciding the merit of the appeal in favour of the defendant-appellant and during disposal of the appeal the learned lower appellate court after considering all the evidence adduced from the sides of the respective parties and on proper sift of evidence in appreciation of law decided the merit of the appeal and reversed the judgment and dismissal decree passed by the trial court. The learned Advocate further submits that the settlement of the defendants as it appears from the face of the papers suffers from non service of notice as malafide act of the concern officials and based on fraudulent activities and the learned appellate court below during disposal of the appeal rightly held that the defendants settlement is liable to be decreed illegal and in absence of tangible evidence from the side of the defendants it cannot be held that they acquired any right, title, interest and possession over the suit land. The learned Advocate further submits that the case nathi which was called for by the defendants during trial of the original suit go to show that their exhibit-Kha does not tally with the report of the concern ‘kanongo’ dated 04.01.2004 for which the settlement of the plaintiffs were cancelled. Under section 67 of the Bangladesh Bhumy Babosthapona Manual, 1990 (বাংলাদেশ ভূমি ব্যবস্থাপনা ম্যানুয়্যাল, ১৯৯০) the reason for which a settlement can be cancelled is totally absent in the instant case but the authority concern illegally being guided by undue influence cancelled the settlement of the plaintiffs which is a malafide act of the government official and for that for the reason stated above the plaintiffs instituted the original suit for getting proper relief from the court of law. The learned Advocate Mr. Swapan Kumar Dutta also submits that there is nothing in the concerned nathi of settlement that the present plaintiffs were ever notified before cancellation of their settlement which was mandatory before drawing any such inference that the settlement is illegal or Dokar as alleged. The learned Advocate for the opposite parties referred from the judgment of the appellate court below read as follows : 

 10. The learned Advocate after citing several decisions of this court and our Apex Court submits that under section 9 of the Civil Procedure Court a Civil Court is quite competent to entertain the original suit and the learned appellate court below after thorough discussions over the evidence on record passed the impugned judgment and decree which deserve no interference of this court in absence of misreading or non-reading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error occasioning failure of justice. 

 13. On perusal of the case record it transpires that during pendency of the original suit the plaintiffs filed an application for declaration of title and also for a declaration that the order of cancellation of his settlement dated 24.06.2004 by the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Charfashion, Bhola is illegal, fraudulent and not acted upon. The said amendment petition was filed under the purview of Order VI rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure. During trial of the original suit four witnesses were adduced from the side of the plaintiffs and three witnesses were examined from the sides of the defendants. The learned Assistant Judge, Charfashion, Bhola during disposal of the original suit after framing six different issues decided that the plaintiffs to the suit after adducing credible, tangible evidence failed to discharge their onus in proving their prima-facie title and possession in the disputed property and also failed to establish that the settlement in favour of the defendants was false and not acted upon. The learned appellate court below in his findings observed that the plaintiffs’ title to the suit land has been denied by the defendants by virtue of their settlement and the evidence which was laid from the side of the defendants does not prove their bonafide and disprove the respective plea of the plaintiffs to the suit land. It was further observed by the lower appellate court the land in dispute is not identical with the settlement papers and the defendants since not filed any plot index or any Commission was held by a survey knowing Advocate Commissioner the land relates to the paper of settlements suffers from vagueness. 

 14. In this regard it was argued from the side of the learned counsel for the petitioners that it was an incumbent duty as well as onus upon the plaintiffs to investigate the land or specify the land in the schedule and for the removal of alleged vagueness or un specification it is the plaintiff who is required to hold Commission to establish their case and the plaintiffs to the suit because of their institution of the original suit must have to prove their case beyond all reasonable doubt and it is the established principle of civil law that the plaintiffs must prove their case and they cannot banked upon weakness of their adversary. 

 21. The jurisdiction of Civil Court in the instant case has been expressly barred under section 76 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and a bear reading of the section itself shows that the jurisdiction of Civil Court has been curtail from entertaining any suit or application against any order passed or any action taken under this law. Apparently in the instant case without exhausting the specified forum as provided the plaintiffs instituted the original suit and I have already there earlier that the Civil Court was not empowered to entertain the original suit and the matter in controversy which is apparently such a dispute which arise out from a settlement granted by the government and it subsequent cancellation of earlier settlements granted in favour of the plaintiff-opposite-parties. The facts remains that the allegation on fraud, malafide practice and non service of notice can be agitated in appropriate forum and in this regard the arguments advanced from the side of the learned counsel for the petitioners that the plaintiffs to the suit not at all raised such plea in their pleading is consistent with the plaint itself. Under Order VI rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure,

 of the suit.  21. On going to the materials on record it is found that it is almost admitted that the land of RS khatian no.35 and 36 originally belonged to Akiluddin Molla, the predecessor of the plaintiffs. But the case of the plaintiffs is that Akiluddin Molla did never settle the suit land to Nazir Sheikh while the case of the contesting defendant nos. 1-5 and 7-16 is that Akiluddin Molla orally settled the suit land in the first part of Boishakh 1354 BS to Nazir Sheikh, the predecessor of these of defendants and took rents from the Nazir Sheikh executing the dakhila on 30, Baishak of [354 BS. 

 23. The trial Court and the appellate Court below concurrently found that the right, title and interest which was available in favour of Akiluddin Molla at the time of preparation of RS record of right has not been extinguished in any way and both the Courts below also concurrently found that Akiluddin Molla did never settle the suit land to Nazir Sheikh nor exchanged with Ansaruddin Mona.  " From the above findings, it appears that the appellate Court below found the right, title and interest of the plaintiffs into the suit land. Noor Mohammad, 36 DLR(AD) 261 it has been held that the findings of the Courts below on the basis of no evidence is of no legal consequence and the finding, of the Courts below could be disturbed if there is any misreading of the evidence or misconstruction of the evidence. In the case of 16 BLD (AD) 197 it has been held that the revisional Court may interfere in the concurrent findings of the facts of the Courts below when there appears misreading of evidence, wrong appreciation of evidence, non-consideration of oral and documentary evidence by the Courts below and when the findings of the Courts below are found to be perverse and not based on the evidence on record which resulted in to an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. In the Case of Abdul Gafur Vs. Md. Abdur Razzak 62 DLR (AD) 242 it was held that the revisional Court cannot reverse the concurrent findings of the Courts below based on proper appreciation of the evidence on record. 

 24. Now, the preponderant views emerged from the above referred decisions is that if the concurrent findings of the Courts below are based on proper appreciation of the evidence on record, the some cannot be disturbed, but if the concurrent findings are based on the misreading of evidence, wrong appreciation of evidence and non-consideration of oral and documentary evidence by the Courts below, the findings and decisions of the Courts below can be disturbed.  27. The appellate Court below though found the title of the plaintiffs into the suit land but ultimately dismissed the suit holding that the plaintiffs have no possession into the suit and and the plaintiffs did not challenge the decree of title suit no.629 of 1981.

 PW3 Sheikh Khali! testified that he has homestead contiguous to the suit land and plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land. From the cross-examination of the defendants it appears that PW3 is the relation of the defendants but their appears no suggestion that for any internal clique or for any other reason he has deposed falsely. Since the PW3 is also a contiguous land holder of the suit land, so he is a competent witness to depose as to the possession of the parties into suit land. From the materials on record it appears that both the P.Ws 2 and 3 are independent and disinterested witnesses and there appears no earthly reason to disbelieve them or to discard their unblemished and noted evidence in the Court. Since the title of the plaintiffs were found into the suit land, so the evidence of PWs 2 and 3 as to their possession into the suit land is consistent with the findings of the title of the plaintiffs. In this regard I can also rely upon the decision of the case of Erfan Ali Vs Joynal Abedin Mia, 35 DLR (AD) 217, where in it has been held that possession generally follows the title. The title of the plaintiffs were concurrently found by the Courts below, so the legitimate, rational and judicious conclusion would be that the plaintiff have been possessing the suit land pursuant to their such title.

 35. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. parties:
Mosammat Shahida Alam ------ Petitioner
Vs.

full_judgment:
Hasan Foez Siddique J.: This Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1781 of 2009 is directed against the judgment and order dated 26.04.2009 passed in Civil Revision No. 4248 of 2004 by a Single Bench of the High Court Division discharging the Rule affirming the judgment and decree dated 25.07.2004 passed in Title Appeal No. 63 of 2004 by the Joint District Judge, Arbitration Court, Dhaka reversing those dated 01.12.2003 passed by the Assistant Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 122 of 1997. 

 2. The relevant facts for the disposal of this petition, in short, are that the plaintiff petitioner instituted the aforesaid suit for declaration of her title and recovery of khas possession, inter-alia, stating that the land appertaining to C.S. khatian No. 470 originally belonged to Mahin Chandra Bhoumick who died leaving four Sons namely, Shrish Chandra Bhoumick, Satish Chandra Bhoumick, Ganesh Chandra Bhoumick and Gayanendra Chandra Bhoumick. Shirish Chandra Bhoumick died leaving his wife Shib Sundari Devi and son Bivutirana. Satish Chandra Bhoumick died leaving wife Hiranbala Devi and three sons, Kartik, Ganesh and Ramendra. Gayanendra died leaving his son Upendra. They transferred 3.47 acres of land to Ismail by kabala deed dated 23.07.55. The land measuring 2.01 acres of Plot No. 740 and 1042 acres of Plot No. 741 of C.S. khatian No. 470 were acquired by the Government in L.A. Case no. 91/1957-58. Ismail died leaving his son Janoruddin and others. Janoruddin transferred .03/(3⁄10) acre of land from Plot No. 741 to Jamila Khatun by deed dated 13.03.70. Jamila Khatun died leaving her husband Haider Ali, son Saidul and daughters Anowara Begum, Runu Begum, Junu, Hasina and Shilpi. Getting permission to sell the said land in Miscellaneous Case No. 1245 of 1979 Haider Ali and others transferred the said land to the plaintiff Shahida Alam by a kabala deed dated 24.11.1979. She mutated her name in the khatian in respect of the said .03/(3⁄10) acre of land and paid rent to the Government. She constructed boundary wall surrounding the suit land and had been in possession through Anowar Hossain. On 07.06.1996, Anowar Hossain informed the plaintiff that some persons had been trying to construct dwelling hut in the suit land. The plaintiff made a G.D. with local Police Station. The Police issued notice to the persons who made attempt to dispossess the plaintiff and directed the parties to be present in the local Police Station. Thus, the defendants became furious. Then the Officer-in-Charge of the Police Station asked the plaintiff to take shelter in the Court. Hence, is the suit. 

 4. The trial Court considering the materials on record decreed the suit. Then the defendant No. 6 preferred Title Appeal No. 63 of 2004 in the Court of District Judge, Dhaka and the said appeal was heard by the Joint District Judge, Arbitration Court, Dhaka who by his judgment and decree dated 25.07.2004 allowed the appeal and dismissed the suit upon setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial court. The petitioner then filed Civil Revision No. 4248 of 2004 in the High Court Division and a Single Judge of the High Court Division by his judgment and order dated 26.04.2009 discharged the said Rule. However, the High Court Division found the title of the plaintiff in the suit land and observed that the plaintiff is required to file a suit for partition. 

 7. It appears from the judgment and order that on consideration of the materials on record the High Court Division found the plaintiff’s title in the suit land but held that the plaintiff purchased the suit land but held that the plaintiff purchased the suit land from a plot having 1.43 acres of land and she did not give description of the land giving sketch map in the schedule of the plaint, so it is difficult to find out the exact position of the suit land. Since the plaintiff and contesting defendant purchased the land from the successive heirs of Ismail Hossain and the suit land is a portion of a big plot having 1.43 acres of land, we are of the view that the High Court Division rightly held that the proper remedy of the petitioner is lying in a suit for partition. It is relevant here to observe that the High Court Division found the title of the plaintiff in the suit land and the contesting defendant did not raise any objection against such finding in the higher forum.

predecessor of opposite party nos. 1-7 and 1 I as plaintiff filed Other Suit no. 28 of 1992. subsequently, the same was renumbered as Other Suit no. 174 of 1992 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Banskhali, Chittagong for declaration of her title.
