 6. The suit was contested by 3 sets of defendants. The defendant nos. 1/3, 5 and 6/7 filing 3 separate written statements contested in the suit. Though they have filed separate written statement, but their case appears to be similar with each other. The common case of the defendants may be narrated as that the suit is not maintainable in its present from, the plaintiffs have no right, title and interest into the suit land, the substituted plaintiffs have long-standing enmity with the defendants and those substituted plaintiffs in order to cause harm to the defendants field the original suit using the name of their grand mother Kamini Bala Das. 

 7. The further case of the defendants are that the suit land originally belonged to Mohendra Chandra Acharja who met with a prematured death leaving two sons Pran Hari Acharja and Sree Hari Acharja and wife Sarat Kumar Acharja. Sarat Kumar Acharja in order to pay the loan and also for some other legal necessity created a benami transaction dated 23.03.1925 in the name of Joy Kumar. But Sarat Kumar Acharja as the mother of minor sons had no legal capacity to execute and register the said deed. Sarat Kumar Acharja did not seek permission from the learned District Judge or such execution. As such, the deed of the settlement dated 23.03.1925 was an illegal document. But for the said deed of patta the continuous possession of Pran Hari Acharja and Sree Hari Achat ja has not been affected. Since Pran Hari Achaija and Sree Hari Acharja were minors at the time of R.S record of right, Joy Kumar using the said opportunity got the said land recorded in his name. But at the attaining majority Pran Hari Acharja and Sree Hari Achaija raised objection against the deed of patta dated 23.03.1925 and Joy Kumar being convinced that ultimately the patta will not stand executed and registered a deed of relinquishment dated 11.04.1933 in favour of them. 

 9. The P.S khatian of the suit land is wrong which had just followed the R.S khatian. At the time of preparation of B.S. record of right, the defendants could not show their title deeds to the concerned officer, as such, though their possession into the suit land has been recorded but their names were not recorded in the columns of tenants. The plaintiffs have tiled a false suit and they are not entitled to get any relief in the suit and the suit is liable to be dismissed with costs. 

 10. Upon the above pleadings the trial Court framed as many as four issues to dispose of the suit at trial. The plaintiffs examined two witnesses and filed some documentary evidences that have been marked as exhibits. The defendants examined 6 witnesses in all and filed some documentary evidences duly marked as exhibits. The trial Court considering the evidences and other materials on record dismissed the suit holding that though Joy Kumar had acquired the suit land through the settlement dated 13.03.1925 but Joy Kumar relinquished his title in favour of Fran Hari Acharja and Sree Hari Acharja executing and registering a deed of Mukti-patra or Nadabi-patra dated 11 .04.1933. 

 11. The plaintiffs of the original suit against the said verdict of the trial Court filed Title Appeal being no. 492 of 1994 in the Court of District Judge, Chittagong which has been ultimately heard by the learned Joint District Judge, Patiya, Chittagong, who by his impugned judgment and decree dated 26.04.2006 reversing those of the judgment and decree of the trial Court came to a conclusion that through the deed of relinquishment dated 11.04.1933 the title which was acquired by Joy Kumar has not gone in favour of Pran Hari Acharja and Sree Hari Acharja and ultimately he decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiffs. The defendant-petitioners being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said judgment and decree moved this Court and obtained the present Rule. 

 12. Mr. Probir Neogi along with Mr. Hassan M.S. Azim, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners supporting the Rule submits that the trial Court on the right assessment of the evidence and on the right evaluation of the facts of the case came to a very fair conclusion that through the deed of relinquishment dated 11.04.1933 Joy Kumar had lost his title and interest into the suit land. But the appellate Court below very erroneously found that through the deed of relinquishment dated 11.04.1933 Pran Hari Acharja and Sree Hari Acharja did not acquire title in to the suit land. The appellate Court below wrongly relied upon the decision of 19 DLR 33 but he has failed to take notice of the fact that though in the reported case it was held that Mukti-patra can never create title to any party unless it is supported by a registered deed of transfer but by the subsequent development that decision has been overruled by the Appellate Division. 

 13. He referring the case of Government of Bangladesh-vs-Aziz Molla being dead his heirs Md. Mozibur Rahman and others reported in 44 DLR (AD) 90 submits that such type of deed whatever they are named like Nadabi-patra or Mukti-patra etcetera ultimately confers title to the recipient of the deed. But the appellate Court below without noticing the development of the law in respect of the Mukti-patra and Nadabi patra as the case may be came to a very wrong conclusion resulted into an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice to the defendant-petitioners. 

 14. He further submits that in fact in this Rule the main points to be considered by this Court whether by the deed of relinquishment dated 11.04.1933 the land was again gone back to Pran Hari Acharja and Sree Hari Acharja or-not and since our Apex Court in the reported case held that by such type of deed of release or nadabi patra the recipient will acquire title and possession in the suit land. So, Pran Hari Acharja and Sree Hari Acharja got the land back in 1933 and in exercise of their such ownership they have settled the land on the same date to Pali Mohon Das, Sukumar Das and Lalit Mohon and from them the present defendants acquired the suit land. 

 16. On the other hand, Mr. H. S. Deb Brahman, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-opposite party nos. 1-7 opposing the Rule very strenuously r submits that Joy Kumar acquired the land through patta from Sarat Kumar Acharja on 23.03.1925 and on the basis of the said settlement the land was recorded correctly in the R.S record' of right in the name of Joy Kumar. But Joy kumar did never return back the said land in favour of Pran Hari Acharja and Sree Had Acharja as claimed by the defendants. Had, there been any such relinquishment in favour of Pran Hari Acharja and Sree Hari Acharja by Joy Kumar that would have been reflected in the subsequent records of right particularly in P.S and B.S records of right. In both the subsequent records of right the land was correctly recorded in the name of Kamini Bala Das, the wife of Joy Kumar who was the original plaintiff of the suit. The defendants did not challenge the R.S and P.S records of right at any point of time though they had the ample opportunity for the same. 

 18. He further submits that in the written statement the possession of Kamini Bala Das has been admitted and it surely indicates that Kamini Bala Das was never ousted from the suit land and the possession of Kamini Bala Das has been considered from the date of patta on 23.03.1925'. But the trial Court on the misconception of law very illegally dismissed the suit. The appellate Court below rightly held that .by the Mukti-patra dated 11.04.1933 no title was conferred to Pran Hari Achada and Sree Hari Acharja. The appellate Court below on the right assessment of the oral and documentary evidence decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiffs which does not call for any interference from this Court. So, the Rule is liable' to be discharged with costs. 

 21. The trial Court though without any reference of law or precedent of the higher Court simply came into a conclusion that by the deed of said Mukti-patra exhibit-Ka, the right, title and interest which was available in favour of Joy Kumar had gone to Pran Haig Acharja and Sree Hari Acharja. As such, neither Kamini Bala I) as nor his grand sons who became the plaintiffs on her death 'acquired nothing in to the suit land. 

 22. But from the judgment of the appellate Court below it is found that the appellate Court below relying on the decision of 19 DLR 33 found that by the deed of Mukti-patra, Pran Hari Acharja and Sree Hari Acharja acquired nothing into the suit land. In the case of Bangladesh-vs-Aziz Molla being dead his heirs Md. Molibur Rahman and others reported in 44 DLR (AD) 90 it was held that by a Muktinama or Mukti-patta the -title and interest confers upon the recipient of the Mukti-patra or Mukti-nama as the case may be and in that case the case of Abdul Gafur Sander and others-vs-Wazedali Talukdar and another reported in 19 DLR 33 was also considered by the Appellate Division. 

 23. The Appellate Division hi answering the question whether the recipient of a Mukti-nama and Mitkti-patra will acquire title into the land through the said Mukti-nama and Mukti-patra considered the decisions of the numerous eases of Indian jurisdiction. It will he beneficial for all of us if the valuable observations and findings made in the said case (para 7 to 13) are reproduced here, which runs as follows: 

 After considering aforementioned cases in Thayil Manno and another- Vs-Kottiath Ramunni and others; AIR 1966(SC) 337 the Indian Supreme Court held that those cases do not lay down a proposition of universal application that a deed styled as a deed of release cannot operate as a conveyance. It further noted Hemendra Nath Mukedi-vs-Kumar Nath Roy, 12 CWN 478. In that case it was held that by a registered deed or disclaimer the executants relinquished all their right, title and interest and claim in the properties in favour of the release upon the condition that the release would discharge certain debts and the executants would be under no liberty to pay those debts. Maclean, CJ held that the deed or release, on its true construction, was a transfer though it was stamped only as a release and not with ad valorem stamp. 

 "We think that a registered instrument styled a release deed releasing the right, title and interest of the executant in any property in favour of the releasee for valuable consideration may operate as a conveyance, if the document clearly discloses an intention to effect a transfer. 

 This principle was extended in Kuppuswami Chettair-Vs-ASPA Arumugam Chettiar and another AIR 1967(SC) 1395, to a registered instrument of release executed without any consideration. After considering that under section 123 of the Transfer of property Act, 1882, a gift may be effected by a registered instrument signed by or on behalf of the doper and attested by at least two witnesses, it was held that a registered instrument releasing the right, title and interest of the releasor without consideration may operate as a transfer by way of a gift, if the document clearly shows an intention to effect the transfer and is signed by or on behalf of the releasor and attested by at least two witnesses. 

 26. The learned Advocate for the plaintiff-opposite parties put much emphasis on the record of right. It is fact that the R.S record of right stands in the name of-Joy Kumar. It is pertinent to point out here that in between 1925 to 1933 Joy Kumar was exercising his right, title and interest into the suit land and that was the time when the R.S record of right was prepared in that particular locality. So, in that view of the matter, there appears no harm and wrong in recording the name of Joy Kumar in R.S record of right of the suit land and it is known to us that at the time of preparation of P.S khatian or S.A khatian after the acquisition of rent receiving interest by the Government, the S.A record of right was prepared relying on the previous record of right and in that view of the matter it is very much natural and probable that the P.S or S.A record of right will be prepared in the name of,/ Joy Kumar as R.S record of right stands in his name. 

 27. In the written statement of the defendant nos. 1-3 they have admitted that Kamini Bala Das being their relation and since she had no any financial capacity she was allowed to stay into the suit land during her life time. This sorts of statement though indicates the possession of Kamini Bala Das into the suit land but at the same time it was stated in the written statement that she was given a simple shelter into the suit land. I find nothing in the suit as a whole that after the deed of relinquishment dated 11.04.1933 the Joy Dr. Kumar or the plaintiffs had exercised their right, title and interest into the suit land. 

 28. Having regards to the above discussion I find that the appellate Court below not justified In holding that the Mukti-patra or Mukti-nama did not confer any title to its recipient in fact he without taking into the notice of the case of 44 DLR(AD) 90 came into a wrong conclusion committing an error of law resulted into an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice to the defendants-petitioners. So, the judgment and decree of the appellate Court below are liable to be set aside.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1030 of 2009
parties:
S. Golam Mostafa ------ Petitioner
Vs.
The Narayangonj District Council, District: Narayangonj and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Muhammad Imman Ali J. This civil petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 13.01.2009 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2987 of 2004 making the Rule absolute and thereby reversing the judgment and decree dated 06.04.2004 passed by the Additional District Judge, First Court, Narayangonj in Title Appeal No. 39 of 2003 allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and decree dated 10.03.2003 passed by the Joint District Judge, Narayangonj in Title Suit No. 102 of 1999 dismissing the suit. 

 2. The facts of the case, in brief, are that the petitioner-plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 102 of 1999 before the Court of Joint District Judge, First Court, Narayangonj seeking declaration of title, confirmation of possession and recovery of khas possession in the suit land measuring an area of 21 decimals as shown in the 'Ka' schedule land to the plaint and also to the structures as shown in the "Kha" and "Ga" schedule land to the plaint appertaining to C.S. Khatian No. 189 and S.A. Khatian No. 47, Poura Fielding No. 210/1, Bangabandhu Sarak, Police Station Narayangonj Sadar. The plaintiff contended, inter alia, that Harun Bepari was the, owner and possessor of the said land and accordingly it was recorded in C.S. Khatian No. 48 in his name; that said Damn Bepari published a public notice in the daily Ittefaq dated 07.01.1978 forming the said land. Thereafter, the plaintiff purchased the said land by sub-kabala deed dated 23.01.1978 and acquired title in the "Ka" schedule land to the plaint, filled up the land with earth, constructed some structures upon the said land and let out the same to his sister, the defendant No. 3 and started possessing the suit land and structure through tenants and also by himself. A dispute arose between the plaintiff and the defendant No. 2 in respect of title of the suit land and the plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 174 of 1981. That suit was dismissed by judgment and decree dated 12.05.1983. Thereafter, the plaintiff purchased the suit land again from the defendants No. 4 and 5 by two registered kabala deeds dated 06.06.1983 and 21.06.1983. The defendant No. 3 entered into a portion of the suit premises on 01.07.1978 by executing an agreement and thereafter he refused to pay rent whereupon the plaintiff instituted SCC Suit No. 28 of 1984 for evicting the defendant No. 3. The plaintiff in the instant suit prayed for declaration of title to the "Ka" schedule land to the plaint and confirmation of possession of the "Kha" schedule structure on the suit land and recovery of khas possession to "Ga" schedule structure on the suit land. 

 3. The defendant No. 2, Narayangonj Jila Parishad contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that the suit was not maintainable as it stands framed. It was claimed that 12 decimals of land out of the suit land was acquired by the Government vide LA. Case No.  of 1935-36 and thereafter .054 acre of land was acquired for the development   of Dhaka-Narayangonj Road. Thereafter, the land was leased out by defendant No. 2 to defendant No. 3 who is in possession of the suit land. The plaintiff previously instituted two suits against the defendants, and having lost those has filed the instant suit. The plaintiff has no right, title, interest and possession in the suit property and there was no cause of action to file the suit and the suit was not maintanable in its present form and manner. Hence, the suit was liable to be dismissed. 

 5. Being aggrieved by the judgment and, decree of the trial Court, the plaintiff preferred Title Appeal No. 39 of 2003. The said appeal was heard by the Additional District Judge, First Court, Narayangonj, who by the judgment and decree dated 06.04.2004 allowed the appeal and decreed the suit upon setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court. 

 10. We note from the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division that observation was made to the effect that the earlier Title Suit No. 174 of 1981 (marked as -Ext."Ka" in the suit) was also filed seeking a declaration of title in the suit land and structures raised upon holding No. 210/1 of Narayangonj Municipality, Plot No.  28/961 corresponding to schedule-`Ka', `Kha' and 'Ga' land of the plaint. It was further observed that the plaintiff of the earlier suit is the plaintiff of the instant suit. In the earlier suit the Zilla Board Narayangonj as defendant produced the; order sheets of the aforementioned L.A. case marked as Exts. 'A', 'B' and 'C' and gazette notification was marked as Ext. D. The trial Court in that suit came to a denied finding that the original owner received compensation in the said L.A. ease and declared that no title passed in favour of the plaintiff on the strength of kobala deed dated 23.01.1978. No appeal was preferred against the dismissal of the said suit. The High Court Division also observed that the instant suit was filed on the strength of two subsequent kobala deeds dated 06.06.1983 and 21.06.1983 (Exts. 11 and 12) from Nazimuddin, son of late Abdul Gafur alleging the executants to be the grandson of Harun Bepari. The High Court Division observed that the compensation in L.A. Case No.  of 1935-36 was in the name of two sons of Harm Bepari, namely Sirajuddin and Tafizuddin and that fact was affirmed in the earlier title suit and therefore the plaintiff could not make out a case of alleged purchase from the heirs of Harun Bepari. The High Court Division observed that so long Ext. 'Ka' stands, the plaintiff is estopped from claiming any title in the suit land through the heirs of Harun Bepari inasmuch as in the previously instituted suit, the Court believed payment of compensation to the sons of Harun Bepari. 

 11. As the suit land is common in both Title Suit No. 174 of 1981 as well as in the instant suit and the plaintiff claimed title through the heirs of Harun Bepari and since the earlier suit was dismissed on contest and the issue relating to right, title and possession is the same, the instant suit is clearly barred by the doctrine of a res judicata.
case_type_name: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal

parties:
Badsha Hawlader (Md.) ------ Plaintiff-Petitioner
VS.
SM Kamaluddin and others   ------ Defendants-Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule on an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure at the instance of the plaintiff-petitioner was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1-5 to show cause as to why the order dated 22-3-1998 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Fultala, Khulna in Title suit No. 35 of 1997 should not be set-aside and or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule, in short, is that the present petitioner as plaintiff instituted Title Suit being No. 25 of 1995 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Fultala, Khulna for specific performance of contract against the opposite party Nos. 6-11 contending, inter alia, that late Abdur Rashid Molla, the predecessor in interest of the opposite party Nos. 6-10 being owner and possessor of 0.73 acres of land appertaining to CS plot Nos. 1939 and 1940 recorded in CS khatian Nos. 1996 and 1998 of Baniakhamar mouza of Khulna Police Station had entered into an agreement to sale 0.085 acres of land to the plaintiff at a consideration of Taka 50,000 and on receipt of an advance of Taka 20,000 executed a bainaparta on 8-2-1986 and thereafter took Taka 25,000 on 13-4-1986 and extended the time for execution and registration of the sale deed for a long period on the ground of pendency of a title suit. Subsequently Abdur Rashid Molla died leaving the present opposite party Nos. 6-10 as his heirs who ultimately refused to execute and register the sale deed on 20-3-1995. 

 3. The said suit was transferred in the Court of Assistant Judge, Fultala and renumbered as Title Suit No. 35 of 1997. On 11-2-1998 the opposite party Nos. 1-5 appearing in the Court below filed an application for impleading them as defendants in the suit averring inter-alia that the suit land originally belonged to one Girl. Bala Debi who got decree in Title Appeal No. 6 of 1958 arising out of Title Suit No. 342 of 1956. Giri Bala died leaving her brother Horimohan as her only heir and Horimohan while was in possession of the said land sold the same to them and 4 others by registered kabala deeds keeping a small portion in his khash. The petitioners and Horimohan jointly filed Title suit No. 701 of 1979 against Abdur Rashid Molla and the said suit was decreed on 30-7-1994. Abdur Rashid Molla had no title and possession in the suit land as such his heirs inherited nothing from him. Abdur Rashid Molla did not execute any bainapatra in favour of the plaintiff and after the death of Abdur Rashid Molla, the plaintiff in collusion with some other interested quarters created ante dated bainaparta with the forged signature. The petitioners having title into the suit land are the necessary party in the suit to protect their interest. 

 5. Mr AKM Alamgir Parvez Bhuiyan for Mrs Purabi Rani Sharma, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner supports the Rule. He submits that the original suit being a suit for specific performance of contract on the basis of a bainapatra dated 8-2-1986 taken place between Abdur Rashid Mollah and the plaintiff, the executant Abdur Rashid Molla or his heirs are the only necessary party in such a suit. He further submits that in a suit like this the only point for determination, is that whether the executant executed the bainapatra in favour of the plaintiff, so other than the executant of the bainapatra no other is necessary party but the Court below ignoring the cardinal principle of such a suit very illegally added the opposite party Nos. 1-5 in the suit as defendants. So, the impugned order is liable to be set-aside making the Rule absolute. 

 6. Mr Probir Haider, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party Nos. 1-5 opposing the Rule strenuously submits that it is fact that in a suit for specific performance of contract generally the necessary parties are those who executed the bainapatra or his heirs in interest as the case may be and though in this particular case the opposite party Nos. 1-5 are not the executants of the bainapatra dated 8-2-1986 but Abdur Rashid Molla who executed the bainapatra in favour of the plaintiff claiming the ownership in the land in question had no title and possession into the suit land. In a former Title Suit being No. 701 of 1979, the title of the present opposite party No. 1-5 along with Horimohan was declared against Abdur Rashid Molla in his presence. So, under the above facts and circumstances the presence of the present petitioners in the present suit was inevitable for an effective and complete justice in the suit and the Court below considering the said facts and circumstances allowed the petitioners to be added as defendants in the suit. So, the impugned order does not call for interference from this Court and the Court below did not commit any illegality occasioning failure of justice to the plaintiff-petitioner. So, the Rule is liable to be discharged with costs. 

 8. On going to the materials on record it appears that Abdur Rashid Molla claiming title and possession into the suit land had entered into a bainapatra to sell 0.085 acres of land to the plaintiff and after his death his heirs the present opposite party Nos. 6-10 denied to exe-cute and register a sale deed pursuant to the said bainapatra and ultimately the said fact rises the present suit. From the impugned order of the Court below it appears that the trial Court was very much conscious and aware about the scope and limit of a suit for specific performance of contract. The Court below categorically observed that in a suit for specific performance of contract, the prime duty of the Court to scrutinize whether there was a contract between the plaintiff and the defendants but even then since the petitioners got a decree for the suit land before filing of the present suit, the presence of the petitioners will facilitate the scope to have an effective and complete justice in the suit and he also observed that if the opposite party Nos. 1-5 are not allowed to be added as defendants in the original suit that may be the cause of more suit among the par-ties. I find it difficult to show any disagreement with the findings and observations of the Court below. 

 9. It is fact that in a suit for specific performance of contract normally the parties to the contract are necessary parties but there may be case and exception to this normal principle that where the persons claim title over the suit land backed by strong instruments are considered as necessary parties to the suit. The case in my hands go to show that the title of the opposite party Nos. 1-5 were declared by a competent civil Court before filing of the present suit. Having regards to those facts, the opposite party Nos. 1-5 appears to be necessary parties in the suit for an effective and complete justice in the litigation among the parties. The Court below considering these all aspects of the suit allowed the petition of opposite party Nos. 1-5 with the following observations: 

 10. From the above observations of the Court below I find that the Court below considering the pros and cons of the suit and the other relevant facts particularly the decree in a former Title Suit being No. 701 of 1979 between the opposite party Nos. 1-5 and Abdur Rashid Mollah from whom the plaintiff has been claiming the suit land passed the very considerate, thoughtful and rational order giving chance to the opposite party Nos. 1-5 to contest in the suit. Since in a former suit the title of the opposite party Nos. 1-5 was declared such parties cannot be kept away from a subsequent suit where their question of title and interest are also involved. If the opposite party Nos. 1-5 are devoiced now from the suit how they will protect their interest in respect of the suit land. 

 13. By the Rule issuing order dated 19-7-1998, the further proceeding of Title Suit No. 35 of 1997 was stayed till disposal of First Appeal No. 129 of 1997 pending before this Court, arising out of Title Suit No. 701 of 1979. From the record of First Appeal No. 129 of 1997 it appears that the appeal has been dismissed on non prosecution on 26-2-2006. So there appears no impediment to vacate the stay order of this Rule.

lawyer:
Md Khalilur Rahman with Md Khalilur Rahman (Helal)—For the Petitioner. 
Md Alamin Sarker, DAG with KM Masud Rumy, AAG—For Respondents Nos. 3 & 4.
parties:
STS Educational Group Limited ------ Petitioners
vs. 
Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Land and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
4. While the aforesaid owners Md Abdul Moyed and others were thus owning and possessing the aforesaid entire 1.10 acres of land, their mutations were cancelled behind their back vide Miscellaneous Case No. 99 of 1991 and Mutation Khatian No. 7640 was opened in the name of respondent No. 6 who then started to threaten to dispossess Md Abdul Moyed and others from the suit land and, under the circumstances, they filed Title Suit No. 156 of 1991 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Sadar Court, Sylhet for permanent injunction restraining respondent No. 6 and other government officials from disturbing the peaceful possession of the plaintiffs in the 1.10 acres of the suit property and also from evicting the plaintiffs therefrom. The suit, being transferred to the Assistant Judge, Circuit Court, Sylhet, was re-numbered as Title Suit No. 20 of 1991 and was decreed on contest on 28-11-1991and upon preferring appeal by respondent No. 6 the same was dismissed on 17-2-2004 and against the said appellate Court's judgment and decree, respondent No. 6 filed Civil Revision No. 4627 of 2004 before the High Court Division, which was also dismissed on contest on 19-4-2007 and, finally, when respondent No. 6 preferred CPLA No. 2041 of 2008 before the Appellate Division the same was dismissed on 14-5-2009 on the ground of limitation. It is stated that, in the aforesaid manner the claim of respondent No. 6 to the case land was finally rejected by the highest Court of this country and, thus, the rightful possession of the petitioners predecessors in the suit property was permanently protected. 

 6. On 28-11-2010, when the writ petitioner filed an application to the District Ansar Adjutant, Sylhet for deploying 10 Ansars in its aforesaid purchased property for protecting its legal title and lawful possession therein, the same was rejected on the plea that the property is an acquired land as shown in the impugned Gazette Notification. The writ petitioner then served a legal notice on 5-1-2011 upon respondent No. 6 and others for cancellation of the said Gazette Notification within 15 (fifteen) days from the date of receipt of the said notice but respondent No. 6 and others did not reply thereto. Being at a loss, the writ petitioner approached this Court for vindication of his legal right. 

 8. It is stated that a copy of the notice under section 5(7) of The (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948 has now been procured from the Commissioner Office, Chittagong Division, Chittagong as the original file of LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64 has been mislaid from the District Record Room by unscrupulous officials of the said office who acted as the collaborators of some land grabbers to help them in making fake, false and forged deeds. It is further stated that the Register of LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64 shows that an amount of compensation money of Rs. 32,400.50 was deposited with the treasury vide TC No. 1642 dated 18-12-1964 and the same was distributed among the awardees by the Special Land Acquisition Officer, Sylhet. Names of awardees and amount of awards are as follows:— 

 10. Thereafter, the property in question was mutated in the name of the Whole Sale Fish Market and respondent No. 6 is paying rent to the government since 1967. It is stated that the aforesaid documents ought to have been placed before the trial Court in TS No. 20 of 1991 but unscrupulous government officers did not come forward to assist the trial Court in adjudicating upon the matter effectively. It is stated that no effort was made by the concerned government officers and employees to establish the fact that without inclusion of 1.10 acres of land in the said Gazette Notification dated 4-3-1965, the total quantum of acquired land does not come to 5.59 acres of land and, thus, non-mentioning of plot No. 41 therein was a mere printing mistake. It is further stated that the said suit was for permanent injunction and the Court has not declared title of the petitioner's predecessors in the said suit and, the title of respondent No. 6 has never been affected. It is stated that since the date of detecting the printing mistake in the Gazette Notification of LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64 regarding non-inclusion of plot No. 41, there were numerous written communication between the BG press and the relevant authority and, finally, the mistake was cured by the impugned Gazette Notification. As such there is no illegality in publishing the same. Hence the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 11. Mr Md Khalilur Rahman, the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submits that the respondents cannot claim the case property as acquired property without setting-aside the judgments passed in Title Suit No. 20 of 1991 which has been affirmed by the lower appellate Court, the High Court Division and finally by the Appellate Division. He argues that the impugned Gazette Notification has been published for frustrating the judgments of the highest Court of our jurisdiction. He submits that there are concurrent findings by the trial Court and the appellate Court that the petitioners predecessors are owners in possession of the said plot No. 41 and the same was not published in the Gazette Notification of LA Case No. 7 of 1963-64 and, therefore, this Court sitting in writ jurisdiction is not empowered to question the findings of fact decided finally by the highest Court. He then places "Explanation IV" of section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure and submits that no issue as to the acquisition of plot No. 41 can be raised after the final disposal of the TS No. 20 of 1991 inasmuch as the said "Explanation" prescribes that the issue which was required to be raised as defense but was not raised by the party, would be deemed to have been raised and will be barred by constructive res-judicata. 

 12. In a bid to deal with the issue of non-production of the relevant papers of the LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64 at the trial Court, he places section 114(g) of the Evidence Act and also refers to the case of M Saeed Sehgal vs Kazi Khurshid Hasan 17 DLR (SC) 111, wherein it was held that "plaintiff not calling for the accounts which were available and within his reach, presumption is to be drawn against him". He submits that the said Plot No. 41 cannot be included in the said Gazette Notification dated 4-3-1965 published in connection with under LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64 by a mere amendment of the aforesaid original Gazette Notification inasmuch as the said LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64 was initiated and, finally, ended up under the (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1984, and the said Act being dead from the year 1982, inclusion of the said Plot No. 41 in 2010 showing the same as an acquired land under LA Case No 77 of 1963-64 under the said Act is illegal and, on the other hand, the provisions of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982 also cannot be applied in publishing the said notice as the case land was not acquired under the Ordinance of 1982. Mr Khalilur Rahman, the learned advocate for the petitioner, then, refers to the case of Osimuddin vs Bangladesh reported in 1 BLC (1996) 375 and, under paragraph 9 of the said judgment, it was held that "in the absence of notification published in the official Gazette as required under sections 4 and 6 of the Forest Act, 1927 the suit land cannot be vested in the Government through Forest Department as the departmental notification cannot affect the right of the public". Thus he submits that since the government did not include Plot No. 41 in the Gazette Notification dated 4-3-1965 finally published in connection with LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64, the right and title of the petitioner's predecessors remained unaffected and their names in SA Khatian No. 1687 remained valid. As such, while they were lawfully owning and possessing the case land upon paying rents/taxes to the government, and they validly transferred the same to the petitioner through other purchases who also got their names mutated in the government record (Annexure A series). 

 14. With regard to the plea taken by the government as to committing mistake, he refers to the case of Secretary, Ministry of Industries, Nationalised Industries Division vs Saleh Ahmed reported in 46 DLR (AD) 148, wherein at paragraph 10 it was held that "nobody is entitled to take benefit of his own wrong. To claim that since no document has been executed the claimant has no right, is nothing but taking advantage of one's own wrong" and submits that if the government has committed the alleged mistake in publishing the Gazette Notification dated 4-3-1965 concerning LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64 by excluding Plot No. 41, the petitioner or its predecessors should not be deprived of enjoyment of their land which they have been possessing for decades by mutating their names and paying government taxes thereof. He submits that since the writ petitioner has purchased the property upon carrying out necessary enquiry in the office of sub-register and office of the. Assistant Commissioner of Land, and having found the gentility of the transferors title are possession the writ petitioner is a bonafide purchaser for value and, therefore, its title to and in the case land is immune from question as provided in section 41 of, the Transfer of Property Act and section 27(b) of the Specific Relief Act which safeguards the bonafide purchaser with value. In support of his submission he refers to the case of Rabeya Khatun vs. Moniruddin reported in 8 MLR (AD) 297 = 8 BLC (AD) 121 and the case of Momtazul Karim vs Abul Hossain reported in 22 DLR (HCD) 146. 

 16. He submits that since the government has accepted the rent of the case land from the petitioner and previously from its predecessors-in-interest upon mutating their respective names in respect of the case land in its record, the respondents are estopped by the principle of promissory estoppel to claim any title and possession of the said land. Then, he places the case of Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Narayanganj vs AKM Latifid Karim reported in 1 BLC (1996) 576, wherein at paragraph No. 11 it was held that "the decision of the local Revenue Officer accepting the plaintiff and his successive predecessors-in-interest as tenants in respect of the suit land under the government is binding on the vested property and so the latter cannot claim the suit property as the vested property" and submits that in view of the fact that the petitioner and his predecessors have been paying rent to the government for nearly the last 50 years, the respondents now cannot claim the land to be an acquired land. Then, he refers to the case of Renupada Chakraborty vs Kurfan Ullah reported in 16 BLD 250 = 46 DLR 532 wherein it was held at paragraph 8 that "equitable principles are the tools for mitigating the rigors of law. In the instant case under the equitable principle of Promissory estoppel the plaintiff is debarred from recovering possession from the defendants as they made substantial improvement in the suit land at their own cost and labour acting on the assurance made by the previous owner Kunja Mohan Chakrabarty, although the defendants did not acquire any title in the suit land by adverse possession on the date of filing of the suit". Accordingly, he submits that the respondents by accepting the rents from the petitioner and its predecessors as well as by mutating their names in respect of the case land are debarred from disturbing the petitioners in the enjoyment of the same. 

 19. He submits that Title Suit No. 20 of 1991 filed by the petitioner's predecessors Md Abdus Shahid and others was for permanent injunction and not for declaration of title and though the suit was decreed and the plaintiffs were successful in maintaining the said judgment and decree up to the Appellate Division, they did not legally acquire any title to Plot No. 41 by the said verdict. He submits that it is apparent from Annexure-I to the affidavit-in-opposition filed by respondent No. 3, which is a certificate of possession of the acquired land dated 28-5-1964 (Form No. 21), that Plot No. 41 is included in LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64. He draws attention of this Court to the notice under section 5(7) Annexure I series to the affidavit-in-opposition filed by respondent No. 4, and submits that Plot No. 41 was acquired in accordance with the provisions of The (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948. He then draws this Court's attention to a rent receipt dated 4-11-2009 annexed to the said affidavit of respondent No. 4 and submits that the District Fishery Office has been paying rent to the government since the date of acquisition. Then, he places before this Court the map of the lands, dated 8-12-1964, also annexed to the said affidavit of respondent No. 4 which were to be acquired under LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64, and shows that the Plot No. 41 is surrounded by Plot Nos. 40, 42 and 44 on three sides and, as such, it is unusual that the government will acquire the plots leaving the Plot No. 41. 

 21. He continues to submit that the respondents, under the given circumstances, are now actively considering filing of review petition, though belatedly, before the Appellate Division for reviewing the judgment passed in Title Suit No. 21 of 1991 which was upheld by the appellate Court and, subsequently, by the High Court Division only on the single finding that the government has failed to produce any paper in relation to acquisition of Plot No. 41 and in view of the fact that presently the relevant papers to establish the act of acquisition of the said plot have been available to the office of the Attorney-General, there should not be any difficulty to file review petition given the fraud practiced upon the Courts and it is very highly likely that the review petition may be admitted by the Appellate Division. He finally submits that in view of the fact that the papers relating to the fact of acquisition of Plot No. 41, which ought to have been produced before the trial Court by the government have now surfaced, thus, any one with minimum prudence, in the facts and circumstances of the case, will come to the definite conclusion that due to the connivance of government officials with the plaintiffs of the said suit as well as corrupt practices or, to say the least, poor performance by the Government Pleader engaged in the trial Court for the said suit, the aforesaid papers were deliberately not produced thereby enabling the plaintiffs to obtain a favourable verdict. By not assisting the said Courts in examining the crucial issue of the said suit in its true perspective, the concerned government officers, employees and the Government pleaders practiced fraud upon the trial Court and other Courts. 

 22. He places section 44 of the Evidence Act and submits that when this sort of fact as to practicing fraud upon Court or, to say the least, adopting unfair means to defeat justice are apparent on the face of the record, this Court by exercising its Constitutional powers is competent to take judicial notice of the said facts in granting equitable relief. He submits that this Court is well equipped to arrive at its own findings, independent of the findings in Title Suit No. 20 of 1991, on the issue of title of the case land on the basis of the papers annexed to the affidavit-in-opposition as the said documents sufficiently establish the fact that plot No. 41 was acquired. He submits that correction of a printing error in any government notification in connection with a concluded acquisition proceeding does not require starting the said acquisition proceeding afresh as section 21 of the General Clauses Act provides that amendment of a Gazette Notification can be made through publication of a subsequent Gazette Notification and, thus, the respondents have rightly corrected the said error by an amendment circular. He submits that the cases referred to by the learned advocate for the petitioner have no manner of application in the instant case inasmuch as the facts of the cited cases are completely different from the fact of the present case. 

 27. Scenario No. 2 in the instant case is that non-mentioning of plot No. 41 in the Gazette Notification dated 4-3-1965 was not a mere typing mistake, rather, they said plot was never acquired vide LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64 as has been adjudicated upon by a competent Court of law in the Title Suit No. 20 of 1991, which has been upheld up to the Appellate Division. In that event, the task of this Court will be to examine as to whether the said judgment and decree dated 18-11-1991 is erroneous or not and, from our examination, if it reveals that the said judgment and decree was erroneous, then the further task of this Court will be to examine as to whether the power of this Court is unfettered or limited in questioning the decisions arrived at by the trial Court in Title Suit No. 20 of 1991 upon digging out the correctness of the findings of the said decree and judgment. 

 29. Now, the question is whether a typing mistake can be corrected by publishing another Gazette Notification. In other words, whether inclusion of plot No. 41 in the Gazette Notification dated 4-3-1965 as an acquired land can be done without starting a fresh acquisition case for the said plot No. 41. We have already found hereinbefore that in order to acquire plot No, 41 together with plot Nos. 33, 40, 42 and parts of the plot Nos. 43 and 44, the entire process has been completed long ago (in the year 1964) under the relevant laws but a typing mistake was committed in publishing the Gazette Notification on 4-3-1965 causing exclusion of the said plot No. 41. Section 21 of the General Clauses Act, 1897 provides that an authority which can pass order, it can vary, amend, alter or rescind that order. From the aforesaid provisions of law, it appears that mere typing mistake in any Gazette Notification can be corrected at any point in time by publication of another Gazette Notification and, thus, the authority in publishing the impugned amendment circular dated 28-8-2010 has resorted to section 21 and, with its aid, the said authority has given the shape of original position of the Gazette Notification dated 4-3-1965, and it does not appear to us that the impugned Gazette Notification, in fact, has altered the original position of the said Gazette Notification dated 4-3-1965. The case of the Government of Bangladesh vs Nurjahan Begum 59 DLR (AD) 80, as referred to by the learned advocate for the petitioner has no manner of application in the instant case given that the fact of the said referred case is quite different from the fact of the case in hand. In the cited case, no material document as to acquisition of the property was placed before the High Court Division to enable the Court to draw an inference to the effect that notices under section 3 and section 5(7), possession certificate and other dealings or communications were made in respect of a particular quantum of land and only at the time of publication of the final Gazette Notification a printing error occurred but in the present case, from the annexures to the affidavits-in-opposition, it clearly transpires that all the work and trans-actions were done with the aim to acquire 5.59 acres of land but in the final publication of Gazette Notification one plot, out of six plots, was not mentioned therein. Thus, subject to our findings and decision on the "Scenario No. 2", for now, we hold that there is no necessity to start a fresh acquisition processes and no illegality has been committed in publishing the impugned amendment circular. 

 30. To attach the instant writ petition with the "Scenario No. 2", the competency of this Court in making any findings on the issue of acquisition of plot No. 41, which has been finally adjudicated upon by the competent Courts, becomes pertinent. As it is a settled principle of the law that writ Court is not an appellate Court and, thus, it cannot get engaged in appreciation of the evidences and examine the correctness of the finding arrived at by the trial Court, we, notwithstanding the aforesaid position of the law, would undertake the task of going through the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court in Title Suit No. 20 of 1991 for the reasons to be stated at the last part of this judgment. 

 31. It appears that the suit was for permanent injunction, which was filed in the early part of the year 1991 and decreed on 18-11-91. It further appears that the father of Rajani Ranjan Gupta was the original owner of the suit land and it was the case of the plaintiffs of the aforesaid suit that Rajani Ranjan Gupta entered into an agreement in the middle of the year of 1982 to sell the suit land and, accordingly, the said Rajani Ranjan Gupta, upon taking the earnest money from the plaintiffs and receiving required income tax certificate, gave delivery of possession of the suit land to the plaintiffs and the registration of the suit land was agreed to be executed after receiving the remaining amount which he could not do due to his death. Then, the sole son of Rajani Ranjan Gupta, Rakkhani Ranjan Gupta executed the said registration of the suit land in favour of the plaintiffs, who, upon mutating their respective names therein, became the owners and possessors of the suit land. The cause of action of the said suit arose when the plaintiffs cultivation of the land in question was halted by the District Fishery Office in the month of Agrahayan of 1397 BS, as appears from the judgment and decree dated 18-11-1991 passed in Title Suit No. 20 of 1991, though from the averments of the instant writ petition it transpires that the suit was instituted when the said office mutated its name behind the back of the plaintiffs upon opening Khatian No. 7640. 

 32. It was the case of defendant No. 1 that the Government acquired 5.59 acres of land vide LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64, which includes the suit land of plot No. 41 consisting of 1.10 acres, and the concerned Acquiring Officer handed over possession of the entire 5.59 acres of land to the requiring body, District Fishery Officer, Sylhet and since then the said department has been possessing the said entire 5.59 acres of land without any hindrance from any quarter. The office of the Fishery Department, graveyard for the officers and employees of the said office and a number of ponds and paddy fields are situated on the said acquired 5.59 acres of land. The paddy fields lands are being possessed through Mr Abdur Noor, son of Hasan Ali of Village-Kumargaon, who vide an agreement with the office of the Fishery Department is cultivating the said land. The records relating to LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64 have been preserved in the office of the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet. Rajani Ranjan Gupta or Rakkhi Ranjan Gupta has never possessed the suit land and no agreement was made between Rajani Ranjan Gupta and the plaintiffs and, as such, no question arises as to the execution of any registered deed to sell the suit property by Rajani Ranjan Gupta to the plaintiffs and the claimed registered deeds of 5-11-90 and 641-90 are forged, false and non-effective, which do not confer title upon the plaintiffs. The defendants have possessed the suit land since 28-5-64 and the story of creating disturbance to the plaintiffs by the defendants in cutting the paddy from the suit land in the month of Agrahayan of 1391 BS is concocted. 

 35. Let us look at the performances of the learned trial Court. It appears that there is no corroborative evidence regarding the claim of entering into an agreement by Mr Rajani Ranjan Gupta with the plaintiffs as no copy of the said agreement was produced before the trial Court. In the plaint, no date of entering into an agreement or the amount of money paid by the plaintiffs to the said Rajani Ranjan Gupta was mentioned. As to the non-production of the said deed of the agreement, PW 1, who is stated to be the sole son of Rajani Ranjan Gupta, makes the following deposition “ বাদীর পক্ষের ১নং সাক্ষী ১নং বাদী নিজে জবান বন্দীতে বলেন উক্ত চুক্তি পত্র তাহার নিকট ছিল, কিন্তু তিনি তাহা খুঁজিয়া পান নাই। Thus, it appears that the very basis of the claims by the plaintiffs over the suit land is based on an agreement (which is undated and does not state the amount of earnest money), which the plaintiffs could not execute due to the alleged death of Rajani Ranjan Gupta, has not been established by any oral or documentary evidence and, therefore, the statements pleaded in the Title Suit no. 20 of 91, that following his death his claimed son Rakkhi Ranjan Gupta came forward to execute the registered deed on behalf of his late father remains questionable. More importantly, there is no evidence, oral or documentary, regarding the identity of Rakkhani Ranjan Gupta by producing any birth certificate or school certificate or his father Rajani Ranjan Gupta's death certificate or any other documentary evidence to ascertain the fact as to whether he is a genuine son of Ranjani Ranjan Gupta. 

 36. In the absence of any oral or documentary evidence as to the identity of Rakkhani Ranjan Gupta as the legal heir of Rajani Ranjan Gupta, the statements made by the respondents in the instant writ petition, being not controverted by the writ petitioner, appears to be true that Rajani Ranjan Gupta left this country during Hindu-Muslim riot and, as such, a fake person with the name of Rakkhani Ranjan Gupta as the son of Rajani Ranjan Gupta was in personated to grab the suit land. In view of the failure of the plaintiff to establish the title of Rakkhani Ranjan Gupta, the trial Court ought to have drawn an inference under section 114(g) of the Evidence Act that he does not have any title to the suit land and, accordingly, it was destined to have been held by the trial Court that the sale agreement by him with the plaintiffs is void ab initio. Also, the Courts below as well as the High Court ought to have examined the law point as to whether is there any bar to file the said Title Suit No. 20 of 91 in an acquired property as laid down in sections 10 &12 of the Government lands and Buildings (Recovery of Possession) Act, 1952 and in section 14A of the (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948 as well as in section 44 of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982. 

 "Judge's powers to put questions or order production: The Judge may, in order to discover or to obtain proper proof of relevant facts, ask any question he pleases, in any form, at any time, of any witness, or of the parties about any fact relevant or irrelevant; and may order the production of any document or thing: and neither the parties nor their agents shall be entitled to make any objection to any such question or order, nor, without the leave of the Court, to cross-examine any witness upon any answer given in reply to any such question: 

 Provided that the judgment must be based upon facts declared by this Act to be relevant, and duly proved: Provided also that this section shall not authorize any Judge to compel any witness to answer any question or to produce any document which such witness would be entitled to refuse to answer or produce under sections 121 to 131, both inclusive, if the question were asked or the document were called for by the adverse party; nor shall the Judge ask any question which it would be improper for any other person to ask under section 148 or 149; nor shall he dispense with primary evidence of any document, except in the cases hereinbefore excepted". 

 44. The crucial role was supposed to play by the concerned government functionaries, whose imperative duty was to produce case record of LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64 as well as to produce the relevant witnesses before the trial Court. Their deliberate failure manifest the fact that Title Suit No. 20 of 1991 was instituted and concluded in collusion with the concerned government employees of the District Fishery Office, Sylhet and office of the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet. Also, the Government Pleader, who was engaged in conducting the said suit on behalf of the government, was also involved in conniving with the parties of the suit inasmuch as the factum of acquisition of total 5.59 acres of land could have been established simply by aggregating the land appertaining to each plots namely, Plot Nos. 33, 40, 41, 42 and parts of Plot Nos. 43 and 44 even if it is conceded that he was really not provided with the case record of LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64 or the relevant witnesses were not presented to him by the concerned government officers and employees of the Deputy Commissioner's Office. 

 45. From the above discussions on the "Scenario No. 2" of this case, any one with ordinary prudence shall have no option but to arrive at a conclusion that fraud has been practiced upon the trial Court and lower appellate Court by the parties of the Title Suit No. 20 of 91 in connivance with the officers, employees of the office of the Deputy Commissioner, Office of the District Fishery Office and Government Pleaders (GP) and, thereafter, the same kind of performance was demonstrated by the law officers of the Attorney-General's Office in dealing with the Civil Revision in the High Court Division and in preferring Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal in the Appellate Division. Accordingly, we hold that fraud has been practiced in obtaining the judgment and decree in TS No. 20 of 91. 

 46. However, it should be noted down here that for the instant writ petition the learned Deputy Attorney-General and Assistant Attorney-General tried their best to assist this Court, as this Court noticed that they devoted themselves to unearth the fact of connivance of the aforesaid people, who were responsible and connected in dealing with the Title Suit No. 20 of 91. Further, their bonaflde is evident from the statements made in their affidavits-in-opposition to the instant proceedings as to taking preparation to file a Revision Petition against the judgment passed by the Appellate Division in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 2041 of 2008 on 14-5-2009. 

 27(b) Relief against parties and persons claiming under them by subsequent title: any other person claiming under him by a title arising subsequently to the contract, except a transferee for value who has paid his money in good faith and without notice of the original contract; 

 53. With regard to the submissions as to the application of section 114(g) of the Evidence Act, we find that since the plaintiff of the Title Suit No. 20 of 91 did not make any application to the trial Court for production of the case record of LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64, drawing an adverse inference against the defendants of the said suit was improper. 

 55. The above painstaking exercises on the "Scenario No. 2" of this writ petition take us to deal with the competency of this Court as to whether the findings of facts of practicing fraud upon the Courts in Title Suit No. 20 of 91, which derived from the threadbare discussion on the judgment and decree of the learned trial Court and appellate Court, examination of the cases of the plaintiffs and defendants, appreciation of the evidences of both the parties, observations on the performances of the learned Judges at the trial and appeal Courts as well as of the Government Pleaders, is capable of vitiating the operation of the judgment and decree passed in the said suit. 

 56. Its unanimous and obvious answer is that this Court is not competent to set-aside the findings as well as decrees and judgments of the said suit while exercising its power and jurisdiction of certiorari. Thus, unless and until the said judgment and decree is set-aside, which might still be possible by filing a Review Petition before the Appellate Division, the aforesaid painstaking exercise in unearthing the fact of practicing fraud upon Courts shall remain useless inasmuch as by virtue of the operation of the said judgment and decree, the predecessors of the petitioner successfully established themselves as the owners in possession of the case land in spite of the fact that the said suit was for permanent injunction, not for declaration of title. Consequently, as long as the said judgment and decree remains in operation, the findings in the said suit, that plot No. 41 was never acquired in LA case no, 77 of 1963-64, remains alive. It follows that Without setting-aside the said judgment and decree in Title Suit No. 20 of 91, plot No. 41 cannot be included in the LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64 by a mere amendment circular albeit we have held that the judgment and decree in TS No. 20 of 91 has been obtained by practicing fraud upon the trial Court but without any consequence to the present writ petition. 

 57. Thus, though in dealing with the "Scenario No. 1" of the instant writ petition, it was apparent that mere printing mistake was occurred in publication of the Gazette Notification dated 4-3-1965, however, in the light of the findings of this Court on the "Scenario No. 2" of the instant writ petition that the existence of the judgment and decree of Title Suit No. 20 of 91 debars the government from including plot No. 41 in the LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64, we are constrained to hold that the publication of the impugned amendment circular was illegal and without lawful authority while the operation of the said judgment and decree remains effective. 

 58. From the above discussions and observations, this Court is led to hold that in spite of detecting the fact of practicing fraud upon the Courts in obtaining the judgment and decree in Title Suit No. 20 of 91, the same being not set-aside by a competent Court and, thus, being in operation as of now, the hands of this Court are tight and not well equipped to discharge the instant Rule. Consequently, the impugned "Amendment Circular" being নং জে প্র সি/এল, এ/ ৪৪৭(৩)dated 28-8-2010 published in the Bangladesh Gazette dated 7-10-2010 (Annexure-E) appears to be without any arms to protect it for now and, accordingly, the same is declared to have been published without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 63. The Registrar of this Court is directed to send a copy of this judgment to Mr Shaha-e-Alam Chowdhury, who was serving as a Senior Assistant Judge in the District of Sylhet and conducted the trial of the Title Suit No. 20 of 1991 and delivered its judgment and decree on 18-11-1991 and also to Mr Manjur Qader, who was serving as an Additional District Judge of the District Sylhet and delivered the judgment and decree on 17-2-2004 in the Title Appeal No. 06 of 1992 having affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial Court, upon tracing their present respective job stations, in order to enable them to be appraised of the questions raised in this judgment as to their performance. The Registrar is further directed to convey the concerns expressed by this Court in the instant judgment about the standard of performance demonstrated by the said two judicial officers to the General Administrative (GA) Committee for its record. 

 64. However, we do not fancy to pass any order of direction to the Office of the learned Attorney-General asking it to take the necessary steps in the CPLA No. 2041 of 2008. We leave it upon the good conscience of the said office to consider as to whether it should immediately take necessary steps in line with its own statement made in its affidavit in opposition in view of our finding as to the involvement of corruption by the Government Headers in con-ducting both the trial and appeal in Title Suit No. 20 of 1991 and Title Appeal No. 06 of 1992 respectively. 

 Mirza Hussain Haider J: Having gone through the judgment delivered by my brother I agree with the decision of making the Rule absolute only. But I have my own reasoning’s to arrive at such decision. Facts and submissions being thoroughly discussed by my brother in his judgment, I do not need to elaborately discuss the same except which are necessary along with some of the submissions of the learned Assistant Attorney-General which are not fully contemplated in the affidavit in opposition and relying upon which, my brother has taken much pain in coming to a conclusion that fraud has been practiced upon the Court in obtaining the Judgment and decree in Title Suit No. 20 of 1991 and accordingly directed the Anti-Corruption Commission to investigate the matter and also directed the Registrar, Supreme Court, to take the matter to the notice of the General Administration (GA) Committee of the Supreme Court, upon holding that the said judgment and decree "being not set-aside by a competent court and thus being in operation as of now the hand of the Court are tight and not well equipped to discharge the instant Rule", I, with much anxiety cannot humbly agree with these parts of judgment. 

 66. So far my reasoning’s are concerned, my looking at the matter is from the angle that the Rule in this writ petition has been issued upon the respondents "to show cause as to why the amendment circular being JaPro C/LA/ 447(3) 'dated 7-10-2010 (Annexure-E) issued under the signature of Respondent No. 7, Land Acquisition Officer, Syhlet by inclusion of the petitioner's land as described in the schedule to the writ petition as Acquisitioned land of LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64 shall not be declared to have been published without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect, "From the aforesaid terms of the Rule it appears that the whole question encircles as to whether the publication of the impugned amendment circular (Annexure-E) was in accordance with law. To answer the query and to come to a conclusion of this point in issue we need to see firstly; as to who issued the impugned amendment circular, Annexure E and whether he had/has the authority to issue such circular under section 5(7) of the (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948; and secondly: if the same is for the purpose of amending/correcting the original circular dated 4-3-1965 then whether the same has been issued or published by the appropriate authority and whether the same can be done after 45 years of final publication of the same in the Gazette under section 5(7) of the said Act 1948, when the said law has been repealed by section 1(3) and (4) read with sections 16 and 17 of the said Act itself. 

 67. The background of the case is, admittedly, Rajani Ranjan Gupta was the CS recorded tenant of CS Plot No. 41 covering an area of 1.10 acres of land whose name was rightly recorded and published in SA Khatian No. 1687 in 1962; after his death his son Rakkhini Ranjan Gupta became the owner of the said property. On the other hand, it is alleged by the respondents that in LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64, the entire 1.10 acres of land in Plot No. 41, along with the entire land of CS Plots Nos. 33, 40 and 42 and parts of Plots Nos. 43 and 44 total 5.59 acres of land were acquired by the authority which was published finally in the Dhaka Gazette on 4-3-1965. It is also admitted that Abdus Sahid and others claimed to be the owners of the entire 1.10 acres of land in Plot No. 41 by purchase from Rakkhani Ranjan Gupta, son of Rajani Ranjan Gupta by five deeds of sale all in 1990 whereupon, they got their names mutated in place of Rajani Ranjan Gupta and enjoying the same by paying rents to the government in their respective names. In 1991 when the District fishery officer, Sylhet, threatened them to dispossess from the said land on the plea that the property is an acquired property, they filed Title Suit No. 20 of 1991, for permanent injunction, against the District Fisheries Officer, Subid Bazar, Syhlet and Bangladesh represented by the Deputy Commissioner Sylhet. It is also admitted that the said two defendants contested the suit by filing written statement contending intralia that entire 1.10 acres of land of Plot No. 41 along with full Plots Nos. 33, 40 and 42 and parts of Plots No. 43 and 44, total 5.59 acres of land, are acquired property and the District Fisheries Office is in possession of the same by way of possession handing over certificate dated 28-5-1964, Ext 'Ka' (Annexure A-I to the affidavit in opposition filed by Respondent No. 3). It is further admitted that the said suit was finally decreed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sylhet, by his judgment and decree dated 28-11-1991 holding that on the face of nonproduction of the records of LA case No. 77 of 1963-64; and on the face of plaintiffs' registered title documents, Mutation Khatian and the proof of possession through payment of land revenue taxes to the government by rent receipts; and on the face of all the evidences, both oral and documentary, of the plaintiffs proving their possession; and on the face of Abdun Noor, the alleged bargadar of the District Fisheries Office, being not produced and examined to prove possession of District Fisheries Office; and in the absence of any pleading as to non-mentioning Plot No. 41 in the finally published gazette dated 4-3-1965 was erroneous or due to mistake the said Plot No. 41 was not mentioned in the said gazettee dated 4-3-1965 as to final acquisition; and also on the face of advocate commissioner's report which concurrently proved plaintiffs' possession in the said Plot No. 41, even after being cross examined by the defendants, the learned Assistant Judge held that 'the plaintiffs have been able to prove their prima facie title in the 1.10 acres of land of Plot No. 41 and also having successfully proved their exclusive possession in the suit land both by oral and documentary evidences and also through the Advocate Commissioners' report and accordingly decreed the suit and the defendants were permanently restrained by an order of injunction from dispossessing the plaintiffs from the said land in Plot No. 41. It is also admitted that the said decree was affirmed in Title Appeal No. 6 of 1992, preferred by the aforesaid two defendants who then unsuccessfully moved the High Court Division and also the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court in Civil Revision No. 4627 of 2004 and CPLA No. 2041 of 2008 respectively. Thus the findings and decision of the learned Assistant Judge in Title Suit No. 20 of 1991 is a valid judgment which is still in operation. After the appeal in the Appellate Division was dismissed on 4-5-2009 the present respondents published the impugned amendment circular on 7-10-2010. Hence this Rule. 

 (3) Notice shall also be served to the above effect on the owner of such property and on all such persons known or believed to be interested therein or to be entitled to act for persons so interested as reside or have agents authorized to receive service on their behalf within the revenue district in which the property is situated. 

 73. Since the subject matter of the Rule is 'whether the impugned amendment circular inserting Plot No. 41 in the Gazette Notification of 1965 in connection with LA Case No. 77 of 1963-64 is proper and since I have come to a conclusion that the said publication of Gazette Notification of 1965 was the finality of the requisition/acquisition proceeding, the correction of the said gazette of 1965 by the impugned amendment circular (Annexure E) published by the land Acquisition Officer, Sylhet after more than 45 years without having any authority of such publication, the impugned circular (Annexure E) thus is without lawful authority as stated hereinabove and since the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 20 of 1991 is not the subject matter of this Rule rather the same has been produced as an Annexure to prove that how the respondents miserably failed to prove any title and possession on the said piece of land, I have got no other option but to constrain myself to remain within the discussion as to the legality of the publication of the impugned Gazette Notification not anything beyond that. Under the present context we cannot extend ourselves to scan the judgment passed in Title Suit No. 20 of 1991 or in the appeal/revision arose out of the same. Moreover, till the said decree is in force and not set-aside by a competent court, the impugned amendment circular, published after leasing the case up to the Appellate Division, shall have no bearing other than Creating chaos and confusion in the mind of the Public. Our jurisdiction being limited within Article 102 of the Constitution we are not empowered to sit as an appellate court to see the validity of the said judgment and the same being not the subject matter of this Rule any observation/finding on the same is nothing but at best be an academic discussion which the Appellate Division directed all to refrain from as has been held in the case of Abdul Mannan Khan vs Bangladesh reported in 64 DLR (AD) 169 that 'while deciding a case, a Court shall not embark upon unnecessary academic discussions and shall confine itself within the issues, which will crop up from the pleadings of the respective parties.' Here in the present case decree of Title Suit No. 20 of 1991 being not the subject matter in issue we are not empowered to see the validity of the same not we can make any observation as to genuinenity of the same and accordingly direct anybody to investigate into the matter.
