parties:
Nazrul Islam (Md) and another ----- Petitioners
VS
Samsun Nahan Azim and others ----- Opposite-Parties
full_judgment:
At the instance of the plaintiffs Leave was granted under section 115(4) of the Code of Civil Procedure against the judgment and order dated 1-4-2010 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Second Court, Dhaka discharging the Rule in Civil Revision No. 226 of 2009 and affirming the judgment and order dated 22-6-2009 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 77 of 2007 under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure allowing the Miscellaneous Case by which the ex-parte judgment and decree dated 10-1-2005 passed in Title Suit No. 375 of 1984 was set aside and the above suit was restored to its original file and number. 

 2. The facts relevant for disposal of Rule are that the petitioners as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 375 of 1984 for Specific Performance of Contract impleading the defendant-opposite-parties and obtained an ex-parte decree on 11-3-1987. Subsequently, the defendant No. 2 Government filed Miscellaneous Case No. 46 of 1987 under order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the ex-parte decree, which was rejected on 15-4-1990. Against the dismissal order, the defendant No. 2 Government filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 158 of 1990 which was allowed by order dated 3-4-1993 and set aside the ex-parte decree dated 11-3-1987. Thereafter Mrs Shamsun Nahar Azim opposite-party No. 1 filed an application on 15-8-1993 under Order I, rule 10(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure for addition of party and by order dated 18-6-1995 she was added/ impleaded as defendant No. 3 in the suit. In the meantime the petitioners preferred Civil Revision No. 1739 of 1993 before the Hon'ble High Court Division and same was dismissed. Then the petitioners filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1001 of 1997 in the Appellate Division, Supreme Court of Bangladesh which was also dismissed on 24-6-2001. Thereafter, the record of the Title Suit No. 375 of 1984 was received back to the trial court on 2-7-2003 but the learned Advocate of the Added defendant No. 3.was not found in court to intimate the date of hearing of the suit. So, the court passed order to serve the notice upon the defendants through process server. Although the notice were duly served upon the defendant as per report of the process server but the defendant-opposite-party did not appear to contest the suit, ultimately the suit was again decreed ex-parte on 10-1-2005. 

 3. The defendant No. 3 opposite-party No. 1 herein appears to have filed an application under Order IX, rule 13 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure on 22-8-2007 for setting aside the ex-parte decree and the same was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 77 of 2007 stating, inter alia, that the present-petitioners as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 375 of 1984 on 24-11-1984 in the First Court of Sub-ordinate Judge, Dhaka for specific performance of contract. The suit property was enlisted as Abandoned property within the meaning of PO 16 of 1972; the applicant, Shamsun Nahar is the wife of Late Captain Anwarul Azim, who sacrificed his life for the sake of independence of Bangladesh in the Liberation war in 1971. In order to pay tribute and homage to her husband's sacrifice, the government allotted the suit abandoned property to petitioner's family by allotment Letter dated 17-12-1974 and delivered possession. Till then petitioner has been in possession of the suit property by paying electricity, gas, water charge and monthly rent to the government. That the learned trial court passed an order on 9-5-2004 for issuing summons upon the defendant No. 3-opposite-party No. 1 after the case record of the suit was received back by the trial court on 2-7-2003 and the defendant No. 3 had no scope to know the progress of the suit. That the summons of the suit was not served upon her on 25-10-2004 and she did not receipt any notice from the court. The process server in collusion with the plaintiffs submitted his report that the summons were duly served upon the defendant No. 3. In the service return the defendant No. 3 or her representative put any signature. Defendant No. 3 as opposite-party No. 1 recently came to know about the ex-parte decree. Then she went to the court and inquired about the matter through her learned Advocate and being confirmed applied for certified copy of the judgment and obtained certified copy on 4-7-2007. Since the defendant had no knowledge about the ex-parte decree, there has been a delay of 944 days in filing this Miscellaneous Case, which may kindly be condoned. At the time of filling of the application, the defendant No. 3 also filed an application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1908. 

 4. The Plaintiffs-opposite-parties contested the said Miscellaneous case by filling written objection, denying the allegations of non-service of summons/notice upon the defendant No. 3 and stating further that the notice of the suit were duly served upon the defendants; that the Miscellaneous case is barred by limitation; that the suit was decreed ex-parte on 10-1-2005. The opposite-party No. 1 was added as defendant No. 3 in Title Suit No. 375 of 1984 on 18-6-1995 and aware of the proceeding of the suit and present Miscellaneous case was filed after eighteen months of the ex-parte decree which is not sustainable in law and filed just to harass the opposite-parties. 

 6. The learned Joint District Judge allowed the Miscellaneous case by judgment and order dated 12-6-2009 and restored the suit to its original file and number on the findings that the summons of Title Suit No. 375 of 1984 was not served upon the defendant No. 3 and the defendant No. 3 as petitioner filed the present Miscellaneous Case within 30 days after obtaining the certified copy of the impugned judgment and decree. There was a fraud upon the defendant-petitioner in respect of service of summons by the court through process server. The process server did not serve the summons in presence of Mokabila witnesses. Consequently, the defendant had no knowledge about the proceedings of Title Suit No. 375 of 1984. 

 12. Mr Kamal-ul-Alam, the learned Advo-cate submits that both the courts below concurrently found that summons/notice upon the defendant No. 3 was not served properly in accordance with law. He further submits that the trial court held that the impugned ex-parte decree passed in Title Suite No. 375 of 1984 was obtained without service of summons upon the defendant No. 3 for that reason she was prevented from appearing in the suit. Thus the learned Joint District Judge rightly condoned the delay and set aside the ex-parte decree. In this connection learned Advocate refers decisions reported in 35 DLR (AD) 162 and 12 BLC (AD) 75. 

 13. The learned Advocate submits that the opposite-party No. 1 filed application for being added as defendant No. 3 in the Title Suit on 15-8-1993 but this order was not signed by the presiding Judge and Civil Revision No. 1739 of 1993 was filed by the plaintiffs-petitioners before the Hon'ble High Court Division, without impleading defendant No. 3, as the plaint was not amended impleading defendant No. 3 and the same was dismissed and Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1001 of 1997 was also dismissed. Then the case record of Title Suit No. 375 of 1984 was received back by the trial court on 2-7-2003 and plaintiff by order dated 18-6-1995 was directed to amend the plaint adding Shamsun Nahar as defendant No. 3, but the plaint was not amended accordingly. 

 14. He also submits that thereafter the learned trial court passed gkrt order on 9-5-2004 to intimate the order dated 18-6-1995 to the learned Advocate for defendant No. 3. Since no intimation was given as he could not be found, learned trial court by order dated 15-9-2004 issued notice through court upon defendant No. 3 and summons was shown to have been served by order dated 15-10-2004 and subsequently suit was decreed ex-parte for second time on 10-1-2005. Mr Kamal-ul-Alam, by referring those orders and service return of the process server submits that the address of the defendant No. 3 mentioned in the plaint and the address of the notice are not same, further PW 1, Shamsun Nahar deposed that no notice was served on her on 15-10-2004 and OPW 2, process server admitted that the Mokabila witnesses were declined to put their signature in the summons, inspite that he wrote the names of two persons as Mokabila witness which clearly proved that the defendant No. 3 was not aware about the ex-parte decree. He further submits that when notice was 'not served upon the defendant No. 3 properly, the ex-parte decree is liable to be set aside. He submits that there was no earthly reason for the opposite-party not to contest the Title Suit No. 375 of 1984 if she had received the summons, particularly in view, of the fact that on her prayer she was added as Defendant No. 3 in the suit on 18-6-1995. 

 19. It appears that earlier Title Suit No. 375 of 1984 was decreed ex-parte on 11-3-1987. Against the ex-parte judgment and decree, defendant No. 1, Government filed Miscellaneous Case No. 46 of 1987 under Order IX, rule 13 and the same was dismissed by the judgment and order dated 15-8-1990. Against the dismissal order, defendant No. 1 filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 158 of 1990 before the District Judge, Dhaka and same was allowed by the judgment and order dated 3-4-1993 and the suit was restored to its original file and number. Thereafter on the prayer of the present opposite-party No. 1 Shamsun Nahar Azim on 15-8-1993 under Order 1, rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the court by Order No.74 dated 18-6-1995 added her as defendant No. 3 in the suit but the plaintiffs did not take any step to amend the suit register, even the order dated 18-6-1995 was not signed by the concerned judge till 9-5-2004 as evident from Order No. 91 dated 21-4-2004 and Order No. 92 dated 9-5-2004. 

 28. This background of the suit has to be kept in mind while considering the question of service of notice in this suit and decreed the suit in ex-parte as well as filing of the Miscellaneous Case No. 77 of 2007 after long delay of 944 days. In this connection learned Advocate for the opposite-party No. 1 has also drawn our attention to the order sheets of the Title Suit No. 375 of 1984 which is already quoted above. 

 30. Opposite party No. 1 clearly stated m her application under Order IX, rule 13 Code of Civil Procedure that no notice was served upon her in Title Suit No. 375 of 1984 and the process server in collusion with the plaintiffs submitted report that the summons were duly served upon the defendant No. 3. 

 38. The service report, (Exhibit-Kha) are devoid of these essential information. The courts below after considering the order sheet, oral and documentary evidence on record and relevant provision of law clearly of the opinion that the summons was not duly served upon the Defendant No. 3 in the Title Suit No. 375 of 1984. 

 40. Mr AF Hassan Ariff learned Senior Advocate for the petitioner mainly submits that the application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure was not filed within 30 days from the date of obtaining certified copy and the same was filed after 18 days which was beyond 30 days as provided under Article 164 of the Limitation Act in as much valuable right has been accrued by the plaintiffs. He also submits about the locus standi of the present opposite-party No. 1 since the paramount title holder is not claiming the suit property.

parties:
Azizur Rahman Khan and another ----- Petitioner
Vs.
State and another -----Opposite-Parties
full_judgment:
3. Relevant facts necessary for disposal ofthe rule are that the complaint petition was filed against the Opposite-party No.2 alleging that his grant mother namely Julaykha Bibi was owner of the schedule property measuring 78 decimals. On 21-3-1981 the said owner transferred the same by registered Heba-bil-ewaz deed in favour of Amina Khatun mother of the complainant who became the owner of 26 and 1/4 decimal ofland on the basis of the said deed of gift and got her name mutated. When she was in possession, the accused-persons threatened to disposes her from the land on the disclosure that they have acquired title to the property on the basis of purchase from one Shamser Ali by a sale deed bearing No. 2523 dated 4-4-2007. It was alleged that this was fraudulent type of deed created for the purpose of grabbing the property illegally. As such, the complainant filed the petition complaint under sections 467/468/471/420/109 of the Penal Code on 22-5-2008. After cognizance the accused-persons appeared before the Court on every dates which were fixed for hearing charge, but the complainant remain absent for several consecutive dates without any application for adjournment. As such, the learned Magistrate was pleased to pass an order of acquittal under section 247 of the Code of Criminal Procedure on 9-9-2009. Subsequently the complainant filed an application before the Magistrate Court on 12-10-2009 seeking restoration of the disposed of criminal case on the plea that he was not aware of the earlier dates fixed for hearing of charge. On the basis of said application, the learned Magistrate set-aside his own order dated 9-9-2009, registered the disposed of criminal case and issued summon upon the accused- petitioners afresh. 

 5. Mr. Fazlur Rahman Khan, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the accused-petitioners, submits that the learned Magistrate had no legal authority to set-aside his own order of acquittal under section 247 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and restored the previously disposed of criminal case and restart proceeding afresh. It is submitted that once an order of acquittal is recorded by the Magistrate under section 247 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, it cannot be interfered with by the same Court and that the order was an appealable/revisable order before the Higher Court. So without setting-aside the order by the High Court, there was no scope reinitiated a disposed of criminal proceeding by the concerned Magistrate Referring to the case of Dewan Obaidur Rahman vs State reported in 1999 BLD (AD) 128 = 4 BLC (AD) 167 and also another case reported in AIR 1953 Calcutta 197, the learned Advocate submits that the acquittal under section 247 is an acquittal in the real sense of the term which creates bar to whole further trial under section 403. It is further submitted that the original complaint case relates to a civil dispute over title of the property having no involvement to invoke under any penal provisions as such, reinitiating of the said criminal proceeding would amount to sheer abuse of the process of the Court and, as such, the same is liable to be quashed. 

 8. On perusal of the original petition of complaint, it appears that there is no allegation of committing forgery in respect of any documents executed by the complainant or his predecessor in interest. The allegation clearly indicates that it is a civil dispute between the parties over the claim of title and interest thereto.

parties:
Abul Kalam alias Kaliullah and others ------ Plaintiffs-Appellants
Vs.
Madhab Bigraho and others ------ Defendants-Respondents
full_judgment:
Sharif Uddin Chaklader J: This appeal by the plaintiffs directed against judgment and decree dated 1-2-2012 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur dismissing Title Suit No. 23 of 2008. 

 3. The case of plaintiffs is that, suit land originally belongs to Bhawal Raj. The suit land of schedule 'Ka' comprising of an area of 23.13 acres of land recorded in CS khatian No. 7 along with other lands in the name of Kumar Rabindra Narayan Chowdhury settled the suit land in raiyati right. On the death of Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury, his heirs as of tenanted right was owner in possession of the entire land of Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury. As per Court of Wards Act 1879, the management and administration of the property including "Ka" schedule land of CS khatian No.  7 was taken over by the Court of Wards. During the last CS record, it was recorded in the name of Court of Wards, for Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury and others, which was subsequently named as Bhawal Raj Courts of Wards Estate or Bhawal Court of Wards Estate or Court of Wards Bhawal Raj Estate. Bhawal Court of Wards Estate as owner and possessor of `Ka' schedule land with other lands of CS khatian No.  7, settled 'Ka' schedule land with the father and husband of the plaintiff. Bashoruddin and co-sharer, Chand Mia through its own printed pattannama. Basiruddin and Chand Mia became owner and possessor in equal share. While Basiruddin and Chand Mia on the basis of pattannama and dakhila and by paying zamindari taxes to Bhawal Court of Wards Estate, the Government, then province of East Pakistan by giving effect of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act acquired the rent receiving interest of the Zaminder and on taking nominal taxes as land development tax, the tenants were classified as owner of their respective land as per sections 3 and 42 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. After acquisition of the rent receiving interest as aforesaid, Government published final gazette as per provision of section 3 of the aforesaid Act on 24-3-1952. After acquisition of the land as aforesaid, Compensation Assessment Roll were prepared and Zaminder as per the aforesaid compensation assessment roll received compensation and gazette was published on 29-5-1956 as per section 42 of the aforesaid Act by which the Zamindari of Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury of `Ka' schedule land, was acquired and the status of tenant. Basiruddin and Chand Mia were changed and become owners. Accordingly SA khatian was finally published in their names. By opening jote in the revenue office and by paying nominal land development tax possessing the suit land SA khatian No.  63 was finally published in the name of Basiruddin and Chand Mia in equal 8 annas share. Basiruddin and Chand Mia upon an amicable settlement partitioned the kha schedule land by which 'Ka' schedule land fallen in the saham of Basiruddin. After acquisition of the land by the Government, 5.40 acres of land remain in the hand of Basiruddin alone which has been mentioned in 'Kha' schedule. Chand Mia got 'Ga' schedule land which comprising of 0.39 acres of land of dag No. 155/1061, 0.51 acres of land of dag No. 1059, 1.42 acres of land of dag No. 1063, 1.18 acres of land of dag No. 1058, 0.60 acres of land of dag No. 1060, in total, 4.10 acres of land and remaining land, in total 13.36 acres including 12.5 as mentioned in 'Gha' schedule was in ejmlali and co-sharers as owners owned and possessed by cultivation. While the aforesaid land was in possession of co-sharers, 1.48 acres of land was acquired by the Government out of 13.63 acres of land for road and remaining land i.e. 12.15 acres of land, "Gha' schedule, was in ejmali of the co-sharers. While co-sharers as aforesaid was in possession having title there to, Government acquired portion of land for defendant No. 16, the Ministry of Agriculture, defendant No. 17, Rice Research Institution from the land of Chand Mia to the very knowledge of defendant No.  1 and 14 in LA Case No.  100/65-66, recognizing Chand Mia as the owner of the aforesaid land. Compensation was received by Chand Mia while in possession, 12.15 acres of land described in schedule `Gha', constructed homestead, planted trees and cultivated agricultural lands in ejmali, died leaving, defendant No.  6 as heir who along with other co-sharers possessing the land in ejmali. While defendant No. 6, plaintiff and Chand Mia was in possession of the ejmali property of 'Gha' schedule comprising 12.15 acres, Government in LA case No.  5/85-86 acquired 10 acres of land for defendant No.  19, Gazipur District Police Line under defendant No.  18, Ministry of Home Affairs. In LA Case No.  3/2001-2002 Government acquired 0.33 acres of land for defendant No.  26, District Fisheries Officer under defendant No.  25, Ministry of Fisheries and Veterinaries under Government of Bangladesh, in LA Case No.  7/90-91 acquired 0.09 acres of land for defendant No. 20, District Jail, Gazipur under defendant No.  18, Ministry of Home Affairs, in LA Case No.  3/95-96 acquired 0.33 acres of land for Defendant No.  District primary Education office under defendant No. 21 Ministry of Education, Government of Bangladesh, in LA Case No.  5/90-91 acquired .50 acres of land for defendant No.  24, Public Health Engineering Department under defendant No.  23, Ministry of Health, Government of Bangladesh. Government disbursed compensation money part of the afore-said 5 LA cases to the plaintiffs and to the co-sharers having found they are legal title holder. Some greedy person of the locality created obstruction in getting compensation money and gave proposal to defendant No. 6, son of defendant No. 9 and brother of defendant Nos.  1 and 8, but recognized their title over 'Kha' schedule land when they would manage in getting the compensation money to the plaintiffs. Later on, Chand Mia died leaving defendant Nos.  2-5 as heirs. Plaintiffs, the heirs of Chand Mia, defendant Nos. 2-5 are waiting for getting compensation money. Suddenly, on 12-12-2007 the manager of defendant No. 14 and the officer of Bhawal Court of Wards came to 'Kha' schedule land whereupon plaintiff could know that defendant No. 1 of the instant suit along with defendant No. 1 of Title Suit No.  1219 of 1985 filed in the court of Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur against defendant Nos. 3-6, in total against 11 persons as defendants and they got decree. Defendant No. 1 of the instant suit got decree up to the Appellate Division of the Hon'ble Supreme Court. In RS record 18.70 acres of land of 'Kha' schedule recorded in the name of defendant No. 1 and they requested plaintiffs to give up possession of the suit land. Defendant No.  1 of the instant suit threatened plaintiff that if they did not give up possession to the defendant No.  14 amicably then they by force evicted the plaintiffs from the suit land. Plaintiffs went to defendant No.  14 to know about the decree, then, the manager of defendant No.  14, Abdur Rouf, gave a paper book to plaintiff No.  1 and requested plaintiff No.  1 to go through paper book to find out how the suit was decreed. Plaintiffs after getting paper book asked defendant Nos.  6 and 3 as to how they got decree in the suit to which they kept silence. Defendant No. 1 with connivance with defendant Nos.  6-13 got the decree surreptitiously. 

 4. It is further case of plaintiffs that defendant No. 1 was never owner and possessor of the suit land from defendant No.  14 in any manner either as tenant or as Raiyat. The lands upon which defendant No. 1, Sree Sree Madhab Bigraho claimed title Extinguished from the moment State Acquisition of Tenancy Act published in gazette on 24-3-1952 and vested in the Government, as such, defendant No. 1 looses his right to collect rent from the plaintiffs or any-body. 

 7. It is further case of plaintiff that as per provision of President Order No.  90 of 1972 when the property have been recorded as 'projabili' no suit can be institute as such decree of Title Suit No. 1219 of 1985 and affirmed up to Appellate Division as per law has no legal support and on the basis of aforesaid decree defendant No. 1 or 14 or anybody cannot evict the plaintiffs from the suit property. 

 8. It is further case of plaintiff, that plaintiff appellant is in possession from the time of pattannama and by this time, their possession is more than 60 years, as such, they got title by adverse possession as per law. 

 10. The case of defendant Nos.  1 and 14 is that, suit land was recorded in CS khatian Nos.  7 and 770 ultimately in RS khatian No.  506 and 1011 and quantum of land was 23.13. Original owner of the suit property was Kumar Rabindra Narayant Roy Chowdhury and others and later, Bhawal Court of Wards. While Chowdhuries were in possession, they installed family deity as Sree Sree Madhab Bigraho and puja expenses were paid from their own income. The aforesaid Bhawal Raj for maintaining the deity for worship, handed over their entire property to Bhawal Court of Wards under Court of Wards Act, 1879 and from 1911 Court of Wards maintained the case property on behalf of Bhawal Raj Estate. CS record recorded the name of Court of Wards on behalf of Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury and other co-sharers. Bhawal Raj maintained the Estate by giving barga and adi Barga, maintained possession, Vz portion of the crops was given to the manager and remaining 1A portion to the cultivator. Manager as shebayet, by the income worshiping the family deity. The name of Sree Sree Madhab Bigraho is correctly recorded in RS khatian. Suits were filed for and against Sree Sree Madhab Bigraho and decree was passed in favour of Sree Sree Madhab Bigraho. The case of plaintiffs is false. 

 11. The case of defendant No.  6 is that this defendant has no claim over 'Kha' schedule land. While his predecessor, Chand Mia was alive out of an amicable partition 'Ka' schedule land was fallen in the share of Chand Mia and since then this defendant possessing 'Ka' schedule land. This defendant never appeared in any of the suit including Title Suit No. 1219 of 1985 as the name of father of this defendant has been written as Rashid Uddin and Ashraf Ali of that suit, is a different person, not this defendant and by that decree title of this defendant cannot extinguish. 

 12. The case of defendant Nos.  16 to 32 is that Gha schedule of the suit land has been acquired by the Government in LA Case No. 100/65-66, LA Case Nos.  5/85-86, 5/90-91, 3/ 95-96, 3/2001-2002 and 7/90-91 giving compensation money to the plaintiffs and his co-sharers. In SA khatian No. 63,23.13 decimals of land recorded in the name of Basiruddin in 8 annas share. In RS khatian No.  506,18/3 acres of land has been recorded in the name of Sree Sree Madhab Bigraho in 8 annas share. The Government has no claim excepting the land which has been acquired by the Government where Government has title. 

 13. It is further case of Government that in Title Suit No. 1219 of 1985 filed by defendant No. 1 as plaintiff in the Court of Joint District Judge 1st Court, Gazipur claiming title but defendant No. 1 of the instant suit has no title and has no possession and defendant No. 1 of the instant suit impleaded defendant No. 2-13 of the instant suit as defendant and got decree and on the basis of aforesaid decree defendant No. 1 illegally threatened the plaintiff of the instant suit from dispossession from the suit land. 

 17. Mr Md Khalilur Rahman, learned Advocate, appearing for the plaintiff appellants, submits that, pattannama exhibit-2 was disbelieved by the learned Judge on the ground that dates mentioned therein in Bengali has no similarity with the corresponding English date without properly going through the contents thereof as the date in Bengali mentioned in the middle side of the pattannama is the preliminary date of pattan subject to the approval of the Chief Manager and the date in English after signature of the concerned Nayeb of Court of Wards, Bhawal Raj Estate is the date after approval of the pattan by the Chief Manager of the said Court of Wards. Learned Advocate further submits that judgment passed in previous Title Suit No. 1219 of 1985 and also of those of the higher Courts up to the Appellate Division wherein decision arrived are not supported by law as the lands of SA Khaian No.  63 of the suit land was settled as pr6jabili and as per President Order No. 90 of 1972 no suit can be filed against the lands settled as projabili as such said judgment having passed on wrong assumption of law affirmed up to Appellate Division is a judgment per in curium. Learned Advocate submits that rent receipts were granted by the Zaminder and thereafter, by the Revenue Authority of the Government after whole sale acquisition of the land and on the face of such legal position, preparation of RS khatian in the name of defendant No. 1 is without any basis, the court below without considering the materials on record abruptly hold pattanana as forged which finding is erroneous in as much as the names of Basiruddin and Chand Mia was duly recorded in the subsequent documents like Register II, the Talab Baki Register, exhibit-5, Compensation Assessment Roll, exhibit-8, rent receiver's Title Description Register, exhibit-4 and lastly in SA khatian, record of right after effecting the 'projapattani'. Learned Advocate further submits that document filed connecting with projapattani being more than 30 years old and has been produced from proper custody of the plaintiff-appellants got presumptive value of its execution and further submits that learned Judge committed gross illegality in holding that SA khatian produced form, the side of plaintiffs is a created document upon using a revenue stamp and bears no signature of Officer-in-Charge of record room is baseless and against the record and also against order No.  68 dated 30-11-2009 passed by the learned Judge on the application filed by the plaintiffs for calling the record from the Revenue Department whereupon the court ordered that since Government produced SA khatian as such record from Revenue Department is not required to be called to settle the dispute without considering that Government produced distorted SA khatian. Learned Advocate further submits that the findings of the learned Judge that in Title Suit No. 12 of 1976 it is decided Chand Mia is a bargadar under defendant No. 1, Sree Sree Madhab Bigraho is baseless and fully on surmise and conjecture as the contesting defendant-respondent No. 1 and 14 who claimed their title through those judgments, had neither filed nor exhibited those judgment in the present suit as such finding of the learned Judge that Chand Mia had admitted in those previous suits that he was a bargadar is baseless and full of surmise and conjecture not supported by any law. Learned Advocate further submits that court below was in erroneous findings of fact as it should have considered the vital documents like the rent receiving interest acquisition gazettes, exhibit Nos. 7 and 9, written statements of defendant Nos.  6 to 32, true copy of the SA khatian produced by the Government, exhibit No.  `Kha; the register No. II i.e. Talab Baki Register, exhibit No. 5, Compensation Assessment Roll exhibit No. 8 and the rent receiver's Title Description Register, exhibit No. 4, which are although in certified copies are not challenged by the Government while marked as exhibits and non-consideration of those vital documents led the Court below to erroneous finding as to the title of the plaintiffs-appellants. Learned Advocate further submits that possession of the plaintiffs-appellants from the time of pattan upto the date of forceful eviction on 3-3-2008 and 5-3-2008 has been proved by the oral and documentary evidences of the plaintiffs-appellants and also by the defendant's witnesses, DW 1 and DW 2, learned Judge committed gross illegality in not declaring title of the plaintiffs over the suit property by adverse possession. Learned Advocate further submits that possession of the plaintiffs have been proved through municipal tax receipts, electric and gas bills, house rent receipts etc. exhibit 13 series and also Advocate Commissioner's report and such non-consideration of those vital documents as to possession of the plaintiffs led the Court to an erroneous finding as to title of the plaintiffs, as possession follows title. Learned Advocate further submits that defendant No.  1, Sree Sree Madhab Bigraho having not been represented by the Shebayet in the previous Title Suit No. 1219 of 2985 as plaintiff and in the subsequent present Title Suit No.  23 of 2008 as defendant No.  1 and the defendant No.  14 the Court of Wards, Bhawal Raj Estate having no connection with the deity, has no locus standi to file the previous Title Suit No.  1219 of 1985 and also to contest the subsequent Title Suit No.  23 of 2008 as its representative, so, the decree passed in previous Title Suit No. 1219 of 1985 and the dismissal decree passed in Title Suit No.  23 of 2008 is illegal and without jurisdiction. Learned Advocate further submits that neither defendant No. 1 nor defendant No.  14 filed any document of acquiring title in the suit property nor proved their possession therein, but the learned trial court dismissed the suit on coming to the conclusion on surmise that the defendant No. 1 is a owner of the suit property. Learned Advocate further submits that defendant No. 1 and defendant No. 14 having admitted that all the properties except ‘Kha' schedule property have been acquired by the Government and also compensation have been paid to the plaintiffs and Chand Mia, decree passed in previous Title Suit No. 1219 of 1985 for recovery of khas possession of the entire 18.73 acres of land including the acquired land, is illegal and not binding upon the persons in possession through acquisition. 

 19. Mr Sashanka Shekhar Sarkar, the learned Deputy Attorney-General, appearing for both defendant Nos.  1, 14, and 16 to 32, submits that, suit property having debuttar property, as per law, nobody could challenge or claim title of the property as such the learned Judge committed no illegality in dismissing the suit. Learned Deputy Attorney-General referred to sections 404, 413, 414, 415 and 415 (A) of the Hindu Law and submits that the property if recorded as deity cannot be alienated except for legal necessity, not for any other purpose, but the pattan in favour of the plaintiffs having not disclosed any legal necessity, the basic document of title of the plaintiffs having gone, as such, learned Judge committed no illegality in dismissing the suit. 

 (i) Whether after wholesale acquisition of the property as per provision of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, defendant No. 1 can be said to be the superior land lord or land lord of the property when the property stand as 'projabili' and whether the ex-land-lord, defendant No. 1 can be said to have title over such property. 

 (ii) Whether plaintiffs acquired title (a) by adverse possession or (b) on modification of law of the land or (c) or in both. 

 (iii) Whether the judgment passed in Title Suit No.  1219 of 1985 affirmed up to Appellate Division can be taken to be a good judgment on the subject matter of this suit to bind these plaintiffs. 

 30. It means that the leassee will be entitled to enjoy the usufruct of the land through his sons and grandsons and successors in interest by digging tanks, constructing buildings and raising structures and by exercising rights of gift, sale etc., and by cultivating the land in khas or by establishing tenants. We are informed that the expression "Nijakarkite" 1 which occurs in this kabuliat means khas cultivation, that is, cultivation, by one's own labour. The expression "Projabili" (establishing tenants) has been judicially interpreted by reference to section 160 (g) in some of the decisions of this Court. In the case of Akhil Chandra Mandal vs Ssurendra Nath Dutt, 11 Cal LI 87 (A), the head lease authorized the lessee to raise embankments, bridges, damkhals, cut jungles and "establish tenants according to your desire, construct houses .... And do other acts". Acting under this authority, the leassee created an 'istemrari maurasi mokarari makadami' tenure which is a kind of subordinate tenure and not a raiyati holding. Mr Justice Sarada Charan Mitra who was affirmed on Letters Patent Appeal held: 

 "The words 'established tenants' do not necessarily indicate that the lessor gave the lessee express authority to create tenancies of the kind set up by the plaintiffs in this case. They are words commonly used in leases to indicate that the tenure created entitled the tenure holder either to cultivate the land himself or cause cultivation by means of tenants." 

 42. Plaintiffs case is that they got pattern of the land from Zaminder of Bhawal and since then they are in possession, at first, under the Zaminder and later on, under the Government until dispossess in 2008. The case of defendant Nos.  1 and 2 is that property having belongs to a deity, this property could not be alienated by anyone except legal necessity; RS khatian prepared rightly, plaintiffs title has been extinguished and defendant No. 1 having got decree in Title Suit No.  1219 of 1985 this suit was dismissed rightly. The case of defendant No.  6 is that he was not a party to Title Suit No.  1219 of 1985 as he did not appeared in the suit and his father's name was not rightly recorded. It is the case of defendant No.  6 that defendant No. 1 had no title nor possession and on the basis of decree of Title Suit No.  1219 of 1985 defendant Nos.  1 and 14 illegally threatened plaintiffs from dispossession from the suit land. Defendant Nos.  6-17 wants saham for 4.10 acres of land which has been acquired for Bangladesh Rice Research Institute. The case of defendant Nos.  16 to 32 is that the suit land has been acquired from plaintiffs by different LA Cases and suit land has been rightly recorded in the name of plaintiffs and SA, khatian No. 63 in 8 annas equal share to Basiruddin, predecessor of the plaintiffs and Chand Mia, predecessor of the defendant Nos.  2 and 6. 

 43. It appears that Government in written statement admitted plaintiffs are the owner of the suit property as in the written statement Government stated that in different LA Cases Government acquired land from plaintiffs and from their co-sharer and SA Khatian No.  63 was rightly prepared in the name of predecessor of the plaintiffs and also of his co-sharer, Chand Mia and it is also the case of the Government that plaintiff of Title Suit No 1219 of 1985 and defendant No.  1 of the instant suit has no title or possession. As such, title of the plaintiffs has well established. On this background let us refer to the depositions of the witnesses particularly of defendant's witnesses who stated as:— 

 45. Together with this fact, if we consider the written statement of the Government it gives title to the plaintiff on admission as per order VIII, Rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 46. Plaintiffs case of title if we look into, relates back to the pattan, exhibit-2 dated 25-5-1938. Trial court disbelieved these documents as Bengali date do not corresponds with English date. Mr Sashanka Shekhar Sarkar, Deputy Attorney-General, submits that, it is forged one as Chand Mia, one of the pattandas did not produced it in Title Suit No. 1219 of 1985 and this pattannama has no legal force. 

 47. We have scrutinized this document. In the pattannama there is a statement to the effect that “ ম্যানেজার সাহেব মঞ্জুর না করিলে বন্দোবস্ত আমলে আসিবে না। ইতি ১৩৪৫ সনের ২৯ শে বৈশাখ।” this pattan requires to be approved by the manager. Pattannama was approved on 25-5-1938. So this deed speaks of proposal and approval as such, there is two different dates as proposal and approval cannot be given on the same date. The learned Judge totally misread this exhibit-2, basic documents of title of plaintiffs as it has a legal force. For non-production of this exhibit in the earlier suit the title of plaintiff cannot extinguish. It may be said that the earlier suit was not properly conducted. In the earlier suit President Order No.  90 of 1972 was not also considered as the suit was filed by Sree Sree Madhab Bigraho. 

 48. This pattannama has been acted upon as from exhibit-3 series it appears that the pat-tan holder paid Zaminderi tax up to 1942 then from exhibit No. 4, dakhila, it appears land has been recorded as 'projabili' extinguishing title of Superior landlord, Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury. From exhibit No.  2-4 it appears from the column of the khatian that name of plaintiffs and co-sharer have been recorded for 23.13 acres of land as projabili. Exhibt-5 is Talib Baki Register-II kept in the custody of Government where also we find the name of the predecessor of the plaintiffs from whom tax was collected. Exhibit-6 series are rent receipts stand in the name of plaintiffs and their predecessor. Up to this plaintiffs have been able to prove that they have paid rent to the Zaminder pursuant to the pattan taken from Zaminder i.e. up to 1952. 

 58. So after acquisition finally took place on the background of the gazette notification, exhibits 7 and 9, and as per decision of the Appellate. Division as mentioned herein above it can be said with authority that it concluded plaintiff’s title to the suit land and no court passes any decree affecting the title of the plaintiff. 

 62. In the case reported in 60 DLR (AD) 24 where it is held that "The plaintiff-respondent who embraced Islam is found to have been in peaceful and uninterrupted possession adversely to the interest of all others for more than 12 years and thereby acquired good and indefeasible title to the suit property described in schedule B of the plaint which was formerly their family debattar property. The family deity was removed there from and consequently the suit property ceased to be debattar property." 

 65. The SA khatian exhibit-la' submitted from the government custody and the SA khatian submitted from the plaintiffs custody, exhibit -1 are of the same and the same was recorded in the joint names of Chan Miah and Basor Uddin citing them as owners of the 'Ka' schedule suit property in equal II, anas owner each. From the judgment of Title Suit No.  1219 of 1985, it is found that the present defendant No.  1 Deity had submitted SA Khatian No.  63 before the court claiming to have recorded in its name as owner. But here in this case, he with-held the said SA khatian and had submitted an information slip exhibit 'kha(1)1 stating that the SA khatian remained in the record room of DC office was turned of for the reason best known to him without explaing whatsoever about the previous exhibited SA khatian No.  63 in Title Suit No.  1219 of 1985. In such circumstances, it can easily be concluded that since the attested true copy of the SA khatian No.  63, exhibit-'Ka" submitted from the government custody and since the government had admitted in their written statements that the SA khatian No.  63 was prepared and published in the joint names of than Miah and Basor Uddin in equal share and since the said SA khatian exhibit `Ka' and the SA khatian of the plaintiffs, exhibit-1 are of the same and since the SA khatian prepared in the name of Chan Miah and Basor Uddin has got the basis i.e. exhibits-4 to 9, the plea of defendant Nos.  1 and 14 that the SA khatian was prepared in the name of defendant No.  1 is forged and fraudulent is not correct finding, rather we can come to the conclusion that the SA khatian, exhibit-1 was duly and correctly prepared and published in the name of Chan Miah and Basor Uddin, the predecessor of the plaintiffs. Moreover, the finding of the previous suit regarding SA khatian prepared in the name of Chan Mian and plaintiffs' predecessor Basor Uddin is not binding upon the plaintiffs as the present plainiffs were not party in the previous Title Suit No.  1219 of 1985. 

 67. Exhibits 7 and 9 published under section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act with reference to particular estates, taluks, tenures, holding and tenancies and in respect of all rent receivers whose properties were under the management of Court of Wards Act, 1876. Sub-section 2(a) was enacted and introduced in section 3 of the Act by ordinance No.  111 of 1956. After this amendment, by general notification dated 2nd April, 1956 issued district wise in regard to all rent receiving interest which thereafter vested in the Government with effect from 14-4-56 in terms of those notification. As such, after 14-4-56 the defendant No.  1 has no right, title, interest or possession in itself what-ever it has, gone under the Government, not of it in any individual form to initiate any proceeding. A title less person has no legal character to initiate any proceeding. 

 68. Since the record show the land as projabili, as such the title of the land vested in the plaintiffs. In the earlier suit Sree Sree Madhab Bigraho was plaintiff and the judgment passed therein was without reference to President Order 90 of 1972 as such the judgment was passed without consulting the law, as such, has no binding effect and the judgment stand as per in curium. 

 71. From the aforesaid statements made in cross-examination it is found that the DW-1 at one time claims that the 'Ka' schedule property is owned by the Court of Wards and at another time claims that the suit property is owned by the Deity, the defendant No.  1. At one stage, the DW-1 admitted that it had no basis for recording the name of Deity in the RS khatian. The two woman Shebayets as cited in the RS khatian had left the then East Pakistan now Bangladesh before Division of Pakistan and India. So the RS record prepared and published in the name of defendant Nod, Bigraha represented by two women as shebayets in equal II. Eight anas share as possessors is admittedly baseless and without foundation and, as such, the plaintiffs-appellants are entitled to have the relief against the said RS record as prayed for in his plaint as wrong, illegal, without any basis and not binding upon the plaintiffs appellants. 

 72. We have also seen the RS record prepared in the name of Surjabala Debi and Bhivabatibala Debi when they are not in Bangladesh as they left for calacutta in 1917. It is prepared as it appears to destroy the title of the plaintiffs after proprunlgation of PO 90 of 1972 abolishing the Zamindari system vesting the lands in Government as such, this record having no basis, has no legal effect. 

 73. Now, we refer to the written statement of the parties. At first we look to the written statement made by the Government. Mr Sashanka Shekhar Sarkar, the learned Deputy Attorney-General, as we see appeared for defendant Nos.  1, 14 and 16 to 32. We are surprised to find that case of defendant No. 1 and 14 is totally contradictory to the case Government as defendant No. 16 to 32 as Government in the written statement support title and possession of plaintiffs and totally denied title of defendant No. 1 and 14 and also possession of defendant Nos.  1 and 14. 

 74. Mr Sashanka Shekhar Sarkar, the learned Deputy Attorney-General, referred to sections 404, 413, 414, 415 and 415A of Hindu Law and submit Government as defendant No.  16 to 32 as Government in the written statement support title and possession of plaintiffs and totally denied title of defendant No.  1 and 14 and also possession of defendant Nos.  1 and 14. 

 75. Mr Sashanka Shekhar Sarkar, the learned Deputy Attorney-General, referred to sections 404, 413, 414, 415 and 415 A of Hindu Law and submit that when there is an endowment without legal necessity same cannot be transfer or cannot be alienated. It appears from the fact of the case that possession of the plain-tiffs has not been denied and combined force by force dispossessed the plaintiffs from the suit property in 2008 whereupon one of the Hon'ble Judge of this Court, Mr. Justice MA Wahhab Miah, as his Lordship was then, issued rule which we will discuss after conclusion of the judgment of the appeal. Sections so referred cannot applicable on the facts of the instant suit as defendant No.  1 did not produce the document selling Bigraho. From exhibit 3 it is seen that pattan has been given and subsequently it was converted to 'Aclhi Barga'. Leter on, Court of Wards entered into management of the property, as such, when the Court of Wards entered into the suit property to manage the entire property of Bhawal Raj including Deity or Bigraho then property changed its character to secular property which we have already seen. Defendant No.  1 did not produce or adduce any witness to prove deity is in existence now. It appears from the written statement as well as deposition of Government witnesses that Sree Sree Madhan Bigraho has no possession or title as such the laws as referred by the learned Deputy Attorney-General has no application in this suit. 

 81. Learned Advocate next relied on 33 DLR (AD) 52, where it is held that "The learned Advocate appearing for the leave petitioner, when confronted with the aforesaid gazette notifications dated 24-3-1952 and 29-2-1956, as to acquisition of rent receiving interest and the vesting of lands of the leave petitioners, including the case lands, found it difficult to substantiate the locus-standi of the leave petitioner in challenging the draft records of right prepared in the names of the respective writ petitioners in respect of their respective case lands prepared during the Mohanagar Survey. Further with the publication of the gazette notifications dated 24-3-1952 and 29-2-1956 the petitioner ceased to have any right, title and interest and possession in the case lands, because acquisition and vesting of said lands in the Government. 

 82. Thus we are of the view that the leave petitioner had no locus-standi to challenge the draft Mahanagar Survey Khatian as prepared in the name of the respective writ petitioners, at-least after publication of the gazette notifications dated 24-3-1952 and 29-2-1956." learned Advocate next relied on the case of 14 MLR (AD) 401 where it is held that "The plaintiffs were never recognized as co-sharers and on the contrary the heirs of Jinnat Ali are in exclusive possession of the suit land since the time of the CS record and they have acquired good title by continuous adverse possession for over 12 years. The right title interest of the plaintiff and their predecessor to the suit land has been extinguished by ouster and hostile adverse possession." Learned Advocate on adverse possession relied on 13 MLR (AD) 329 where it is held that "The plaintiff-respondent who embraced Islam is found to have been in peaceful and uninterrupted possession adversely to the interest of all others for more than 12 years and thereby acquired good and indefeasible title to the suit property described in schedule B of the paint which was formerly their family debattar property. The family Deity was removed there from and consequently the suit property ceased to be debattar property. The High Court Division set-aside the judgment and decree of the appellate court and restored the judgment and decree of the trial court on the above findings which the apex court held perfectly justified. 

 83. Learned Advocate next relied on the case 13 MLR (AD) 353 where it is held that "A receipt witnessing a transfer of an immoveable property is not a deed of title and, as such, it cannot confer title to the transferee. But nevertheless the transferee can acquire title in the land by uninterrupted adverse and hostile possession for over 12 years. 

 84. Learned Advocate next relied on the case 24 BLD (AD) 43 on record of right without basis, it is held that "Mere entry in the record of right shall not create right and title over any property without any corroborative evidence and materials. This proposition of law gets sup-port from the view taken by the Appellate Division in the case reported in 28 DLR (AD) 61. 

 85. Learned Advocate next relied on the cases of 61 DLR 635 and 32 DLR 252, on time limit for declaratory suit. Against record of right, learned Advocate relied on the case of 8 BLD 497 where it is held that " The law is now settled that against the wrong record of rights the person whose interest is affected by such wrong recording need not file suit questioning legality of the record of rights so prepared and finally published within 6 years from said date or from the date of knowledge of such wrong record of rights, but he is required to file the suit seeking declaration of title within six years from the date the person in whose name record has been wrongly prepared and finally published raises claim denying his claim on the basis of wrong record." On wrong record of right learned Advocate next relied on 9 MLR (AD) 82 where it is held that "Knowledge of wrong record of the right can be starting point of limitation and a litigant public even if aware of wrong record of a cord of right can wait and wait till his right is invaded by other side and his suit will be well within time if he institutes suit within six years from date when his right on suit property is denied and invaded." 

 86. Since the plaintiffs proved their title, both by legal document as well as by adverse possession, we find merit in the appeal. 

 88. The judgment and decree dated 1-2-2012 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur dismissing Title Suit No.  23 of 2008 is set-aside. Title Suit No. 23 of 2008 is decreed as:— 

 90. Now, whether the plaintiffs-appellant can get back the possession of the suit property taken over by the defendants on 3-3-2008 by force during the pendency of the Title Suit No.  23 of 2008 as per prayer of the petition dated 16-3-2008. The plaintiffs-appellants filed an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for restoration of the dispossessed 'Kha(2)' schedule suit property before the High Court Division. At the time of disposing the said petition dated 16-3-2008, the High Court Division passed an order as follows:— 

 "We are of the view that the allegations being serious in nature in that the respondent opposite parties dispossessed the petitioners from the 'Kha (2)' scheduled land violating the order of injunction passed by this Court it should be investigated into by the Trial Court during the trial by framing an issue to the above effect and if the allegations are found to be correct then possession must be restored back to the plaintiffs if their title to the land is found. We are of the further view that nobody should be allowed to violate the order of a court of law be it the sub-ordinate court or this court and one should not also be given the benefit of a situation on creates after the institution of a suit. Accordingly, we send the application filed by the plaintiff-petitioners under section 151 of the Code of the court below to dispose of the same along with the suit in the light of the observations and direction given hereinbefore. The rule stands disposed of accordingly." 

 91. The both the plaintiffs-appellants and defendant Nos.  1 and 14 had accepted the said judgment of the High Court Division as neither of them had preferred any steps to the Appellate Division against that judgment and order dated 10-7-2008 of the High Court Division. Apart from the aforesaid judgment it has already been established by different judicial pronouncements that if any party of the pending suit is dispossessed by other party of the said suit, then the dispossessed party can get back possession of the suit property by an order of temporary mandatory injunction under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The said principle of getting back possession by temporary mandatory injunction has been confirmed by our Appellate Division in the case reported in 35 DLR (AD) 42, 47 DLR (AD) 6. Since from the admitted evidences on record it has been proved that the plaintiffs-appellant has been dispossessed from their homestead property as described in the 'Kha (2)' scheduled property on 3-3-2008 during the pendency of Title Suit No. 23 of 2008 by force with the help of DC and SP Gazipur at the instance of defendant Nos.  1 and 14 and since the plaintiffs have proved their title in the 'Kha' schedule suit properties by producing both oral and documentary evidences, as such, they are legally entitled to return the possession of 'Kha (2)' schedule dispossessed property by an order of temporary mandatory injunction as prayed for in their petition under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure dated 16-3-2008 within specified time as may be fixed by this court. 

 92. From the aforesaid facts, evidences both oral and documentary and also law involved in the case we conclude that the entire 23.13 acre `Ka' schedule property was a probability property before SAT Act. 1950. So, the said 23.13 acre 'Ka' schedule property was duly recorded in the names of the then projas namely Chan Mian and Basaruddin in SA Khatian No.  63 (Exhibit-1) by operation of section 3 of the SAT Act, through publishing probability property Gazette (Exhibit-7) and also by PO 90 of 1972 the RS Khatian No.  506(Exhibit-12) recorded in the name of  শ্রী মাধব বিগ্রহ সেবাইত দং সুরুজ বালা দেবী। বিভাবতি দেবী। জং কুমার রবিন্দ্র নারায়ন রায় চৌধুরী সাং নিজ।” is baseless and without foundation, as such, the same is not binding upon the plaintiffs. The defendant No.  14, Court of Wards, Bhowal Raj Estate claiming as shebaiyet of defendant No.  1 and the defendant No.  15, Land Reform board had illegally evicted the plaintiffs appellants on 3-3-2008 and 5-3-2008 from the `Kha' schedule property violating the order of injunction passed by the High Court Division on 3-3-2008 in Civil Rule No.  132(FM) of 2008 and also during the pendency of Title Suit No.  23 of 2008 of the joint District Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur and as such, the plaintiffs are entitled to recover the said dispossessed 'Kha(2)' schedule property as prayed for in their petition dated 10-7-2008. The plaintiffs appellants having proved their right, title and possession in the rest of the 'Kha' schedule property i.e, `Kha(1); 'Kha(3); 'Kha(4); 'Kha(5)' and Kha 6 schedule property are entitled to protect their said property by the decree of confirmation of possession and permanent injunction. 

 98. So, the First Appeal No.  128 of 2012 is hereby allowed with contest against defendant respondents Nos.  1, 14 and 16-32 without cost. The judgment and decree binding upon plaintiffs. The decree passed in Title Suit No.  1219 of 1985 of the Court of 1st Joint District Judge, Gazipur which affirmed by the High Court Division in FA No.  104 of 1997 and by the Appellate Division in CPLA No.  94 of 2006 is hereby declared collusive and illegal and not binding upon the plaintiffs-appellants. The defendant Nos.  1, 14 and 15 are directed to hand over possession of the 'Kha(2)' schedule dispossessed property within 60 days from today to the plaintiffs-appellants, failing which they will get compensation @ Taka 1,00,000 per day till the plaintiffs get possession thereof through the process of the Court. The possession of the plaintiffs-appellants in the rest of the 'Kha' schedule properties, i.e. 'Kha(l)', 'Kha(3)', 'Kha(4),"Kha(5)' and Kha (6) schedule proper-ties hereby confirmed against the defendants respondents Nos.  1, 14 and 15. The defendants-respondents Nos.  1, 14 and 15 are also restrained by a decree of permanent injunction from disturbing the possession of the plaintiffs in and evicting the plaintiffs-appellants from the `Kha (1)', 'Kha (3)', 'Kha (4); 'Kha (5)' and Kha (6) schedule properties.
justice_names: Mr. Justice Sheikh Md. Zakir Hossain
